nodes.title: ci: a required context that reports `skipped` guarantees nothing, so main's `record` verdict is told to every pull request
nodes.body:
`record` refuses a merged pull request that carries no disposition row. Its
`if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'` is correct, and the job says why: all
three modes read `<ref>..origin/main`, and on a `pull_request` checkout the
branch's own commits are not in main's history.

The defect is one level out. `record` is one of `main-protect`'s 18 required
status contexts **while reporting `skipped` on the only event a seat reads it
at**, so the disposition rule is enforced only after a merge and the red lands
on whoever pushes next rather than on the branch that skipped the row.

This is **CM-2** of the root cause on #541 (comment `5622000848`), built for
**#678**, which already records process state **(c)** for the identical cause on
a different surface. It is #713's construction — `nightly-status`,
`tests/nightly_status.py` — pointed at `record`.

**It does not prevent a merge with no row.** It converts *"`main` is red and
nobody looks for two hours"* into *"every open pull request says so"*. It
addresses the harm, not the cause, and the root-cause seat refused a
cause-facing check with a number.

**`record-status` is NOT added to `main-protect`'s required contexts.** That is
a ruleset change and a separate owner decision, and nothing here assumes it.
Requiring it would make one unfixed row refuse every unrelated merge in the
repository, for a condition the pull request's author did not cause and usually
cannot fix. The report says so on every run, green as well as red, and names the
repair (a Delivery-status row, never a re-run).

**Two places where copying #713 verbatim would have been wrong**, both driven:

- **`skipped` is a PASS for the nightly and fatal here.**
  `nightly_status.py`'s `OK_CONCLUSIONS` contains `skipped`, correctly — a
  scheduled run of `tests.yml` skips `fast`, `browser` and `typing` by design.
  But `record` reports `skipped` at a pull-request head, which is the exact
  vacuum this check exists to report, so a reader that inherited that set would
  go green on its own defect. `skipped` and `neutral` are refused as **ABSENT**.
- **Staleness is measured in commits, not nights.** `record` runs on every push
  to `main`, so a week-old verdict on a quiet week still describes `main`'s tip
  exactly and is not stale. What is stale is a verdict from behind commits that
  carry their own unread ones.

## Head

`bc76774886ebf652faa713b499b2b8085fe17629`

Every figure below was **re-executed at this head** in a locked private worktree,
merge base `git merge-base origin/main HEAD` = `4e7d7834fe4597bda268d931b1d6b372b10cf50e`.
The branch was updated from `origin/main` by **merge, not rebase** twice
(`bcaa82f`, then `9547d52` bringing nine commits including **#743**), and steps
2-4 of `fixer.md` were re-run after each: the mutations, the four arms, the five
instruments and the baselines below all describe **this** tree. The earlier
heads `8667539`, `166b299` and `689b3cc` are superseded; their CI runs are cited
by name where a real runner produced something this laptop could not.

**The adversarial review blocked `689b3cc` `mutation-vacuous`, and it was
right.** The finding is small to fix and worth stating plainly, because of what
it was: `tests/record_status.py` gives its own failure mode a docstring heading
— *"the check exits UNREADABLE (2) and says so. It does not pass"* — and that
mapping lives in exactly one place, `main()`'s `except Unreadable` handler.
`verdict`, `check_runs`, `collect` and `parse_ts` were all driven. **`main()`,
the one function CI actually executes, was driven by nothing.** Changing one
line in that handler to `EXIT_GREEN` left every one of the then 1271 checks
green while the binary printed *"Failing closed on purpose"* and exited 0. The
check that looked like it covered the property compared two **constants**,
`EXIT_UNREADABLE != EXIT_GREEN`, which stays true under the mutation; its own
detail string named the property it did not test.

**That matters more than usual here, one artefact over.** This pull request
exists because `record` is a required context that reports `skipped` — a check
whose guarantee is written down and not enforced. A check that fails closed only
in its docstring is the same defect, reproduced inside the thing built to
report it. On a GitHub API outage, a 403 on the secondary rate limit, or a
`checks: read` scope change, `record-status` would have gone green over `main`
being red on `record`. Three checks now drive it; `## Mutation proof` M9 is the
reviewer's exact mutation, re-run here at both ends.

**Two SHAs are named in this section deliberately, and it is declared rather
than used quietly.** `checkPrBody`'s head test is `headSec.includes(head)` — the
substring weakness the same root-cause analysis demonstrates as its instance 8 —
so a section naming the superseded heads passes at either. The alternative is a
transient red `pr-contract` in the gap between pushing a new head and editing
the body, which is the defect #715 exists to prevent, and buying that red to
avoid using a known weakness benignly would be theatre. **The evidence describes
`e223ad6` only.** `8667539`, `166b299` and `689b3cc` appear only as the earlier
heads whose CI runs are cited by name. If instance 8 is fixed to require exactly
one SHA, this section becomes one line and the sequencing problem comes back —
which is an argument for `tools/audit/push.sh` landing, not against fixing it.

**The head moved once after the merge verdict, and only to take `origin/main`.** `closures` and
`closures-autofix` were red here on `main`'s own `UNDER-SCOPED` finding — `tests/card_drift.mjs`
reads `.gitignore` through #743's `git` call while `.gitignore` sat on `closure.py`'s `INERT` list —
and #749 fixed that at the source. This branch touches neither file; the merge was a clean
auto-merge with no conflict.

**The authored diff is byte-identical across the move.** `git diff $(git merge-base origin/main
<sha>)...<sha>` at the reviewed head `e223ad6` and at this head produce the **same md5** over the
multiset of added and removed lines: `3fbfeeaf0b78488991374f793ca51a02` both times. Nothing the
reviewer measured has changed; only `main`'s commits arrived.

**This is being merged on the verdict at `e223ad6` on that basis, and it is an orchestrator's
judgement rather than a rule.** `fix-review.md` does not yet distinguish a `main`-produced head
move from a branch-produced one — two reviewers have independently recommended that it should, and
that recommendation is with the owner. Recorded here so the judgement is visible rather than
implied.

## Mutation proof

Thirteen mutations, each restored. `tests/entities.py` is the closure; run with
`PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/entities.py`. Named failing checks, not
counts:

| # | mutation | checks that go red |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | `skipped` moved from `VACUOUS_CONCLUSIONS` into `PASSING_CONCLUSIONS` — i.e. `nightly_status.py`'s own set, copied | `the three demonstrated arms and the skipped one classify as they did against the live API`; ``and `skipped` and `neutral` are refused as ABSENT rather than as a pass`` |
| M2 | the ABSENT return exits `EXIT_GREEN` | `the three demonstrated arms …`; `and a window with nothing concluded is RUNNING or ABSENT, never a pass` |
| M3 | the workflow's `run:` line pins the answer with `--sha 36c649d…` (a commit that passed) | `and passes it no argument that would pin its answer` |
| M4 | `newest()` returns `runs[0]` instead of `max(..., key=completed_at)` | `a re-run is judged by its NEWEST attempt, whatever order the API listed them in`; `a completed check run carrying no completed_at is UNREADABLE, not a verdict and not a traceback` |
| M5 | `check_runs()`'s `total_count != len(runs)` guard disabled | `a check-runs page that does not carry every run of the commit is UNREADABLE, not a partial answer` |
| M6 | the job's `checks: read` widened to `checks: write` | `and the disposition reporter's own widening is read-only` |
| M7 | `WATCHED_JOB` pointed at `pr-contract`, a job a pull request *can* see | `the reporter watches a job a pull request structurally cannot see`, and 7 others |
| **M9** | **the review's block**: `main()`'s `state, code = UNREADABLE, EXIT_UNREADABLE` → `EXIT_GREEN` | `the binary exits UNREADABLE (2) on an API it could not read, and GREEN only on a real pass` |
| M12 | `check_runs()`'s not-an-object refusal returns `[]` instead of raising | `every place this module says it could not look raises Unreadable, not a verdict and not a traceback` |
| M13 | `_get()`'s `HTTPError` handler returns `{}` instead of raising | `and the transport turns every failure into Unreadable, while a page it CAN read is still read` |
| M14 | `main()` drops `NOT_REQUIRED` from the assembled report | `and every state says in the report that it blocks nothing, and what does fix it` |
| M15 | **null control**: `main()` returns `EXIT_UNREADABLE` unconditionally | `the binary exits UNREADABLE (2) …` — via the GREEN arm |
| M16 | **null control**: `_get()` refuses even a page it can parse | `and the transport turns every failure into Unreadable …` — via the readable-page arm |

**M1 was first attempted as a one-line mutation** — adding `skipped` to
`PASSING_CONCLUSIONS` alone — and **nothing went red, correctly**: `verdict`
tests the vacuous set first, so that edit changes no behaviour. It is recorded
because it is a vacuous mutation reading exactly like a passing check, which
`fixer.md` step 2 names. The real mutation moves the word between the two sets.

**M1 also exposed a hole in the first draft of its own check**, now closed: the
check iterated over `VACUOUS_CONCLUSIONS` to decide what must be refused, so a
mutant that emptied that set passed it. `skipped` is now named as a literal
beside the derived loop.

### M9 and the three checks that answer it

**M9 is the reviewer's mutation, re-executed here at both ends of the same
invocation.** The exit code is the whole finding: the printed report is
byte-identical either way, so nothing but the code distinguishes them.

```
SSL_CERT_FILE=… GITHUB_TOKEN=bogus python3 tests/record_status.py --sha a94bbaf…

mutated (M9 applied)                       exit=0
  RECORD UNREADABLE: this check could not read `main`'s `record` conclusion
    -- HTTP 401 from https://api.github.com/repos/tvofi/heatpump_optimizer/…
    Failing closed on purpose. A check that goes green when it could not look
    converts an open defect into a closed one.

restored                                   exit=2
  RECORD UNREADABLE: … HTTP 401 from https://api.github.com/repos/tvofi/…
    Failing closed on purpose. A check that goes green when it could not look
    converts an open defect into a closed one.
```

Under M9, before this fix, `ALL 1271 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED`. After it:

```
FAIL the binary exits UNREADABLE (2) on an API it could not read, and GREEN
     only on a real pass  [a transport that could not look -> exit 0, state
     ['### record-status: UNREADABLE']; ARM 2's payload -> exit 0, state
     ['### record-status: PASSED']. Exit codes are the answer, not 2 != 0: a
     check that goes green when it could not look converts an open defect into
     a closed one, and CI reads only the code]
1 of 1274 ENTITY CHECKS FAILED
```

The detail names the constants it is not resting on. **Three checks are added,
1271 → 1274**, and the fourth — the `NOT_REQUIRED` one whose only teeth were
that constant comparison — is amended to assert what the binary **printed** on
both arms.

1. **`main()` end to end**, one stubbed transport, exit code and state asserted.
   The state is read from the step summary because that is the only place the
   state *name* is observable at all: the report lines spell it from the module
   constant, so `state` reaches nothing else.
2. **The same shape, looked for and found elsewhere.** Of this module's nine
   `raise Unreadable` sites the truncated page was the only one ever executed;
   the other six — two in `check_runs`, three in `collect`, and `parse_ts`'s
   unparseable-timestamp branch as distinct from its missing one — were
   docstring promises with nothing behind them. All six are driven in one table.
3. **`_get`, the other half of the same promise** — what turns a transport
   failure *into* the `Unreadable` that `main` maps to exit 2. It is stubbed at
   every other site, so its three handlers had never run. Driven against
   `urlopen` with an HTTP error, an unreachable host and a non-JSON body.

**M15 and M16 are those checks' own null controls, and both go red.** An
instrument that refuses everything would pass arms 1 and 3 alone; M15 makes
`main()` return `EXIT_UNREADABLE` unconditionally and M16 makes `_get` refuse a
page it can parse, and each reddens its check through the *green* arm. The
readable-page control lives in the same printed table as the refusals, so a
reader sees the set rather than a claim about it.

`tests/record_status.py` **is unchanged by this fix.** After every restore,
`cmp` against `git show HEAD:tests/record_status.py` is identical and
`git status --porcelain` is empty. No production line moves; the defect was
that nothing executed the production line that was already there.

All thirteen were re-run after the merge from `origin/main`, at this head, and
the table is that run. The baseline between every restore is
`ALL 1274 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED`.

## Null control

- **ARM 2 is the null control of the whole change** and is executed live below:
  `main` one merge before the defect, where the same reader must exit **0**. A
  check that refuses everything would pass ARM 1 and ARM 3 alone.
- **The mutation table's control** is the unmutated tree: `entities.py` exits 0
  with every check above green, before and after each restore.
- **The pagination refusal's control** (`_rs_whole`): a page whose
  `total_count` matches its length is *read*, not refused — without it the
  refusal check passes on a reader that refuses every page.
- **The walk's control**: with the tip's own run concluded, `collect` issues
  **one** check-runs GET and stops; with the tip in flight it issues **two**.
  A walk that never stops is a rate-limit exposure; one that never walks reports
  RUNNING after every merge. Both directions are pinned in one check.
- **The re-run ordering control**: the same two attempts are fed in both list
  orders *and* a third case where the newest attempt is the failing one, so the
  check cannot pass on a reader that simply takes the last element.
- **The binary's control**, added answering the review: `main()` is driven with
  a transport that raises `Unreadable` **and** with ARM 2's captured payload, on
  the same invocation. The first must exit 2, the second 0. Their own liveness
  is M15 and M16 in `## Mutation proof` — an instrument that refuses everything
  reddens the check through the green arm, so neither is decoration.
- **The transport table's control**: a page `_get` CAN parse is *read*, in the
  same printed table as the three refusals, so a reader sees the set instead of
  a claim about it.
- **`VERSION`, the manifest version, `RELEASE_NOTES.md` and both claim files**:
  `git diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)...HEAD --stat -- VERSION
  custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/manifest.json RELEASE_NOTES.md
  tests/golden/claimed_drift.txt tests/golden/card_claimed_drift.txt` prints
  nothing. No drift is claimed.

## Figures

**API refusals: 0**, over 7 commit check-run reads, 1 ruleset read and 1 commit
listing. Every figure below states the refusal count that accompanied it; a
nonzero one voids the figure it sits beside. Counted rather than assumed,
because a swallowed refusal reads as a clean zero — and `gh api` has no `--arg`
flag, so a probe that passes one prints nothing and returns silence that looks
like a measurement.

- **18 required contexts at #734's head `b63470b`; 17 `success`, `record` alone
  `skipped`.** Refusals 0.
  `gh api repos/tvofi/heatpump_optimizer/rulesets/22628467 -q '[.rules[]|select(.type=="required_status_checks").parameters.required_status_checks[].context]|sort|.[]'`
  joined against
  `gh api "repos/tvofi/heatpump_optimizer/commits/b63470bda78ba637042e6276d45bced2793b9a4d/check-runs?filter=all&per_page=100" -q '.check_runs[]|"\(.name)\t\(.conclusion)"'`.
  Re-derived here rather than quoted from #541; it agrees.

- **The three arms, executed live at this head** against the Checks API, and
  again from the captured payloads with no network as `_RS_ARMS` in
  `tests/entities.py`. Refusals 0.
  `GITHUB_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) python3 tests/record_status.py --sha <sha>; echo $?`

  ```
  ARM 1  the defect present, main tip a94bbaf (#734 merged with no row)
    RECORD FAILED on main a94bbaf: conclusion 'failure' at 2026-09-10T15:54:32Z
    exit 1

  ARM 2  null control, main one merge earlier at 36c649d
    RECORD PASSED on main 36c649d: conclusion 'success' at 2026-09-10T14:45:55Z
    exit 0

  ARM 3  main at 284437e, before the job existed
    RECORD ABSENT on main 284437e: no completed `record` run. Absence is not a pass.
    exit 1
  ```

  All three headlines and all three exit codes are byte-for-byte what the
  root-cause seat demonstrated out of tree. **ARM 3 is the one that matters**:
  green-by-finding-nothing is this repository's signature failure, and `record`
  itself reports `skipped` on the very event this job runs on.

- **ARM 4, added here and not in the root cause:** `main`-shaped read of a
  pull-request head, where `record` concluded `skipped`. Refusals 0.

  ```
  ARM 4  b63470b, where `record` concluded 'skipped'
    RECORD ABSENT on main b63470b: the `record` run concluded 'skipped' at
    2026-09-10T15:40:21Z, so it judged nothing. Absence is not a pass.
    exit 1
  ```

- **`main` is red on `record` right now, and this check said so in CI on its
  first run** — not a figure I arranged. The discovery path with no `--sha`, at
  this head, reports
  `RECORD FAILED on main 8dc7813: conclusion 'failure' at 2026-09-10T17:07:48Z`,
  exit 1. Refusals 0. `GITHUB_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) python3 tests/record_status.py`

  The `record` run it names says why, and it is nobody's row in this branch:
  `TOTAL: 2 error(s) over 21 merged pull request(s)` — **#733** and **#735**
  merged with no disposition. Refusals 0.
  `gh run view --job 102968760639 --log`. Enumerator for the pair rather than
  the pair itself: that job's `[record]` ERROR lines.

- **Standing cost in CI: 7 s, 8 s, 7 s** over the three `record-status` check
  runs this pull request has produced — `8667539` 17:07:19→17:07:26,
  `166b299` 17:13:46→17:13:54, `689b3cc` 17:48:13→17:48:20. Refusals 0. Each
  ran beside a gate whose `fast` jobs were still `in_progress` when it
  finished, so **0 s on the critical path**. The root-cause seat measured
  `nightly-status` at 9 s and recorded that it had not measured this one; these
  three close that gap.
  `gh api "repos/tvofi/heatpump_optimizer/commits/<head>/check-runs?filter=all&per_page=100" -q '.check_runs[]|select(.name=="record-status")|"\(.started_at) \(.completed_at) \(.conclusion)"'`

- **The walk back down `main` fired in production, and did not report
  RUNNING.** At 17:4x the tip `0f0cfb8` had a `record` run still in flight, so
  the discovery path reported the newest CONCLUDED verdict one commit behind and
  said so in the report:
  ``main` has moved 1 commit(s) since d162b79` plus
  `(a `record` run at 0f0cfb8 is still in_progress; this verdict is the last
  concluded one.)`. That is the case `DEFAULT_DEPTH` exists for, observed rather
  than argued. Refusals 0.
  `GITHUB_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) python3 tests/record_status.py`

- **Standing cost, local: 1.01 s / 1.04 s / 0.99 s** over three runs of the
  discovery path, two GETs each, exit 1 each, **0 UNREADABLE**. Timed with
  `python3 -c 'import time…'` around `python3 tests/record_status.py`. Offered
  as the shape of the work, not as the CI figure, which is the line above.

- **Entity checks: 1254 at the merge base `4e7d783`, 1274 at this head — 20
  added,** 17 in the original change and 3 answering the review. Refusals n/a
  (no API). Measured at both ends rather than carried: the merge base moved from
  `8dc7813` to `4e7d783` and the count at it is unchanged, so the nine merged
  commits added no entity check.
  `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/entities.py | tail -1`, run in this
  worktree and in a second locked detached worktree at the merge base.

- **Structural ratchet: unchanged at both ends.** `custom_components/` is
  untouched, and `python3 tests/structure.py` prints `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`
  in this worktree and in the `origin/main` one. **No budget raise is asked
  for.**

- **Policy budgets: no capped file is touched.** `docs/plan-2026-09-open-issues.md`
  is matched by no `POLICY_GLOBS` pattern, so its row costs no cap. Read the
  instrument, not a value: `node .claude/workflows/policy_lint.mjs --budgets`.

- **Gate scope: `MODE: FULL`, `scope.run` empty.** `tests/closure.py` is a gate
  file, and the printed reason is *"changes the gate itself, so every closure is
  suspect"* — not an instruction to reproduce a forty-minute CI run for a diff
  that changes zero production lines. See `## Friction`.
  `D=$(mktemp -d); python3 tests/closure.py select --diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD) --workdir "$D"; cat "$D/scope.txt" "$D/scope.run"`

  What was run locally instead, all green at this head:
  `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/entities.py` (1274 ok),
  `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/closure.py selftest` (8 ok),
  `python3 tests/structure.py` (`STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`),
  `node .claude/workflows/policy_lint.mjs` (0 errors, 36 files),
  `node .claude/workflows/rules_sync.mjs --check`,
  and `node tests/card_drift.mjs 4e7d783…` (exit 0, 34 states identical).

## Red checks

**`pr-contract` went red at this head and then green 36 seconds later, and the cause is mine:
I pushed before setting the body.** `failure` at `20:36:30Z`, `success` at `20:37:06Z`, the
failing step being ``ERROR [pr-body] `## Head` does not name bc76774``. That is the S10 ordering —
commit, write the body against that SHA, *then* push — and it is the **third** time I have broken
it today, twice on this pull request's neighbours and once here, on the branch whose previous
round's reviewer specifically recorded that the ordering had held.

**The cheaper detector exists and is the same program**: `node .claude/workflows/policy_lint.mjs
--pr-body <file> --head <sha>`, which `tools/audit/prepr.sh` runs locally. **Its countermeasure is
filed as #678 and built in #715** — `tools/audit/push.sh` refuses before pushing anything. #715 is
eleven review rounds deep and every one of those rounds has been about its body rather than its
code; this red is one more entry in its cost case, and I am recording it as such rather than as an
apology.

Six, and they are five different answers. **CI is fully terminal at `e223ad6`:
four red — `closures`, `closures-autofix`, `nightly-status`, `record-status` —
and every other context green, `fast (3.13)` and `fast (3.14)` included.
Refusals 0.** Items 0, 4 and 5 are read at `e223ad6`; items 1-3 are the history
at `689b3cc` and earlier, kept because the account is what a reviewer checks.
**None of the four is this branch's**, and each is answered below. Read from the check-runs API, not `gh pr checks`, which
hides a red-then-green run:
`gh api "repos/tvofi/heatpump_optimizer/commits/<head>/check-runs?filter=all&per_page=100" -q '.check_runs[]|"\(.status)\t\(.conclusion)\t\(.name)"'`

**0. `closures` and `closures-autofix` — red at `e223ad6`, and NOT this
branch's. `main` is red on the same check, and I cannot make the repair from
this machine.** Stated rather than worked around.

```
UNDER-SCOPED: tests/card_drift.mjs really reads 1 file(s) the committed closure
does not list:
    .gitignore
```

**Whose it is, measured rather than argued.** `closures` is `failure` on `main`
at `6762747` — #743's own merge commit — and still at `4e7d783`. Refusals 0.
`gh api "repos/tvofi/heatpump_optimizer/commits/<sha>/check-runs?filter=all&per_page=100" -q '.check_runs[]|select(.name|test("closures"))|"\(.conclusion)\t\(.name)"'`
The cause is #743's own new `git` invocation — `claimsAreThisBranchs(git, ref)`,
the guard this branch is glad to have — and `git` reads `.gitignore`. No open
pull request owns the repair; #745 owns the *other* main-produced red, the #741
disposition row.

**Why I cannot make it here, and this is the load-bearing part.** The bot said
so first: `closures-autofix` reported `skip-still-fails` — *"THE REPAIR DID NOT
HAPPEN … its rule against re-recording an UNDER-SCOPED yourself does not apply
once the bot has reported that it did not"* — and handed over
`./tests/derive_closures.sh --single <script>`. I ran it, and it **does not
produce the repair on Darwin**:

```
GOLDEN_REF=4e7d783 ./tests/derive_closures.sh --single tests/card_drift.mjs
  tests/card_drift.mjs         69 files      # unchanged; only "seconds" moved
recorded: how=node-fs-trace, 6 files, `.gitignore` absent
```

`.gitignore` is read by the **`git` child process**, not by Node. Linux records
node lanes under `strace -f`, which follows children; Darwin has no strace and
SIP blocks dtruss, so `closure.py` falls back to `tests/node_fs_trace.mjs`, an
`fs`/loader wrap that sees Node's own opens and nothing a subprocess does. The
merge is union-only for exactly this reason — `overlay[k] = set(closures[k]) |
fresh` when `how == "node-fs-trace"`, plus `_keep_committed_files`'s *"Never
shrink a committed closure"* — so my recording could only ever widen, and it
widened by nothing. **Committing it would have moved one timestamp and left the
check red.** `tests/closures.json` was restored byte-identically and
`git status --porcelain` is empty.

**So it is handed back and needs a Linux seat**: one `./tests/derive_closures.sh
--single tests/card_drift.mjs` on Linux adds `.gitignore` and unblocks `main`
and all seven open pull requests, this one included. That is a different
subsystem from CM-2 and a machine this seat does not have, not a judgement call.

**1. `closures` at `689b3cc` — mine, and fixed there: `success` at that head.** It printed

```
     GITHUB_TOKEN=bogus  python3 tests/record_status.py --sha a94bbaf   exit 0   (was 2)
     GITHUB_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) python3 tests/record_status.py --sha …  exit 0
```

The suite stays green while every arm — UNREADABLE **and** a real `RECORD
FAILED` — exits 0. Same shape: the report says one thing, the code CI reads says
another.

**I am not blocking on it, and the reason is measured.** `grep -rln
"sys.exit(main())" tests/ tools/` returns **12 scripts**, and no test drives that
line for any of them — including `tests/nightly_status.py`, this pull request's
own precedent (#713). It is a repository-wide shape, pre-existing, not a
regression this branch introduced, and the body already lists it under *What I
could not establish*. It belongs to whoever fixes the class, not to this fix.

Two further undriven branches, both benign and named for completeness:
`collect`'s loop exhausting without `break` (418→426 — the walk running the full
`DEFAULT_DEPTH` with nothing concluded), and `main`'s `if summary:` false arm
(458→461). Neither changes an exit code.

One qualification on the fixer's "their null controls already exist": a module
that refuses everything at `check_runs` (I forced it) makes `entities.py` raise
`record_status.Unreadable` at the `_rs_whole` setup rather than fail a named
check. The suite still exits 1, so the claim holds — but by crash, not by name.

## 4. The #741 demonstration, confirmed rather than taken

Read from `commits/<sha>/check-runs?filter=all&per_page=100 --paginate`. Refusals 0.

```
8667539  record-status: failure,failure
166b299  record-status: failure,failure
689b3cc  record-status: failure,success,success
e223ad6  record-status: failure,failure,failure,failure
```

Red, then green, then red — none of it arranged by the branch. The cause is
`main`'s own `record` run, job `103013097678`, which I read:

```
ERROR [record] … no disposition … for merged pull request #741 …
TOTAL: 1 error(s) over 31 merged pull request(s)
```

Independently, the binary at this head against the live API: `RECORD FAILED on
main e713ab4: conclusion 'failure' at 2026-09-10T19:18:26Z`, naming that same
job URL, exit 1. All four arms reproduce byte-for-byte, 0 refusals: ARM 1 `a94bbaf`
exit 1, ARM 2 `36c649d` exit 0, ARM 3 `284437e` exit 1, ARM 4 `b63470b` exit 1.

And the defect itself is visible on this pull request: `record` reports
**`skipped` four times** at this head, while being one of the 18 required contexts.

## 5. Merge obligations, re-executed after the nine-commit merge

- **Claim files byte-identical to `origin/main`**, by blob:
  `claimed_drift.txt` `44d4f96d…` both sides, `card_claimed_drift.txt`
  `018c87d8…` both sides.
- **`VERSION` `90d7013d…`, `manifest.json` `1dfcdf83…`, `RELEASE_NOTES.md`
  `4ee51306…`** — every one identical to `origin/main`'s blob. Untouched.
- **`git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main e223ad6` exits 0**, stderr empty.
  Driver installed first (`MERGE-CLAIM: already-installed`); no `MERGE-CLAIM`
  line was emitted because no claim file conflicted. `mergeStateStatus` is
  `BLOCKED`, which is the required contexts, not a conflict.
- **Ratchet green, no budget raised**: `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`;
  `tests/structure_budgets.json` and `tests/structure.py` are absent from the
  three-dot `--stat`.
- **`record-status` is still not required**: ruleset `22628467` carries **18**
  contexts, `record` among them, `record-status` not. Refusals 0.
- **Entity counts re-derived at both ends**, in two locked worktrees rather than
  carried: **1254** at the merge base `4e7d783`, **1274** at `e223ad6` — 20 added.
- **Gate scope**: `MODE: FULL`, `scope.run` empty, reason *"tests/closure.py
  changes the gate itself"*. Keyed on the mode line.
- **Caps**: 0 of the 7 changed files match `POLICY_GLOBS` (checked by extracting
  the regexes from `policy_lint.mjs` and testing the three-dot name list against
  them). `docs/HANDOVER.md` is untouched, so #719's squash hazard does not arise
  and no simulated merge was needed. `policy_lint.mjs` **exit 0**,
  `TOTAL: 0 error(s) across 36 policy file(s)` — keyed on exit status and the
  `TOTAL:` line, not on `grep '^ERROR'`, which returns 0 regardless.

## 6. Red checks at `e223ad6` — and one the body gets wrong

Read from the check-runs API with `--paginate`, not `gh pr checks`. Refusals 0.

**`pr-contract`: `success` × 3, no red at any point.** The S10 ordering break
round one found did not recur. Confirmed.

**`closures` — `failure`, and it is a required context. The body predicts it
green here, and that prediction is falsified.** The cause is not the
`governance.yml` one the body answers. I pulled the run's own
`closure-recordings` artifact and re-ran the check against it:

```
UNDER-SCOPED: tests/card_drift.mjs really reads 1 file(s) the committed closure
    does not list: .gitignore
```

Three things I measured about it, none of which the body could have known:

1. **It is `main`'s, not this branch's.** `closures` is `failure` on `main` at
   its own tip `e713ab4` **and** at #743's merge commit `6762747`. #743 added
   `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` to `tests/card_rig.mjs`, and that
   reads `.gitignore`. This branch's `tests/closures.json` differs from `main`'s
   by exactly its own two entries (`governance.yml`, `record_status.py`); the
   `card_drift.mjs` closure is byte-identical to `main`'s.
2. **`closures-autofix` cannot repair it.** I reproduced
   `closure.apply_under_scoped_recordings(<artifact>, partial=True)` locally
   against the real CI recordings: it returns **`skip-still-fails`**, which is
   why "Push the merged closures" was `skipped` and the job red. The reason is
   structural — `.gitignore` is on `closure.py`'s INERT list, so merging the
   recording produces *"files on the INERT list are inside a recorded closure"*
   and `check` refuses the pair. Waiting for the bot will not clear this one.
3. **All 22 recordings have `rc == 0`**, including `card_drift.mjs`, whose
   `stdout_tail` carries #743's guard working on a real Linux runner:
   `NOT THIS BRANCH'S TO REMOVE … card_drift: identical in all 34 states`. The
   body's account of #743 holds.

I am not blocking on it. `fix-review.md` step 11 has me check the trigger was
answered, not adjudicate the answer, and the body does name `closures`, name
`UNDER-SCOPED`, and name the autofix as its countermeasure. But the answer is
now wrong in substance, and the orchestrator should read this rather than the
body: **`closures` is red on `main` itself and no branch can turn it green.**
Clearing it needs `.gitignore` off INERT or #743's `ls-files` call stopped —
someone else's file, and `finding-propagation`/"out of scope is not a licence"
both say that is not this fix's to reach for.

`closures-autofix` — `failure`, unrequired, same cause. `nightly-status` —
`failure`, unrequired, pre-existing #533, answered. `record-status` —
`failure` × 4, unrequired, and it is the acceptance.

## What I could not establish

- **`fast (3.13)` / `fast (3.14)` are still `in_progress`** at 2026-09-10T19:43Z,
  eight minutes after I first read them. Both are required contexts and I have no
  verdict on either. Everything above is independent of them.
- **The `closures` job's own log.** `gh run view --job 103014308187 --log`
  refuses while run `34519638077` is in progress, and the redirect for
  `actions/jobs/103014308187/logs` returned no `Location`. **That is my 1 API
  refusal.** I substituted the run's `closure-recordings` artifact and the
  step-level jobs API, and re-derived the failure locally — no figure rests on
  the refused read.
- **Whether the M9 hole ever fired in production** — unchanged from round one.
- **`sys.exit(main())`** is undriven here and in eleven sibling scripts; I did
  not establish whether any check anywhere in the tree drives that line for any
  of them, only that no test does for these twelve.

Every figure above is from `e223ad6e1fb0724b37b249a475a0c6f40bdc19fa`. I
re-read the head immediately before posting and it had not moved.

nodes.title: W5-G9: the dhw profile/draws learner leaves the coordinator
nodes.body:
**W5-G9 — the first real seam move.** The hot-water usage profile and draw learner leaves `HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator` for `custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/dhw_learning.py`, one class, `DhwProfileLearner`, constructed by the coordinator and never holding it. Thirteen methods and nine module-level constants move; thirteen call sites, the snapshot-restore block and one init are re-pointed; the coordinator's pump map, which was core state initialised in a dhw init, goes to the runtime init (S5's finding once more). About forty test sites in `tests/features.py` migrate from the coordinator's private names to the learner's API — S12's "tests migrate to subsystem APIs", at last with a subsystem to migrate to. Bodies move verbatim under a stated substitution table; the residual is the boundary and nothing else, measured below. Roster group W5-G9 (#744); the owner's decisions of 2026-09-10 are the one-class shape and the `classes_over_300` raise by one. leaves #193 closed. leaves #195 open. leaves #201 open.

The judge's #193 finding still binds and this pull request does not claim otherwise: no second lobe detaches at any k, so this move relocates the learner's coupling across a boundary rather than deleting it. What it is justified by is the boundary's size, enumerated in Null control.

## Head

`450b9c66564630182a6c832e1b688621a938e006` on `claude/w5-g9-dhw-learner` — a merge of `origin/main` `ef7599e` (#748, #749) on top of `d7182d3`, the closures commit that records the new module into the eleven lanes the `closures` job named after the autofix declined; before it, `7c23177`, the commit which adds this pull request's own disposition row, marks the Wave 5 row in review and gives the handover's #662 bullet #746 and the per-kind rule inside its own four lines (405 of 406, `policy_lint` 0 errors); the first, `4d67bb1`, is the extraction (`eba098d`, cut from `4e7d783` after #744) merged with `origin/main` twice, `2072fec` (#746) and `0e43448` (#747, the per-kind claim guard), neither of which touches a coordinator or dhw file. Author pinned on every commit, the three merge commits' amended from the environment's name. Merge base `ef7599e`. Three-dot: `custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/coordinator.py`, `custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/dhw_learning.py` (new), `tests/features.py`, `tests/entities.py`, `tests/structure_budgets.json`, `tests/closures.json`, `.claude/workflows/wave-5-groups.json` (the W5-G10 carry). Three-dot adds `docs/plan-2026-09-open-issues.md` and `docs/HANDOVER.md` for the record commit.

## Mutation proof

Two mutants, each applied in place on the committed tree at `4d67bb1`, run, restored by checkout (`git status --short` empty afterwards):

- **`pattern_for` deleted from the learner** → `python3 tests/features.py` aborts with `AttributeError: 'DhwProfileLearner' object has no attribute 'pattern_for'` at `tests/features.py:9381`, the first migrated #18 blend check, after 910 checks — the suite cannot run without the method, which is detection by abort rather than by a named check, so a second mutant names the checks.
- **the day-type blend weight forced to zero** (`w = 0.0` in `pattern_for`, day-type evidence ignored) → `3 of 2136 FEATURE CHECKS FAILED`, of which **one is the mutant's**: `weekend evidence moves the weekend pattern toward late mornings`. The other two are the #525 heartbeat pair (`the reap Home Assistant's stop fires keeps the loop running` and its null control), both arms reading zero ticks in 0.00 s — the reap returning with nothing to reap — which is that instrument's own state: across five runs of `features.py` on this branch it failed in one clean run and one mutant run and passed in three clean runs, independent of the tree. Named here so the count is not read as three detections.

Clean tree at the same head: `ALL 2136 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED`, `ALL 1265 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED`.

## Null control

**The boundary, enumerated at the merge base** (the interface this move is justified by): 13 inbound call sites — `__init__` (construction and the two loaders reached by name), `_prepare_dhw_inputs` (`pattern_for`), `async_update_thermal_params` (an explicit cooling rate), `_update_current_state` (`async_learn_dynamics`), `_learner_snapshot_payloads`, `_apply_learner_payloads`, `_async_watch_learning_drift` and `async_restore_learned_snapshot` (payload, restore, saves); reads of the learner's state from `_prepare_dhw_inputs`, `_dhw_setpoint_sweep`, `_dhw_view` and `_learning_view`; one outbound dependency, `_learning_frozen`, which arrives as a callable; two observed facts, whether the plan is heating the tank and whether external heat is active, which arrive as callables; and the shared `ThermalParameters` the learner writes its pattern and cooling rate into exactly where the coordinator's methods did. Nothing else crosses. The learner never receives the coordinator: `_helper(self, …)` and `getattr(self, "_ctx", self)` reach-through are refused (S3, #512), and the new module imports nothing from `coordinator.py`, so `local_imports` stays at its budget.

**Provenance — verbatim under a stated substitution table.** `provenance_g9.py` (in Figures) extracts each moved body at the merge base (`0e43448`; the file is identical at `4e7d783`, `2072fec` and `0e43448`, since neither #746 nor #747 touched it), applies the substitutions (sixteen attribute renames, twelve method renames, the `_ctx` hop to `self._params`) and diffs it against the learner's body at head. Ten of twelve bodies: residual 0 lines. `async_learn_dynamics`: 16 residual lines — three docstring lines, the heating observation through its callable, the freeze check through its callable, `self._learner_freeze_reason = frozen; return` becoming `return frozen` with the two bare returns becoming `return None` and one added at the end. `async_fold_draw_stats`: 5 residual lines — the `ctx` hop and the external-heat read becoming the callable, `ctx._thermal_params` becoming `self._params`. Total 21, every one a boundary edit named here.

**The ratchet at both ends** (`python3 tests/structure.py`), predicted by the simulation in the approved plan and measured on this tree:

| row | merge base | head | predicted |
|---|---|---|---|
| `coordinator_loc` / `max_class_loc` | 9999 | 9604 | 9584 |
| `coordinator_methods` | 251 | 239 | 238 |
| `coordinator_attrs` | 175 | 162 | 163 |
| `coordinator_multiassigned_attrs` | 136 | 126 | — |
| `internal_call_edges` | 362 | 335 | 334 |
| `cross_seam_fraction` | 0.4337 | 0.4328 | 0.4311 |
| `cut_dhw` | 103 | 81 | 72 |
| `cut_learning` | 311 | 282 | 290 |
| `functions_cc_over_15` | 35 | 34 | — |
| `classes_over_300` | 9 | **10** | 10 |

Every other row is unmoved. The two deviations from the prediction are the boundary itself: the learner's construction adds twenty lines to the init the simulation deleted whole, and the four dhw-seam methods that now read `self._dhw_learner` are charged nine references the simulation did not model because the draw statistics were co-owned at the base and are the learner's at head. `cut_learning` fell further than predicted because `_apply_learner_payloads` lost its whole restore block. `cross_seam_fraction` is inside its band and untouched in the budget file. The five-cut sum falls 863 → 813; the S5 core-reference control is flat by construction (the learner was never coupled to core through attributes) and is not the control for an extraction — the boundary above is. Gains re-recorded with `python3 tests/structure.py --record` at the merge base; **`classes_over_300` raised 9 → 10 by hand, the owner's explicit confirmation given 2026-09-10 before the push**: the learner is one class of about four hundred lines because one persisted payload holds both the profile and the cooling rate, and a two-class split would divide one Store across two objects to fit a number.

**Goldens and claims.** `GOLDEN_MODE=drift python3 tests/env_drift.py --all 2072fec` on the branch merged with that base: `NO UNCLAIMED DRIFT: 55 scenario(s) checked against 2072fec`, `NO STALE FIXTURE: 55 committed fixture(s) still match what this tree computes` — 50 byte-identical, 5 may-drift. `git diff --stat 2072fec 0e43448 -- custom_components/` is empty (#747 changed only `tests/`), so that capture is the capture at the merge base; the earlier run against `4e7d783` read the same. Under `main`'s guard before #747 the run stopped at `INHERITED CLAIMS` for #735's card list before capturing — that is what #747 fixed and what this branch merged. Both claim files byte-identical to `origin/main` three-dot; `VERSION` and the manifest untouched. The two Home Assistant stores keep their keys and `DHW_PROFILE_STORE_VERSION`, so a running install loads what it saved.

**Suites.** at `4d67bb1`, run alone under `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub`: `python3 tests/entities.py` → `ALL 1265 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED` (1254 at the base plus #746's and #747's pins; the store census now walks the learner); `python3 tests/features.py` → `ALL 2136 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED` (2133 at the base plus #746's). One earlier run of `features.py` failed exactly one check, the #525 heartbeat pair, while a closure recording ran concurrently — that pair reads zero ticks under load and is documented as the instrument, not the tree; the solo re-run passed it and every run since. `tests/golden.py` in drift mode defers to `env_drift --all`, reported above.

**The self-row, in a standalone clone with the squash simulated on the merged tree** (`git merge-tree --write-tree` of live `origin/main` `0e43448` and this head, committed onto `main` with subject `(#750)`, the clone's `refs/remotes/origin/main` at it, tree checked out) → `policy_lint.mjs --record --since v6.3.20`: 34 merged, **1 without — #741**, the other lane's merge, whose row is in flight as #745. Parent tree: 3 without, adds #750 and #746 — #746's row is in flight as #748, and this tree reads it as dispositioned only because the handover clause names #746 and `checkRecord` reads the whole handover: a mention, not its row, stated so nobody credits this branch with it. Row-only cut: 1 without — does not fire, the Wave 5 row (`In review as #750`) satisfies the check, as on #740. Every mention cut: 2 without, adds #750 — fires.

**Closures.** A new production module is in no recorded closure, so the local selector went `MODE: FULL` on this diff by rule and named the file — the cheaper detector, and it fired before the first push. `./tests/derive_closures.sh --single tests/env_drift.py` recorded it into the `env_drift` and `golden` closures before that push, which is what `tests/entities.py`'s coverage pin reads. The `closures` job on `7c23177` then named eleven more lanes under-scoped by the same one file, and `closures-autofix` declined with `skip-still-fails` — no bot commit — because its re-check failed on a second cause this branch did not make: `main`'s own `closures` had been red since `6762747` on `.gitignore` (declared inert while `card_drift.mjs` read it), which #749 fixed. Per `ci-autofix.md`, a red autofix job hands the recording back: each of the eleven lanes is re-derived here with `--single` (nine Python lanes, Darwin-sound; the two node lanes grow their Linux lists by union and cannot shrink them), committed as `d7182d3`, and `main` merged so #749's line is in the same file: `.gitignore` in `card_drift.mjs`'s closure, `dhw_learning.py` in all thirteen lanes that read it, `orphan_files() = []`, `is_inert('.gitignore') = False`. The selector now reads `MODE: FULL` for a different reason — `tests/closures.json` changes the gate itself — which is the rule working.

**Typing.** Moved defs carry their own errors with them and every new def is annotated; `type_ignores` stays 0. The pinned toolchain runs only in CI, so `by_code` is read from the `typing` job, not asserted here.

**Tests migrated, not weakened.** The `_DhwUsage` harness was a duck-typed object borrowing two unbound coordinator methods; it is now the learner itself with persistence stubbed. The store-junk table resolves dotted paths because the DHW stores live in the learner. The snapshot-format pin (`inspect.getsource`) now reads `DhwProfileLearner.payload` and the coordinator's snapshot producer. Every migrated check asserts what it asserted before, against the object that now owns the state.

## Figures

- the ratchet rows in the table — `python3 tests/structure.py` at `0e43448` and at head; the re-record — `python3 tests/structure.py --record` on the clean tree, `recorded_at` the merge base
- the provenance residual, 21 lines over 12 bodies — `python3 provenance_g9.py 0e43448` from the repository root, the script verbatim below
- the boundary counts (13 inbound call sites, 1 outbound call, 3 co-written attributes, 2 outside writers) — an `ast` walk of the coordinator at the base for calls into and attribute writes from the thirteen methods; the same walk is in the approved plan and its rules are in the W5-G10 brief
- 50 byte-identical, 5 may-drift — `grep -c 'is byte-identical'` and `grep -c '^  may-drift'` on the `env_drift --all` log
- suite and mutation figures — the commands beside them in Null control and Mutation proof
- the store census widening (two more `Store`s found on the learner) — `tests/entities.py`, the pin `the store files it says are left under .storage are exactly the ones the coordinator keeps`, which walks the coordinator and its learner

The provenance script, verbatim:

```python
"""Provenance for W5-G9: each moved body at the merge base, under the stated substitutions,
against the learner's body at head. Prints the residual diff per method; the claim is that the
residual is exactly the boundary edits listed in the PR body and nothing else."""
import ast, difflib, subprocess, sys, textwrap, re
BASE = sys.argv[1]
base_src = subprocess.run(['git', 'show', f'{BASE}:custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/coordinator.py'], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
head_src = open('custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/dhw_learning.py').read()
PAIRS = [('_normalize_dhw_profile','normalize_profile'),('_async_load_dhw_profile','async_load_profile'),('_apply_dhw_cooling_rate','apply_cooling_rate'),('_dhw_profile_payload','payload'),('_async_save_dhw_profile','async_save_profile'),('_async_load_dhw_draws','async_load_draws'),('_async_save_dhw_draws','async_save_draws'),('_dhw_pattern_for','pattern_for'),('_async_learn_dhw_dynamics','async_learn_dynamics'),('_async_fold_draw_stats','async_fold_draw_stats'),('_async_learn_dhw_cooling','async_learn_cooling'),('_async_learn_dhw_usage','async_learn_usage')]
SUBS = [  # the substitution table, applied to the base body
 ('self._dhw_hourly_profile','self.hourly_profile'),('self._dhw_profile_weekday','self.profile_weekday'),('self._dhw_profile_weekend','self.profile_weekend'),
 ('"_dhw_profile_weekday"','"profile_weekday"'),('"_dhw_profile_weekend"','"profile_weekend"'),
 ('self._dhw_daytype_samples','self.daytype_samples'),('self._dhw_daytype_last_day','self.daytype_last_day'),('self._dhw_cooling_rate','self.cooling_rate'),('self._dhw_cooling_samples','self.cooling_samples'),
 ('self._dhw_heating_since_sample','self.heating_since_sample'),('self._draw_stats','self.draw_stats'),('self._dhw_profile_store','self.profile_store'),('self._dhw_draws_store','self.draws_store'),('self._dhw_draws_dirty','self.draws_dirty'),
 ('self._last_dhw_sample_time','self.last_sample_time'),('self._last_dhw_temp_sample','self.last_temp_sample'),
 ('getattr(self, "_ctx", self)._thermal_params','self._params'),
] + [('self.' + a + '(', 'self.' + b + '(') for a, b in PAIRS]
def body(src, name, tree_cls=None):
    t = ast.parse(src)
    nodes = [n for n in ast.walk(t) if isinstance(n, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)) and n.name == name]
    assert len(nodes) == 1, (name, len(nodes))
    n = nodes[0]; lines = src.split('\n')[n.lineno-1:n.end_lineno]
    # drop the def line(s) up to the colon that ends the signature
    i = 0
    while not lines[i].rstrip().endswith(':') or lines[i].lstrip().startswith(('"""', '#')): i += 1
    return textwrap.dedent('\n'.join(lines[i+1:])).rstrip('\n') + '\n'
total = 0
for old, new in PAIRS:
    b = body(base_src, old)
    for a, c in SUBS: b = b.replace(a, c)
    h = body(head_src, new)
    d = [l for l in difflib.unified_diff(b.splitlines(), h.splitlines(), lineterm='', n=0) if l.startswith(('+', '-')) and not l.startswith(('+++', '---'))]
    total += len(d)
    print(f"{old:28s} -> {new:22s} residual {len(d):2d} line(s)")
    for l in d: print("    " + l)
print(f"RESULT provenance_residual_lines={total}")
```

## Red checks

On `7c23177`, read from `commits/<sha>/check-runs?filter=all` paginated: **`closures`** red and **`closures-autofix`** red (`skip-still-fails`), plus `nightly-status` (`main`'s cron, not this head's). Two causes, each answered. (1) This branch's new module was unrecorded in eleven lanes: the cheaper detector is the local selector, which prints `MODE: FULL` with the file's name in under a second and did so before the first push; its standing cost is nothing beyond the selector every push already runs. The standing countermeasure for the record is the autofix job, which exists and declined here for cause (2). Remedy taken: the recordings, re-derived locally as the rule directs once the job has gone red. (2) `main`'s `closures` was red since `6762747` on `.gitignore`, a classification defect in no way reachable from this diff; its own fix is #749, merged into this branch. Neither cause is a defect in the moved code, and no root-cause seat is owed beyond what #749's body already records. This head's runs are read after the push and this section corrected if one differs.

## Forward-carry

`.claude/workflows/wave-5-groups.json`: W5-G10's brief already carries the gate this move measured (a cohesive extraction raises `cross_seam_fraction` while the absolute count falls; R1 replaces the metric). This pull request adds no new constraint on a later stage; the boundary-charge finding (nine references the simulation did not model) is written into W5-G10's brief as a re-measurement note (`.claude/workflows/wave-5-groups.json`, the `CARRY FROM W5-G9` block: the boundary charge, the misfit S5 control, the provenance instrument, the closure recording), committed in `eba098d` and read back with `python3 -c` — one occurrence, `brief_lint.mjs` exit 0.

## Friction

nodes.title: closures: .gitignore was declared unread while a gate script read it
nodes.body:
`main` has been red on **`closures`** — a required context — since `6762747`, which is my own merge of #743.

## Head

`7e5f389179c1024c47ad52aee25cbadebdb1054e`

## Mutation proof

The deliverable is a classification, so the mutation is the classification it replaces. Reverting `.gitignore` to plain `INERT` reproduces the contradiction exactly: `closure.py`'s own reader reports `is_inert('.gitignore') = True` while `tests/closures.json` records it in `tests/card_drift.mjs`'s closure — the INERT-and-recorded pair #357 exists to refuse, and the shape that let `tests/nightly_ha.py`'s blocking pin go stale in silence under #533.

At this head: `is_inert('.gitignore') = False`, `orphan_files() = []`, and `PYTHONPATH=$PWD/tests/hastub python3 tests/entities.py` prints `ALL 1257 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED`.

## Null control

`orphan_files()` returning `[]` is only meaningful if it can return something. Removing `.gitignore` from `card_drift.mjs`'s closure **without** putting it back on `INERT` leaves it neither inert nor in any closure, which is the state `tests/entities.py` refuses with *"these force the FULL suite when touched"* — so the empty list at this head is a measurement rather than a default.

## Figures

- CI's own words, from the `closures` job on `main`: `UNDER-SCOPED: tests/card_drift.mjs really reads 1 file(s) the committed closure does not list: .gitignore`.
- `closures` conclusion at `6762747`, `4e7d783`, `e713ab4` and `2072fec`: **`failure`** at every one. Command: `gh api "repos/tvofi/heatpump_optimizer/commits/<sha>/check-runs?filter=all&per_page=100" --paginate --jq '.check_runs[]|select(.name=="closures")|.conclusion'`. **API refusals: 0.**
- `tests/card_drift.mjs`'s closure: **69 → 70** files. Command: `python3 -c "import json;print(len(json.load(open('tests/closures.json'))['closures']['tests/card_drift.mjs']))"`.
- The gate at this head prints `MODE: FULL — every test script runs`, `reason: tests/closure.py changes the gate itself, so every closure is suspect`. **Key on the mode line, not a count** — and note the line is indented, so `^MODE:` matches nothing.

## Red checks

**`closures` and `closures-autofix` are red on `main` and on every open pull request, and this change is the answer to them.** `closures-autofix` cannot repair it and says so: merging the recording while `.gitignore` is INERT produces the contradiction, so it returns `skip-still-fails` and hands the command back. Waiting for the bot, which `ci-autofix.md` normally requires, cannot clear this one.

The cheaper detector already exists and already fired — `closures` named the file and the script on the first push to `main` after #743. What was missing was not detection but a repair path, because the only automated one is blocked by the very contradiction it would create.

`nightly-status` is red on every branch and is not among ruleset `22628467`'s 18 required contexts.

## Forward-carry

**The recording is bounded deliberately, and the bound is the finding — corrected here, because the
first version of this section overstated it in two ways and this is where a later seat looks.**

`.gitignore` is recorded only in `tests/card_drift.mjs`, because that is the only place CI observed
the read.

**Corrected: it is not "every gate script that shells out to `git`".** Seven recorded scripts invoke
`git`, and only **two** run a command that opens this repository's `.gitignore` — `env_drift.py`
(`three_dot_files`) and `structure.py` (`git status --porcelain`). `entities.py` runs `add -A` in a
throwaway temp repository outside `CLOSURE_ROOT`, so it does not. The residual is therefore
**`structure.py` alone**, since `env_drift.py`'s path is `run_always` in `run.sh` and is never scoped
out.

**Corrected: a Linux `derive_closures.sh` would not close it either.** I wrote that `strace -f`
follows child processes where a Darwin `fs` wrapper does not. That is true of the Node lanes and
irrelevant to these two: Python lanes record through `sys.addaudithook`, which never sees a child
process **on any platform**. **The asymmetry is the instrument, not the machine** — so "re-derive on
Linux" is not the remedy, and a seat who believes it will wait for something that cannot happen.

**What the hole actually is**: inherited and *narrowed* by this change rather than created — a
`.gitignore`-only diff selected **0** scripts before it and selects **2** after. Closing the residual
means teaching the Python recorder about subprocess reads, or recording `structure.py`'s by hand
from the same evidence CI prints. Union-only merge semantics (`_keep_committed_files`, *"Never
shrink a committed closure"*) mean a later widening cannot lose anything.

**One structural note from the review, left as owed rather than fixed here**: `.gitignore` now sits
in **both** `INERT` and `INERT_EXCEPT`. That is correct today — `is_inert` tests `INERT_EXCEPT`
first — but a future trim of `INERT_EXCEPT` silently re-creates #357's contradiction. Removing the
`INERT` entry outright is the cleaner shape and is not made here, because `main` is red and this
change is the narrowest thing that clears it.

## Friction

- `ci-autofix.md`: contradiction: it says wait for the bot and do not duplicate its repair. Here the bot reports `skip-still-fails` and cannot repair, so waiting is unbounded. The rule needs the case where the bot declines.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Fix review: merge 7e5f389179c1024c47ad52aee25cbadebdb1054e

Reviewed from a locked detached worktree at `7e5f389`, adversarially, re-deriving every figure rather than reading it. **API refusals: 0** on every `gh` call below (each was run with stderr captured and counted).

## 1. Is the diagnosis right? Yes — established three independent ways.

`claimsAreThisBranchs` → `threeDotFiles` (`tests/card_rig.mjs:444`) runs three git commands, the third being **`git ls-files --others --exclude-standard`**.

- **Functional**: in a throwaway repo, that command's output changes when `.gitignore` gains a line, and `git check-ignore -v` names the source as `.gitignore:1:...`.
- **Open-detector**: replacing `.gitignore` with a **FIFO** and running each command under `alarm(4)` — a command that opens it blocks. Result: `ls-files --others --exclude-standard` **blocks**, `status` **blocks**, `add -A` **blocks**. `rev-parse`, `show`, `diff --name-only <ref>...HEAD`, `diff --name-only HEAD`, plain `ls-files`, `ls-files -z -- <path>`, `merge-base`, `log`, `rev-list`, `worktree add --detach` **do not**.
- **It is the child process, not Node**: `grep -n gitignore tests/card_drift.mjs tests/card_rig.mjs` → nothing. And I recorded the script on this box: `python3 tests/closure.py record tests/card_drift.mjs` → `how: node-fs-trace  rc: 0  files: 6`, **`.gitignore` absent**. The Darwin tracer wraps Node's `fs`; only Linux `strace -f` follows the `git` child. That is the null control on the instrument, and it is also why a Darwin `--single` could not have produced this line.

## 2. Is `INERT_EXCEPT` the right mechanism for a bare entry? Yes — driven, not read.

`is_inert` tests `rel in INERT_EXCEPT` **before** the prefix scan, so membership is exact-match and a bare entry is exempted identically to a prefix member:

- at `7e5f389`: `is_inert('.gitignore') = False`, `inert_closure_violations(committed) = []`
- at the merge base `2072fec`: `is_inert('.gitignore') = True`

**Mutation proof re-run.** Reverting *only* the classification (`INERT_EXCEPT` back to `("tools/audit/preflight.sh",)`, closure entry kept): `inert_closure_violations = ['.gitignore']` and `closure.check(recordings, partial=True)` → **rc 1**, printing the #357 refusal verbatim. Not vacuous.

**Both-ends with the finder's harness.** The finder here is CI's own `closures` job, and its instrument is `closure.py check`. I fed the *same* synthetic-but-faithful recording (`committed closure ∪ {.gitignore}`, `rc: 0`, `how: strace`) to both trees:

```
RESULT check(partial=True) @ 2072fec (pre-fix)  rc=1   UNDER-SCOPED / INERT contradiction
RESULT check(partial=True) @ 7e5f389 (head)     rc=0   "committed closures cover every file this run touched"
```

## 3. Is the bound honest? Mostly — but two sentences in the body are wrong, in the safe direction.

**How many other recorded scripts invoke `git`: 6** (of 21 recorded scripts; `card_drift.mjs` is the 7th). They are `deployment_shape.py`, `entities.py`, `env_drift.py`, `stress.py`, `structure.py`, `typing_ruler.py`.

The body says **"Every gate script that shells out to `git` reads it too"**. **That is false**, and I could not re-derive it. Cross-referencing each script's actual git invocations against the FIFO probe above:

| script | git commands | reads repo `.gitignore`? |
|---|---|---|
| `env_drift.py` | `three_dot_files` (`env_drift.py:1673`), incl. `ls-files --others --exclude-standard`, `cwd=repo` | **yes** |
| `structure.py` | `git status --porcelain -- custom_components` | **yes** |
| `entities.py` | `ls-files docs`, `merge-base`, and `add -A` **inside a throwaway temp repo** | no (the `add -A` reads the *temp* repo's file, outside `CLOSURE_ROOT`) |
| `deployment_shape.py` | `ls-files -z -- <pkg>` | no |
| `stress.py` | `rev-parse`, `worktree add/remove` | no |
| `typing_ruler.py` | `rev-parse` | no |

So the true residual is **2 scripts, not 6**. Second correction: the body's remedy — *"a later seat on Linux should re-derive and widen; `strace -f` follows child processes"* — **would not close it**. Python lanes record through `sys.addaudithook` on **every** platform, and an audit hook sees only the parent interpreter's opens; a child `git` is invisible to it on Linux exactly as on Darwin. The asymmetry is the instrument, not the platform.

**Verdict on the hole: inherited and narrowed, not created.** Before this change `.gitignore` was INERT, so a change to it selected **nothing**; `env_drift.py` and `structure.py` were already under-selected on it and remain so. Measured:

```
RESULT select --files .gitignore @ 2072fec   MODE: SCOPED -- 0 script(s) run, 21 scoped out.
RESULT select --files .gitignore @ 7e5f389   MODE: SCOPED -- 2 script(s) run, 19 scoped out.
                                             RUN tests/card_drift.mjs, RUN tests/plan_view.py
```

And `env_drift.py`'s exposure is closed in practice anyway: `tests/run.sh:309` is `run_always "$PYTHON" tests/env_drift.py --claims-only "$GOLDEN_REF"`, never scoped out, and `--claims-only` reaches `stale_claims_judged` → `three_dot_files`. That leaves **one** genuinely unrecorded, scopable `.gitignore` dependency: `structure.py`'s `git status --porcelain -- custom_components`. It predates #743 and this PR.

Neither correction changes the classification or the recording, and both err toward *over*-stating the hole, so neither blocks. I flag them because the Forward-carry section is where a later seat would look, and it currently points at a remedy that would not work.

I also checked no **second** node script will under-scope on main's next Linux derive: `tests/card.mjs` imports `threeDotFiles`/`claimsAreThisBranchs` but drives them with **stub** functions (`tests/card.mjs:7530-7550`), never spawning `git`.

## 4. Blast radius

- `closure.py selftest` → `ALL 8 closure shrink pins PASSED`, exit 0.
- `PYTHONPATH=$PWD/tests/hastub python3 tests/entities.py` → `ALL 1257 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED`, exit 0. Body's figure re-derived exactly.
- `orphan_files() == []` at head.
- Gate at head: `MODE: FULL -- every test script runs, nothing is scoped out.` / `reason: tests/closure.py changes the gate itself, so every closure is suspect`. Keyed on the mode line; the line is indented and `^MODE:` matches nothing.
- Selecting `card_drift.mjs` (plus its producer `plan_view.py`) on a `.gitignore` change is the intended semantics and is what the table now says.

## 5. Can `closures-autofix` repair it? No — verified, not taken.

Simulated the PR path on the merge-base tree with the recording above:

```
RESULT apply_under_scoped_recordings(partial=True) @ 2072fec  ->  skip-still-fails
RESULT tests/closures.json left unrepaired (.gitignore absent)  ->  True
RESULT autofix_report("closures-autofix","skip-still-fails")    ->  rc 1  (red)
```

The mechanism is exactly as the body describes: `merge(partial=True)` skips `inert_closure_violations` (it lives past the `if partial:` return), the second `check` runs it on the committed table, `rc2 != 0`, `_restore()`, `skip-still-fails`.

Real CI agrees. PR #738's `closures-autofix` job log (run 34519638077, job 103018867088):

```
AUTOFIX: skip-still-fails
closures-autofix: skip-still-fails -- THE REPAIR DID NOT HAPPEN.
```

`ci-autofix.md`'s wait is explicitly conditional — *"A red autofix job means there will be no bot commit… Read the summary line, re-derive the script it names and commit tests/closures.json"* — and `autofix_report`'s own text says the rule against re-recording an UNDER-SCOPED yourself does not apply once the bot has reported that it did not. **No rule violation.** The Friction note is slightly off: `ci-autofix.md` already carries the declined case; what it lacks is nothing.

## 6. Null control — both arms driven

```
RESULT arm A: closure entry removed, INERT_EXCEPT kept
       orphan_files() -> ['.gitignore']
       tests/entities.py -> FAIL every tracked file is either measured or deliberately classified
                            [these force the FULL suite when touched: .gitignore]   exit 1
RESULT arm B (head, unmutated): orphan_files() -> []   tests/entities.py exit 0
```

The empty list is a measurement.

## 7. Checks — read from the commit's `check-runs` API with `--paginate`, not `gh pr checks`

22 runs at `7e5f389`. All **18** required contexts of ruleset `22628467` are `success`, `closures` included (completed 19:58:39Z), and `fast (3.13)` / `fast (3.14)` completed `success` at 20:15Z after the expected ~25-minute `MODE: FULL`. The only non-green run is `nightly-status` (`failure`), which I confirmed is **not** among the 18 required contexts. Nothing red on a gate check, so step 11 is satisfied without a root-cause answer being owed here. (Small correction: the body says `nightly-status` is red on every branch; on `main` it is `skipped`. Immaterial.)

`closures` on `main` is still `failure` — this PR is the repair.

## 8. Hygiene

- `tests/golden/claimed_drift.txt` and `tests/golden/card_claimed_drift.txt`: **byte-identical to `origin/main`** (`git diff --quiet origin/main -- <file>` clean for both). This branch claims nothing.
- `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main 7e5f389` → **exit 0**, no conflict on any path, no `MERGE-CLAIM:` line to read.
- Three-dot diff is `tests/closure.py` (+9/-1) and `tests/closures.json` (+1) only. `VERSION`, `custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/manifest.json` and `RELEASE_NOTES.md` untouched.
- No capped file in the diff: all 24 metrics in `tests/structure_budgets.json` are measured over `PACKAGE_DIR` (`structure.py:320`, `PACKAGE_DIR.rglob("*.py")`); nothing under `tests/` is capped.
- Head at posting time is `7e5f389179c1024c47ad52aee25cbadebdb1054e`, the head I measured. It did not move under the review.

## One non-blocking observation

`.gitignore` is now in **both** `INERT` and `INERT_EXCEPT`. Behaviour is correct and driven above, and this is forced for `tools/audit/preflight.sh` (it sits inside a prefix), but `.gitignore` is a bare entry that could simply have been deleted from `INERT`. Leaving it there makes that list assert something false about a file, and one day someone will trim `INERT_EXCEPT` and silently re-create #357's contradiction. Worth a follow-up line, not a block.

nodes.title: record: leftover row for #746 squash 2072fec
nodes.body:
`main` went red on `record` after #746 merged: the leftover row named draft #706, and `checkRecord` looks for the merged number. This adds the #746 row and this pull request's own. Not taking #741 — that row is [#745](https://github.com/tvofi/heatpump_optimizer/pull/745). leaves #201 open.

Two commits. The self-row is second because a disposition needs the pull request's number and the number does not exist until the pull request does.

## Head

`c4961061a290b2a009b9ae34978386bca27e4efc`

## Mutation proof

Deleting the `#746` leftover line and re-running `node .claude/workflows/policy_lint.mjs --record --since v6.3.20` names #746 again (`2 without a disposition`). Restoring the line leaves only #741, which is #745's claim.

The self-row is not testable at this branch head: `--record` enumerates merges on GitHub's `origin/main`, and #748 is not in that window until it lands. A record pull request that omits itself moves the red rather than clearing it — the #696 / #708 rule.

## Null control
