`10 + 2` is gone. **The placement the row now names is the one that produces the stated numbers**, and I measured the other arm to confirm the row is doing work: inserting `return 'instrument'` **after** the `gh`/`git` line gives `9 passed, 4 failed`; inserting it **before** gives `6 passed, 7 failed` — also 13, also exactly what the body says that placement gives. The ambiguity the round-two block turned on is resolved in the row itself and both readings are stated correctly.

Same invariant on the other two instruments. `figure_lint.mjs --self-test` is **22** at head, `prepr.sh --self-test` **38**, and all seven of those mutations reproduce, restored byte-identical:

| mutation | body | measured | sum |
|---|---|---|---|
| `if (bad.length)` → `if (false && bad.length)` | `20 / 2` | **matches**, same two assertions | 22 |
| `!flags` branch → `flags = new Set(); used = sub` | `21 / 1` | **matches** | 22 |
| `if (inTree(rel))` → `if (true)` | `21 / 1` | **matches** | 22 |
| `gh` accept path made a refusal | `21 / 1` | **matches** — *a body whose figure commands all resolve is silent (null control; got 3)* | 22 |
| `ghEnv` returns the inherited environment | `21 / 1` | **matches** — *the word resolves to nothing and the alias does not run* | 22 |
| containment never fires, `rel` is raw | `21 / 1` | **matches** | 22 |
| `prepr.sh` `figures_check` rewired to `policy_lint.mjs --pr-body` | `36 / 2` | **matches**, and the two failures are the output-reading assertions | 38 |

**Ten mutations, ten reproductions, ten totals equal to the assertion count.** Nothing in `## Mutation proof` is now a number its command does not print.

## What I re-took at this head

**Null control, my own run, the live corpus** — 11 open pull requests, each at its own `refs/pull/<n>/head`, resolved with `--at`, 23 `gh`/`git` calls, **0 refusals**:

| PR | head | resolved | not verified | refused |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| #742 | `07fa9d8` | 1 | 1 | **0** |
| #741 | `6ab7e8c` | 5 | 0 | **0** |
| #738 | `689b3cc` | 8 | 11 | **0** |
| #736 | `d237c62` | 9 | 5 | **0** |
| #732 | `72fe4ed` | 23 | 7 | **0** |
| #723 | `3b2d088` | 4 | 5 | **0** |
| #722 | `801841a` | 20 | 3 | **0** |
| #719 | `405c875` | 8 | 3 | **0** |
| #715 | `1ab940b` | 8 | 12 | **0** |
| #706 | `a534b95` | no `## Figures`, rc 0 | | **0** |
| #704 | `8c395fb` | no `## Figures`, rc 0 | | **0** |

**0 refused across all eleven, including this body at this head.** Three of these (#742, #741, and #738 at a moved head) are bodies written since the fixer last tuned anything, so the result is not an artefact of the corpus under test.

**Both arms on a real body.** #722 unmodified → `rc 0`, `0 refused`. The same body with `--arg n "$n"` inserted into one `gh api` call and no other character changed → `rc 1`, `1 refused`, and the refusal names the flag. **Dead-arm control**: `FIGURE_LINT_GH=/nonexistent/gh --self-test` → `14 passed, 4 failed`, and the same variable over #722's body **refuses 11 `gh` lines rather than accepting them** — the inventory arm cannot die silently.

**Both corrections re-derive a third time, under the branch's own rule, on a corpus that has moved again.** `node .claude/workflows/figure_census.mjs`, which imports `figure_lint.mjs`'s recogniser, so this is the checker's counting rule and not one I built (contract step 8). 11 bodies, 2 with no `## Figures`, **0 API refusals**:

| class | commands | templated |
|---|---|---|
| `gh` | 29 | 8 |
| `git` | 25 | 3 |
| in-tree instrument | 60 | 6 |
| inline code | 5 | 0 |
| other interpreter | 3 | 2 |
| **total** | **122** | **19** |

`gh` is **29 of 122** — about a quarter, not most — and in-tree instruments at 60 are the largest class, so reason 2's correction holds. Templated is **19 of 122**, and **6 of 60** among the in-tree instruments #679 actually targets, so 54 of 60 instrument figures are literally spawnable: reason 1 is a cost and not a veto, as the header now says. The absolute totals differ from the body's (122 vs 112) and from round two's (115) because the window is open and the corpus moves — which is precisely why the enumerator is in the tree and the literals are only in `## Figures`. **Three independent runs under two different counting rules agree on both directions.**

**Surfaces, ratchet, gate.** `VERSION`, the manifest, both claim files, `structure_budgets.json` and `policy_budgets.json`: **no lines** in the three-dot diff against `a94bbaf`. `RELEASE_NOTES.md` heading delta `0`. `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`, no metric moved. `ALL 1244 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED`. `closure.orphan_files()` `[]`, `is_inert()` `True` for both new scripts. Gate: `MODE: SCOPED -- 0 script(s) run, 21 scoped out`, `scope.run` one newline — keyed on the mode line, never the count. Six corpus lints exit 0 (`policy_lint.mjs`, `policy_lint_mutants.mjs`, `rules_sync.mjs --check`, `fragments_sync.mjs`, `check-wave-script.mjs`, `brief_lint.mjs`).

**This branch authored no card claim.** `git diff a94bbaf...HEAD -- tests/golden/card_claimed_drift.txt` is empty, both directions. The two claim files are **not** byte-identical to `origin/main` today, and the divergence is entirely main's: `git log a94bbaf..origin/main -- tests/golden/card_claimed_drift.txt` names exactly `8dc7813` (#735), which added the ten `# tank bar on Setup` lines. A squash of this pull request applies its three-dot diff, which touches neither file. `python3 tests/env_drift.py --all` prints `RECORD PR CLAIMS: ... they differ from the baseline's` locally — that is the two-dot reading `CLAUDE.md` warns about, main-produced, and nothing for this branch to do.

**Checks and the root-cause trigger.** Read from `commits/72fe4ed/check-runs?filter=all&per_page=100 --paginate`: **24 run records, 24 distinct names**, so no red-then-green is hidden. One red — `nightly-status` (`failure`) — and it is **not** among the 18 required contexts on ruleset `22628467 main-protect` (I listed them). It is named and answered in `## Red checks`. Every one of the 18 required contexts is `success` or `skipped`. Trigger answered.

`fast (3.13)` and `fast (3.14)` are **green** at this head, both started `17:17` — after #735 merged at `17:06`. The repository-wide `card_drift.mjs` red is a `MODE: FULL` phenomenon on `main`; this branch selects zero scripts, and in any case it wrote none of the claims that cause it. Main-produced, not this branch's, and a separate fix is in flight.

**Forward-carry: present and unchanged.** `docs/plan-2026-09-open-issues.md` line 397, the **#541** row — read out of the file, not the diff. It carries the precondition in its positive form, **the control** (*running it twice is the whole test*), the two further preconditions, and the re-measurement instruction naming the enumerator. The #679 row at line 400 is the disposition and carries the corrections qualitatively with no literal from the open window.

**`## Approval` is present** and names what changes for a seat: `pr-contract` gains three steps and can refuse a body for the shape of a command, the template states that refusal, `prepr.sh` binds every seat locally, and `figure_census.mjs` is the enumerator a later stage re-runs. **This still needs the owner's approval before merging** — it changes a required context and a role contract, and the body is right to say so.

## Things I could not establish, and one note

- **The absolute census totals are a sliding window and will not converge.** 112 in the body, 115 last round, 122 today, over 8, 9 and 11 bodies. The body says this will happen and puts the enumerator in the tree for it. The *directions* — `gh` about a fifth to a quarter, instruments the largest class, templated a small minority — reproduce under every rule anyone has applied. I report the shares as confirmed and the absolutes as unfixable by construction.
- **Round two's end-to-end containment work I did not repeat**, per the dispatch: the sentinel arms and the `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` route. What I did re-take is the committed form of that claim — the `ghEnv` mutation, which kills *the word resolves to nothing and the alias does not run* — so the assertion is live at this head even though I did not re-run the sentinel.
- **Non-blocking, carried from round two and still true**: `figure_lint.mjs` line 583 `mkdtemp`s beside the repository root rather than in `os.tmpdir()`, which the file's two other `mkdtemp` calls use. It is race-free and removed in a `finally`, and the assertion it pins is worth pinning. Worth moving on the next touch; not a reason to hold this.

Nothing blocks. The two findings that blocked round two are repaired at their roots rather than at the copy that was caught, and the repair to the second one is verified against the invariant — `passed + failed` equals the assertion count — rather than against the row.

nodes.title: docs: the handover restated two Delivery-status rows and had three lines of headroom against a cap
nodes.body:
Third repair round on this branch, all three after a `claims` block. The review
at `1c17ec8` reproduced the whole verdict finding across three independent
sweeps — one a GraphQL sweep over every pull request's review bodies that no
earlier round ran — with zero API failures, and blocked on **two supporting
statements in `## Red checks` and nothing else**: a containment claim about
`479519f` that was false at every head this branch has had, and a "measured
closure" that `nightly_ha.py` does not have. **The conclusion they supported
survives unchanged**; the two supports are replaced with ones that hold. Nothing
the three reviews verified is re-opened.

**The head moves because round four blocked this on `claims`, and the block was
correct.** `updated-for:` named `6799ef4` (#727's merge) while the head had
merged `c157bc3` (#728), and the row quoted a `diff` result — `554a555` — that
was two commits old. The field and the quoted figure each named a SHA
independently, so they could drift apart silently, and they did.

**The repair removes the coupling rather than refreshing the number.** The row's
verification command now reads the SHA out of `updated-for:` with `sed` instead
of naming one, so it cannot disagree with the field it is checking; and the
merge count is given by an enumerator rather than stated, because it moves at
every update and that sentence had already gone stale twice. `updated-for:`
names the `origin/main` commit merged at this head. `origin/main` moved again
during the round, so the branch is updated onto `0f0cfb8` (#739).

## Head

405c875b701da743f0c2ec0488b9d8c95f471919

**Merge resolution at this head, by the orchestrator.** `main` moved again, to
`0f0cfb8` (#739), and this time `docs/plan-2026-09-open-issues.md` auto-merged
with no conflict — so unlike round four there was no hand resolution to get
wrong. The previous round's per-row account is **dropped rather than restated**:
it described a resolution this head no longer sits on, and the review was right
that it counted "rows" under a rule it never stated.

Whole-file comparison against `origin/main` as a line multiset: **0** of its
lines absent, **1** added, and that line is this branch's own row; **0** of
`main`'s disposition rows dropped. Null control: the same comparison against the
pre-merge branch side reports **2** and **0**, so the check discriminates rather
than always reporting clean. `main` has not touched `docs/HANDOVER.md` at all —
zero commits on that path between this head and `main`.

**The head moved after the verdict**, so the verdict no longer names it. What
changed is a merge commit and one row of a document this pull request does not
otherwise edit.

**Round five blocked this on `conflict`, and it found a real defect in the repair besides.**

**The defect first, because it is the more useful half.** The row's verification command captured
with `sed -n 's/^updated-for: //p'` — one literal space — while `tests/entities.py` accepts
`^updated-for:[ \t]*`. With **no** space after the colon the capture is empty, the argument
becomes `:docs/plan-2026-09-open-issues.md`, and git resolves that as the **index** rather than
erroring — so in a clean tree the broken command prints **zero bytes and exits 0**, the cleanest
result it has. That state passes `entities.py` and `policy_lint` today, so it was reachable. This
is the same failure class the whole branch is about: a command that answers nothing, silently.
Now `s/^updated-for:[[:space:]]*//p`, and **driven in the state that broke it** — it prints the
one-line add rather than nothing. The reviewer's other three edge cases were already loud
(`fatal:` plus 1528 added lines, rc 1).

**The conflict was `main`-produced.** `main` took #733, #735 and #739 after this head was cut,
colliding at the disposition list's tail. Resolved **per row against the merge base**: this
branch changed the #719 row only, `main` added three, **the intersection is empty**, so the
resolution is the union in ascending pull-request order. Whole-file line multiset against
`origin/main`: **1** line only in the resolution, **0** only in `main`, **0** of `main`'s rows
dropped; null control against the pre-merge branch side prints **8** and **5**.

**`updated-for:` is repointed to `0f0cfb8`**, the `origin/main` commit merged at this head, and
the row's own command re-run against it prints the one-line add. `docs/HANDOVER.md` stays at 406
of 406; every role cap, the floor and the corpus are flat.

**One decay the reviewer found and did not block on, recorded because it is the tree's own
instrument doing what this branch is remediating**: `policy_lint --record --since <ref>`
enumerates `<ref>..mainRef()` — a fixed start with a **moving** endpoint — so a quoted result
goes stale as soon as anyone merges. That is the same defect class as the one that blocked this
branch in round four, one artifact over.

## Mutation proof

**Re-executed at this head, not carried**, because the branch took a fourth
merge and `fixer.md` steps 2–4 re-execute after one. Both arms in this
worktree, `git status --porcelain` empty after each:

* **The cap.** One line appended to `docs/HANDOVER.md` (406 → 407), then `node
  .claude/workflows/policy_lint.mjs`: `ERROR [budgets] docs/HANDOVER.md: 407
  lines exceeds its cap of 406`, `TOTAL: 1 error(s)`, rc 0 → 1. Restored:
  `TOTAL: 0 error(s) across 36 policy file(s)`, rc 0. **Disclosed, because the
  body cites `--budgets` as the instrument elsewhere:** `--budgets` is a
  *reporter*, not the refusal. At 407 lines it prints `docs/HANDOVER.md 407 406`
  and still exits 0; the plain run is what refuses.
* **`updated-for:`.** This commit repoints it at `0f0cfb8`. Mutated to
  `45a16d3`, which `git merge-base --is-ancestor 45a16d3 HEAD` reports is not an
  ancestor, then `PYTHONPATH=$PWD/tests/hastub python3 tests/entities.py`:
  rc 0 → 1. Compared as **sets, not totals**: the mutated run's `FAIL` set is the
  unmutated run's plus exactly one — `FAIL and that commit is reachable from HEAD
  [updated-for: 45a16d3 is not an ancestor of HEAD]`. Disclosed, because it is
  the reason a set comparison is not enough on its own: one further `FAIL` line
  differs between the two runs, `a8:register_once`, whose `extra=[…]` list is
  that acceptance drive's own set iteration order and differs between two
  *unmutated* runs as well. `^updated-for:` occurs once in the file, checked
  before the edit, so the run that failed is the mutated one.

**The arm for a Delivery-status row is `policy_lint --record`, and this round
executed it rather than describing it.** At this head, with the branch updated
onto `0f0cfb8`: `node .claude/workflows/policy_lint.mjs --record --since
07bdc55` prints `TOTAL: 0 error(s) over 0 merged pull request(s)`, `CAPS: 0
stated cap(s) disagreeing`, `RENDER: 9 table(s), 137 row(s), 4 list(s), 45
item(s) across 2 disposition document(s)`, rc 0. The both-ends form of this arm
was executed in round four and is unchanged by this repair — the earlier account
of it is dropped rather than restated, because it named a merge this head no
longer sits on.

**That arm does not reach *this* row, and the negative result is stated rather
than hidden.** Deleting the `#719` row outright, and separately stripping its
list marker, leaves every `--record` figure identical — `RENDER: 9 table(s), 137
row(s), 4 list(s), 45 item(s)` in all three states — and rc 0, because
`checkRecord` iterates *merged* pull requests and #719 is not one yet. A row
written before the merge is unenforced until the merge it precedes. That is a
Friction line below, not a claim that the row is checked.

## Null control

Unmodified tree at this head, all rc 0:

* `PYTHONPATH=$PWD/tests/hastub GATE_SCOPE=auto GOLDEN_MODE=drift GOLDEN_REF=$(git merge-base origin/main HEAD) ./tests/run.sh`
  — `MODE: SCOPED -- 1 script(s) run, 20 scoped out.`, `ALL 1244 ENTITY CHECKS
  PASSED`, `3 TEST SCRIPT(S) PASSED`. **The mode line is the verdict, not the
  count** — this one reads SCOPED.
* `entities.py` — `ok exactly one handover, with no date in its name`, `ok the
  handover names the commit it reflects`, `ok and that commit is reachable from
  HEAD`.
* `policy_lint` — `TOTAL: 0 error(s) across 36 policy file(s)`, `KNOWN-BAD: 13 of
  13`, `FIXTURE ok: 72 error(s) hold 103 pins`.
* `policy_lint --budgets` — rc 0, `docs/HANDOVER.md 406 406`.
* `policy_lint --record --since 0f0cfb8` — `TOTAL: 0 error(s)`, `TABLES: 0
  split`, `CAPS: 0 stated cap(s) disagreeing`, `RENDER: … across 2 disposition
  document(s)`.
* `brief_lint.mjs`, `rules_sync.mjs --check` — clean.

**The update onto `main`, verified by whole-file comparison and not by reading
the conflict region.** `origin/main` moved again during this round, to `07bdc55`
(#733), under a fetch this seat did not run — worktrees share the repository's
refs, so another session's fetch moves `origin/main` here. This merge was a
clean auto-merge with no conflict.

**The proof is a command that names no SHA of its own**, which is the whole
repair: `diff <(git show "$(sed -n 's/^updated-for: //p' docs/HANDOVER.md):docs/plan-2026-09-open-issues.md") docs/plan-2026-09-open-issues.md`
reports `555a556` — one added line, this row, and nothing removed. It reads the
SHA out of the field it is checking, so it cannot quote a result for a different
commit than `updated-for:` names, which is exactly how round four's `claims`
block arose.

**Whole-file, with a null control, because the row I edited is not the file.**
Against `origin/main` as a line multiset: **1** line only in the resolution
(this row), **0** only in `main`, and **0** of `main`'s disposition rows
dropped. The identical comparison against the *pre-merge* branch side prints
**2** and **0**, so the zero above is a measurement rather than a blind
comparison.

**The merge left `docs/HANDOVER.md` untouched**, and the only handover change
this round is the one-token `updated-for:` repoint, which is line-neutral:
`--budgets` prints `docs/HANDOVER.md 406 406` at both ends and the `record` role
is flat at `~6865` against `6869`.

**The verdict set re-derived at this head, by the repository-wide sweep, 0 API
failures and 0 contaminated rows.** `gh api --paginate
'/repos/tvofi/heatpump_optimizer/issues/comments?per_page=100' --jq
'.[]|.html_url+"\t"+((.body//"")|split("\n")[0])'`, matched against `^Fix
review:` on the first-line field: `#686 ×1, #687 ×1, #689 ×1, #690 ×2, #708 ×1`.
Controls, all from that same fetch: **#531 carries no `revise`** — its `Fix
review:` first lines are `Fix review: blocked — …`, a non-parsing shape with no
SHA and no class, plus one bare `Fix review: merge`, so its absence is a fact
and not a miss; **a verdict class the repository has never used returns none**;
**#201 is reached**, which is the asymmetry the second sweep exists for; and
**#501 returns none from this endpoint**, which is the other one, its `Fix
review: merge` having been posted as a *review*. **The contamination control is
counted, not assumed**: `grep -ci 'rate limit\|API rate'` over the result file
returns 0, because a sweep that appends the response body on failure writes the
403 JSON into its own result — see Friction.

**The per-pull-request sweep is not re-run this round, and that is stated rather
than glossed.** Its subject is the comment corpus and not the tree, so a head
move does not re-date it; it was run whole in round three and reproduced by the
review at `1c17ec8`, including the GraphQL arm over every pull request's review
bodies. Re-running it here is three endpoints for every pull request in the
repository, sequentially, against a live secondary rate limit, for a corpus this
commit does not touch.

**The three marker arms**, re-run at this head, tree clean after each: no marker
→ `MODE: SCOPED`; `.seat-claim-probe` at the repository root → `MODE: FULL` /
`reason: no recorded closure mentions .seat-claim-probe`; the same marker under
`.claude/` → `MODE: SCOPED`. Keyed on the mode line alone, since the script
count is a figure the suite moves.

## Figures

Corpus totals over an open window are stated as enumerators, per #724; literals
appear only here.

* the verdict set and its span — the two sweep commands, quoted in full in the
  Delivery-status row. The set is a closed window and carries its literals:
  **#686 ×1, #687 ×1, #689 ×1, #690 ×2, #708 ×1**, between
  **2026-09-09T15:19:48Z** and **2026-09-10T06:33:11Z**
* **comment mutability, the finding in `## Forward-carry`** — enumerator
  `gh api --paginate '/repos/tvofi/heatpump_optimizer/issues/<n>/comments?per_page=100' --jq '.[]|[.id,.created_at,.updated_at,((.body//"")|split("\n")[0])]|@tsv'`
  over `n` in 686, 687, 689, 690, 708, 201, comparing the two timestamp fields.
  Its literals, this round, 0 API failures: **8 of 406 comments have `updated_at
  != created_at`, and 5 of the 53 `Fix review:` first lines in that sample were
  edited after posting.** The control that this does not weaken the set above:
  **all six `revise` comments have `updated_at == created_at`.**
* the merges the handover did not carry — the row states the enumerator and no
  number: `git log --format='%s' a6e95ff..HEAD | grep -cE '\(#[0-9]+\)$'`, its
  `record:`-excluding variant, and
  `node .claude/workflows/policy_lint.mjs --record --since a6e95ff`
* `docs/HANDOVER.md` against its cap —
  `node .claude/workflows/policy_lint.mjs --budgets` reports it and
  `node .claude/workflows/policy_lint.mjs` refuses on it
* the gate mode and the selected script —
  `GATE_SCOPE=auto GOLDEN_MODE=drift GOLDEN_REF=$(git merge-base origin/main HEAD) ./tests/run.sh`
* which rosters the citation linter reads — `node .claude/workflows/brief_lint.mjs`
* whether `nightly_ha.py` has a measured closure —
  `python3 -c "import json;print('tests/nightly_ha.py' in json.load(open('tests/closures.json'))['closures'])"`,
  which prints `False`
* the required contexts on `main-protect` —
  `gh api /repos/tvofi/heatpump_optimizer/rulesets/22628467 --jq '.rules[]|select(.type=="required_status_checks").parameters.required_status_checks[].context'`.
  **The literal count is removed rather than moved here, and that is a decision,
  not an oversight.** The review named it as a bare literal over an out-of-tree
  corpus with an open window and deliberately did not block, on the ground that
  the load-bearing claim is membership. That ground is right, and it decides the
  disposition: what `## Red checks` asserts is that `nightly-status` is absent
  from that set and that every context present in it is `success` bar a
  `skipped` `record`. A cardinal is not a term of either half — neither claim
  changes if the owner adds a nineteenth context — so the number is a figure
  carrying nothing, which `writing-for-agents.md` cuts rather than relocates.
  Moving it here would have kept a figure alive by giving it a command.

**#686, #687, #689, #690 ×2, #708 and the 2026-09-09/2026-09-10 span stay.**
They describe a closed historical window, which is the test every other corpus
total in this body failed — and `## Forward-carry` now records what that test
is worth.

**What the same test removed, from the row and the handover.** The corpus size
and the two enumeration totals; the pull-request count; #201's first-line count;
#531's line counts; the merge enumerations over `a6e95ff..HEAD`, where round one
printed one figure and round two a different one; the handover's remaining
headroom; the `MODE:` script counts, since `CLAUDE.md` rule 1 keys on the mode
line and not the count; `brief_lint`'s file count; and now the required-context
count. The literal outputs in `## Mutation proof` and `## Null control` are a
different thing — a run's own printout, dated by the head it ran at, which is
what a control is made of.

**#724 landed the rule this repair applies, while the repair was being written**,
and it is the root-cause seat's countermeasure for this same defect. It moves
*name the instrument, never the figure it prints* out of `docs/HANDOVER.md`'s own
paragraph into `writing-for-agents.md`'s criteria paragraph and extends it:
where the corpus is out of the tree and its window still open, the artifact
carries the **enumerator** — the command that, run alone, prints exactly that
number — and the literal goes only in `## Figures`; a count over a **closed**
window is carved out. This branch was already in that shape; it is now the rule
and not this seat's judgement. **One consequence was taken in round two:** the
handover's copy of the moved sentence became a restatement of policy the harness
loads on that path, so it is a pointer, keeping only what
`writing-for-agents.md` does not carry — the `coordinator_loc` measurement the
rule was written from. That re-flow was equal-line, and `--budgets` reads
`docs/HANDOVER.md 406 406` before and after.
* **The `updated-for:` mutation, re-executed at this head and compared as sets.**
  Unmutated `PYTHONPATH=$PWD/tests/hastub python3 tests/entities.py` — rc 0,
  `ALL 1252 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED`, **30** indented `FAIL` lines (fixture
  demonstrations that run in both arms, which is why a total is useless here).
  With `updated-for:` mutated to `45a16d3` — rc 1, `1 of 1252 ENTITY CHECKS
  FAILED`, **31** `FAIL` lines: the unmutated set plus exactly one, `FAIL and
  that commit is reachable from HEAD [updated-for: 45a16d3 is not an ancestor
  of HEAD …]`, and **none** lost. Enumerator:
  `grep -cE '^  FAIL ' <out>` — note the two leading spaces; a `^FAIL` pattern

nodes.body:
W4-G14 / S13: the #193 decomposition programme closes. Docs and roster only. W4-G13 (plan S12) was already a recorded halt — #637, `30a202e` — and its roster entry still read `pending`; W4-G10 read `pending` after #224 had closed. Claimed on #201 (comment 5623242735). Owner's decisions of 2026-09-10: close #193 in this pull request; drive to merge. The roster flip of W4-G14 itself to `done` follows in its own record pull request, because a `done` entry needs the squash SHA.

## Head

`15764159a6afe70448aaa016bda5e001b7195c40` on `claude/w4-g14-s13-closeout` — the second commit, which names this pull request in its own disposition row and puts W4-G14 at `in-review`; the first, `7c5ec0f`, carried everything else. Merge base `0f0cfb8e7a12fc5cb431ba36d5e0666a2b0e289b`, which is `origin/main` at writing. Three-dot against it touches `.claude/workflows/wave-4-groups.json`, `.claude/workflows/wave-5-groups.json`, `docs/HANDOVER.md`, `docs/audit-2026-09.md` and `docs/plan-2026-09-open-issues.md`.

## Mutation proof

The record is the deliverable, so each mutation removes or corrupts one field it carries. Each was applied in place, run, and restored — `git status --short` empty afterwards, and both detectors green again on the clean tree.

- **W4-G13 `resume.merge_sha` blanked** → `node .claude/workflows/check-wave-script.mjs` exit 1, `47 passed, 1 failed`, the line `miss   wave-4-groups.json W4-G13 at done: none of merge_sha`. Clean tree: exit 0, `48 passed, 0 failed`.
- **W5-G7's carry made to cite a symbol the tree lacks** (`learner_newton_step` → `learner_newton_stepp`) → `node .claude/workflows/brief_lint.mjs` exit 1 with two `[W5-G7] symbol:` errors. Clean tree: exit 0.
- **Not relied on, recorded so nobody reads the rule as covering it**: a bare literal count sentence appended to the same brief — "22 metrics in `tests/structure_budgets.json`" — did **not** fire the stale-count rule under that phrasing; the fixture that drives the rule uses another form.
- **The self-row, in a standalone clone** (never by repointing the shared `origin/main` under live worktrees): `git commit-tree` over this head's tree with the real `origin/main` (`0f0cfb8`) as parent and the squash subject `(#740)`, the clone's `refs/remotes/origin/main` pointed at it and the tree checked out, then `node .claude/workflows/policy_lint.mjs --record --since v6.3.20`:
  - simulated squash: `RECORD: 24 merged pull request(s) ... 0 without a disposition`, `TOTAL: 0 error(s)`.
  - null control A, the parent tree under the same subject: `1 without` → names #740, exit 1.
  - null control B, this head's tree with only the `- [#740](...)` row cut: **`0 without` — did not fire.** The check is satisfied by the two Delivery-status cells that also name #740 (the Wave 4 top-table cell and the W4-G14 row), so the row alone is not what dispositions this merge; the section text does. Recorded rather than dropped: a control that reports clean is worth nothing until it has reported a difference, which is control B'.
  - null control B', every `#740` mention cut from the plan (three, at lines 79, 252 and 501): `1 without` → names #740, exit 1.

## Null control

Unmodified tree at the merge base `0f0cfb8`: `python3 tests/structure.py` → `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`, identical rows at head, because nothing under `custom_components/` moves. `node .claude/workflows/policy_lint.mjs --record --since v6.3.20` → 0 without a disposition and 0 split tables at both ends. `node .claude/workflows/policy_lint.mjs --budgets` → `docs/HANDOVER.md` under its line cap at both ends; the file cap is the one that binds, and corpus and role caps are unmoved. Both claim files and `VERSION` / manifest byte-identical three-dot.

The re-survey measures the tree at the merge base and this branch does not change that tree; a rerun at head prints the same RESULT lines, which is the control that the survey is not measuring its own edits.

Scoped gate at head: `GATE_SCOPE=auto GOLDEN_MODE=drift GOLDEN_REF=0f0cfb8 ./tests/run.sh` → `MODE: SCOPED -- 1 script(s) run, 20 scoped out.` — `tests/entities.py`, selected by `docs/HANDOVER.md` — `ALL 1254 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED`, `claims hygiene: 0f0cfb8 ok`, summary `3 TEST SCRIPT(S) PASSED; 20 SCOPED OUT AND NOT RUN`, exit 0. `tests/stress.py` not selected, so no lease.

## Figures

- `docs/HANDOVER.md` at 405 lines against a cap of 406 — `node .claude/workflows/policy_lint.mjs --budgets`
- five commits to `coordinator.py` since #637's survey base — `git log --oneline 30a202e..0f0cfb8 -- custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/coordinator.py`
- `describe_setup` bound from `sensor.py` twice — `grep -rn "coordinator.describe_setup" custom_components/`
- the four zero-reference properties — `for p in last_optimization next_optimization current_action floor_return_temp; do grep -rn "\.$p\b" custom_components tests | wc -l; done` → `0 0 0 0`
- every RESULT line below — the re-survey script at the end of this section, run from the repository root at `0f0cfb8` (`python3 w4_g13_resurvey.py`):
  - `subsystem_named_classes=1` — `CoordinatorContext`
  - `module_funcs_taking_coordinator=19` — `away.py` 4, `boost.py` 7, `coordinator.py` 2, `diagnostics.py` 1, `sensor.py` 2, `setpoint_check.py` 2, `wood_fuel.py` 1
  - `delegate_shaped_methods=1` — `describe_setup->topology.describe_setup`
  - `properties=13 hub_descriptors=4`, `zero_reference_properties=4`
  - `coordinator_methods=251 unbound_methods=0`
  - `instance_attrs_assigned=175 write_only_by_ast=10 write_only_after_control=3` — `_dhw_draws_dirty`, `_last_energy_sample`, `_last_manual_setpoint`; the control column caught `_unsub_defrost`, `_unsub_ecl110_state`, `_unsub_peak_guard` and `_slab_temp_initialized` at one string literal each, read by name
- the mutation figures — the two commands named in Mutation proof

The re-survey script, verbatim:

```python
"""W4-G13 re-survey at a merge base. Run from the repository root; prints RESULT lines.

Rules, so every number is re-derivable:
  subsystem class    = ast.ClassDef in custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/*.py whose name
                       matches subsystem|seam|facade|delegate|context (case-insensitive)
  coordinator-taking = module-level def whose FIRST parameter is named coord/coordinator or is
                       annotated with a name containing "Coordinator"
  delegate-shaped    = coordinator method whose body after the docstring is ONE Return/Expr whose
                       call is <module>.<fn> with <module> a package module name
  property refs      = occurrences of ".<name>" (word-bounded) in production (definition excluded)
                       and in tests/*.py
  unbound method     = coordinator method with ZERO word-bounded occurrences of its bare name in
                       production beyond its own def (HA-convention lifecycle names excluded)
  write-only attr    = self.<attr> Stored inside the class and never Loaded inside it; the CONTROL
                       column counts the attr name as a STRING LITERAL in coordinator.py, which is
                       how a by-name loop or hasattr() reads it invisibly to an AST Load walk
"""
import ast, re, pathlib, collections
ROOT = pathlib.Path('.')
PKG = ROOT / 'custom_components/heatpump_optimizer'
prod = {p: p.read_text() for p in sorted(PKG.rglob('*.py'))}
tests = {p: p.read_text() for p in sorted((ROOT / 'tests').glob('*.py'))}
src = prod[PKG / 'coordinator.py']
tree = ast.parse(src)
coord = next(n for n in tree.body if isinstance(n, ast.ClassDef) and n.name == 'HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator')
methods = [n for n in coord.body if isinstance(n, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef))]
mods = {p.stem for p in prod}

named = [(p.name, n.name) for p, t in prod.items() for n in ast.walk(ast.parse(t))
         if isinstance(n, ast.ClassDef) and re.search(r'subsystem|seam|facade|delegate|context', n.name, re.I)]
print('RESULT subsystem_named_classes=%d %s' % (len(named), named))

taking = collections.Counter()
for p, t in prod.items():
    for n in ast.parse(t).body:
        if isinstance(n, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)) and n.args.args:
            a = n.args.args[0]
            ann = ast.unparse(a.annotation) if a.annotation else ''
            if a.arg in ('coord', 'coordinator') or 'Coordinator' in ann:
                taking[p.name] += 1
print('RESULT module_funcs_taking_coordinator=%d %s' % (sum(taking.values()), dict(taking)))

deleg = []
for m in methods:
    body = [s for s in m.body if not (isinstance(s, ast.Expr) and isinstance(s.value, ast.Constant))]
    if len(body) == 1:
        v = getattr(body[0], 'value', None)
        if isinstance(v, ast.Await):
            v = v.value
        if (isinstance(v, ast.Call) and isinstance(v.func, ast.Attribute)
                and isinstance(v.func.value, ast.Name) and v.func.value.id in mods):
            deleg.append('%s->%s.%s' % (m.name, v.func.value.id, v.func.attr))
print('RESULT delegate_shaped_methods=%d %s' % (len(deleg), deleg))

def dotrefs(name):
    pat = re.compile(r'\.' + re.escape(name) + r'\b')
    return (sum(len(pat.findall(t)) for t in prod.values()), sum(len(pat.findall(t)) for t in tests.values()))

props = [m.name for m in methods if any(isinstance(d, ast.Name) and d.id == 'property' for d in m.decorator_list)]
hubs = [t.targets[0].id for t in coord.body if isinstance(t, ast.Assign) and isinstance(t.value, ast.Call)
        and getattr(t.value.func, 'id', '') == '_hub']
print('RESULT properties=%d hub_descriptors=%d' % (len(props), len(hubs)))
zero = []
for name in props + hubs:
    pn, tn = dotrefs(name)
    print('  refs %-30s prod=%-4d tests=%d' % (name, pn, tn))
    if pn == 0 and tn == 0:
        zero.append(name)
print('RESULT zero_reference_properties=%d %s' % (len(zero), zero))

HA = {'__init__', '_async_update_data', 'async_shutdown', 'async_config_entry_first_refresh', '_async_setup'}
unbound = []
for m in methods:
    pat = re.compile(r'(?<![A-Za-z0-9_])' + re.escape(m.name) + r'(?![A-Za-z0-9_])')
    n = sum(len(pat.findall(t)) for t in prod.values()) - len(re.findall(r'def ' + re.escape(m.name) + r'\(', src))
    if n == 0 and m.name not in HA:
        unbound.append(m.name)
print('RESULT coordinator_methods=%d unbound_methods=%d %s' % (len(methods), len(unbound), unbound))

stored, loaded = collections.Counter(), collections.Counter()
for m in methods:
    for n in ast.walk(m):
        if isinstance(n, ast.Attribute) and isinstance(n.value, ast.Name) and n.value.id == 'self':
            (stored if isinstance(n.ctx, ast.Store) else loaded)[n.attr] += 1
wo = sorted(a for a in stored if loaded[a] == 0)
real = []
for a in wo:
    other_prod = sum(len(re.findall(r'\.' + re.escape(a) + r'\b', t)) for p, t in prod.items() if p.name != 'coordinator.py')
    tst = sum(len(re.findall(r'\.' + re.escape(a) + r'\b', t)) for t in tests.values())
    by_name = len(re.findall(r'["\']' + re.escape(a) + r'["\']', src))
    print('  write-only %-24s other_prod=%-3d tests=%-3d CONTROL string_literal_in_coordinator=%d' % (a, other_prod, tst, by_name))
    if other_prod == 0 and tst == 0 and by_name == 0:
        real.append(a)
print('RESULT instance_attrs_assigned=%d write_only_by_ast=%d write_only_after_control=%d %s' % (len(stored), len(wo), len(real), real))
```

## Red checks

nodes.title: fix: the nightly lane's abort was async_shutdown cancelling the task that had merely driven a refresh
nodes.body:
The nightly real-Home-Assistant lane has aborted inside `_async_check_a5_options`
since it started reaching Home Assistant again, and the cause is production code,
not the harness. `HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator._async_update_data` records
`asyncio.current_task()` as the handle `async_shutdown` cancels (#237) and never
drops it. On the inline path — `await coordinator.async_refresh()` — that task is
the **caller's**, not one the coordinator created, so the entry's next unload
cancels whatever the caller has gone on to do. The lane's driver drove a refresh,
the A5 options save reloaded the entry, and the driver's own `asyncio.run` main
task was cancelled at its next suspension point, `hass.async_block_till_done()`,
before `_emit`. No result marker reached the host, so every declared
container-side check was reported as never-run — including the ones that had
printed `ok` on the container's own stdout.

The handle is now recorded only for a solving refresh and dropped in a `finally`.
A refresh that has **finished** cancels nothing; a refresh still **in flight** is
cancelled exactly as #237 requires. The setup-time light refresh, which runs in
the config-entry setup task and never solves, records no handle at all.

**This does not make the lane green, and no tranche should read it that way.**
Three causes were carried into the #533 rows and this branch fixes one of them:
`log:no_integration_traceback` still counts the A4 tranche's own injected fault,
`log:blocking_positive_control` still sees nothing inside its probe window, and
`a3:roster` still has no independent baseline.

### Which side initiated the cancellation, and how that was established

The previous seat offered the reload-in-flight reading and labelled it a reading.
It is not adopted here; four legs establish the initiator instead.

1. **Home Assistant's own gate says a real `Task.cancel()` happened.**
   `config_entries.py` logs `Setup of config entry '%s' for %s integration
   cancelled` only inside `except asyncio.CancelledError:` and only when
   `asyncio.current_task().cancelling() > 0`. The container log carries that
   message. The two Home Assistant frames in the container's traceback
   (`config_entries.py` `result = await component.async_setup_entry(hass, self)`
   and `core.py` `await asyncio.sleep(0)` at the head of `async_block_till_done`)
   resolve to those exact lines in the 2026.9.1 wheel, so the source read is the
   source that ran.
2. **The cancellation carries no message.** Both tracebacks in that job print a
   bare `asyncio.exceptions.CancelledError`. In the four modules on this
   traceback's path every `.cancel(` passes a message. The message-less
   `.cancel()` sites in the rest of `homeassistant/`, `homeassistant/helpers/`
   and `homeassistant/util/` — the scope searched, not the whole distribution —
   each cancel a timer, a warn task or a progress task the same object created,
   so none of them can reach a caller's task.
3. **The one message-less `.cancel()` reachable is ours**, and its handle is the
   caller's task.
4. **Reproduced without a container, and it is the same shape.** A caller drives
   a refresh to completion, parks on a gate, and the entry unloads: on the
   unmodified tree the caller is cancelled and never resumes.

The reload's own setup task dying too is `asyncio.run`'s shutdown cancelling the
loop's remaining tasks once the main task is gone — which is why Home Assistant's
setup-cancelled record carries the driver's traceback as its context and lands
immediately before the driver's own uncaught exception. That is the reading, and
it is not load-bearing: legs 1–4 stand without it.

## Head

`3fcf3b5822e9f0d782ce98acdecf4a70fbf2924f`

**Merge resolution at `65dbba8c`, by the orchestrator.** `main` moved several times and
the other lane truthed nineteen rows this branch's copy still called pending.
Resolved per row against the **merge base**, not per side: where only `main`
changed a row I took `main`'s; where only this branch changed one I kept it.

**Four rows both sides changed, and taking either wholesale would have lost
something.** `main` truthed #584, #585, #587 and #588 to `CLOSED`, shortening each
and ending it *"#533 still carries the abort precondition"* — a sentence this pull
request makes **false**. This branch had appended the discharge to the older, longer
text `main` had just replaced. Neither side's row was right: the substance was
merged into `main`'s truthed text, so each now records that the abort precondition
is discharged here and that **the rest of it stands** — the lane still discards a
container's results on any abort, one check counts the A4 tranche's own injected
fault, the positive control sees nothing in its probe window, and the roster check
has no independent baseline.

Verified by whole-file multiset against `main`: **5 lines absent, 5 added, zero
duplicated** — the #533 row and those four. Null control: the same comparison
against the unresolved side reports 29 absent, so the check discriminates.

**The head moved because the review blocked this on `conflict`, and the block was right.**
`git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main 65dbba8c` exited 1 on `coordinator.py` — GitHub's
`mergeable` field read `unknown` on three polls, so the reviewer measured it rather than
reading it off the status. `main`'s #733 **replaced** the line `# Apply current action to
heat pump` with the production call `boost.apply(self)`; this branch had **deleted** that same
line as one of its two ratchet payments. One position, both sides changed — so it had to be
merged by hand, and either side taken whole loses something real: *ours* silently drops the
boost switches, *theirs* hands back a line the payment was made from. No conflict marker would
have survived a squash and no test would have failed.

**Resolved by keeping `boost.apply(self)`.** The comment is gone on both sides regardless, so
nothing of #733's is lost. Verified whole-file rather than at the hunk: `diff` of the resolved
`coordinator.py` against `origin/main` shows **only** this branch's own #533 change — the moved
assignment, the `finally` that drops the handle, the docstring — and `grep -c 'boost.apply(self)'`
is **1**.

**The resolution cost the ratchet payment, and that is stated rather than absorbed.** #733 had
already removed the line this branch was paid for, so `coordinator_loc` came out at **10000**
against a budget of **9999**. Paid again by cutting `# Update current state from sensors`, a
comment that restates the call on the line below it — the same class of line as the one #733
took, so the payment is like-for-like. **No budget raise and no re-record.** `STRUCTURE RATCHET
PASSED`; `cross_seam_fraction` unmoved at `0.4337`, which is a tolerance metric and is never
re-recorded.

## Mutation proof

Two production changes, two mutations, each answered by exactly one check.

- Delete `finally: self._refresh_task = None` from `_async_update_data`:
  `and a refresh that already FINISHED leaves no handle behind, so the task that
  drove it survives the unload (#533)` goes red in `tests/features.py`, with
  `caller survived=False, cancelled=True, handle kept past the refresh=True`.
  Nothing else moves.
- Move `self._refresh_task = asyncio.current_task()` back above the
  `_skip_solve_once` early return: `and the setup-time light refresh — which runs
  in the SETUP task and never solves — records no handle at all (#533)` goes red,
  same detail string. Nothing else moves.

Both restored byte-identically — `cmp` against `git show HEAD:…coordinator.py` is silent and
`git status --porcelain` is empty after each — and the script is green again at the head above:
`ALL 2129 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED`. **Re-executed after the merge**, as `fixer.md` steps 2–4
require; the count moved from 2123 to 2129 because `main` added six checks, not this branch.

**One failure appeared that was not the mutation, and it is named rather than dropped.** The
first run of mutation 1 printed a second red — `the reap Home Assistant's stop fires keeps the
loop running (#525)`, with `fixed 0 ticks in 0.00s vs blocking 0 ticks in 2.00s`. That is a
wall-clock check, and this machine was running several seats at the time. Re-run alone from the
committed tree, mutation 1 prints **`1 of 2129 FEATURE CHECKS FAILED`** and the only red is the
#533 check. So it did not reproduce and I am recording it as load rather than as an effect of
the mutation — but it appeared once, on a timing check, and a seat that sees it again should
suspect the harness before the fix.

## Null control

- **The fix is not "stop cancelling".** The paired #237 check `async_shutdown
  cancels the in-flight refresh rather than trusting the base class to have done
  it` is green on this head. Had the cancellation been removed to make the new
  checks pass, that one would be the check that went red.
- **The unmodified tree fails the new checks**, with the detail strings quoted
  under Mutation proof — that is the arm that separates the defect from its fix,
  and it is the same discrimination the container produced.
- **I could not run the container.** There is no Docker on this machine and
  `nightly-ha` does not run on pull requests, so the end-to-end claim — that the
  lane now walks past `_async_check_a5_options` — is **not** measured here. It is
  substituted by the in-process reproduction above, which pins the property (a
  finished refresh's task survives an unload) rather than the instance (the
  driver's task surviving A5). Saying which of the two was measured is the point
  of this paragraph.
- **The container-side evidence is read, not produced.** Every figure about the
  lane below comes from a named job log, not from a run of mine.

## Figures

- `28` — declared container-side checks that printed `ok` inside the container
  and were reported to the host as never-run, in the last `nightly-ha (stable)`
  job that reached Home Assistant. Enumerator (job `102803274073`, run
  `34456269514`):

      gh run view --repo tvofi/heatpump_optimizer --job 102803274073 --log \
      | awk -F'\t' '{ $1=""; $2=""; sub(/^[ \t]*[0-9T:.Z-]+ /,"",$0); print }' \
      | awk '/--- inside the container ---/{i=1;next} i && $1=="ok" {print $2}' \
      | sort -u > /tmp/ok.txt
      python3 -c "import importlib.util as u;s=u.spec_from_file_location('n','tests/nightly_ha.py');m=u.module_from_spec(s);s.loader.exec_module(m);d=set();[d.update([x] if isinstance(x,str) else x) for x in m.INSIDE_CHECKS];print(len(d & set(open('/tmp/ok.txt').read().split())))"

- `1` — `.cancel(` call sites in this package. Enumerator:
  `git grep -n "\.cancel(" -- custom_components/`
- `6` — `.cancel(` call sites in the four Home Assistant modules on the
  traceback's path, all of them passing a cancel message. Enumerator:

      pip download homeassistant==2026.9.1 --no-deps --ignore-requires-python -d "$D"
      python3 -c "import zipfile;zipfile.ZipFile('$D/homeassistant-2026.9.1-py3-none-any.whl').extractall('$D/ha')"
      grep -rn "\.cancel(" "$D"/ha/homeassistant/{core.py,config_entries.py,runner.py,util/timeout.py} \
      | grep -v "handle.cancel()\|_timeout_handler.cancel()\|self\._cancel"

- **Structural cost: none.** `python3 tests/structure.py` reports the ratchet
  passing at this head with no metric moved. `coordinator_loc` and
  `max_class_loc` sit at zero headroom, so the two lines the `finally` costs were
  paid inside the same class — a comment that restated the call beneath it, and a
  blank line — rather than re-recorded or raised. Read the metric off the script,
  not off this sentence.
- **Gate scope:** `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff $(git merge-base
  origin/main HEAD) --workdir "$D"` prints `MODE: SCOPED`, and every script
  `scope.run` names is green locally at this head, `tests/golden.py` under
  `GOLDEN_MODE=drift` against the merge base. `tests/stress.py` is not selected,
  so no gate lease was taken.

## Red checks

`nightly-status` is red here, and the rule rather than a run list: #713's check
reports the verdict of the last **concluded scheduled** `nightly-ha` run, which
attaches to whatever commit was `main`'s head when cron fired. No pull request
can change that verdict — only a merge and the next schedule can — so a red
`nightly-status` on a branch is a report about `main`'s last night, not a finding
about the branch's head. It is not one of `main-protect`'s required contexts.
Read the run the check names before treating it as this branch's defect.

The root-cause question it would otherwise trigger is answered by the same
reading: the cheaper detector for **this** defect is the one this pull request
adds — an in-process check that a finished refresh leaves no handle behind, which
runs in the seconds-long PR gate and needs neither Docker nor a schedule. Its
standing cost is two checks in `tests/features.py`. The defect reached a lane
that no pull request enters, which is exactly the gap #713 was built for; it
needs no second countermeasure here.

Any other check that goes red on this head is answered by naming it and the
cheaper detector, in this section. An enumeration written before the branch is
pushed would be falsified by the edit that writes it.

## Forward-carry

`docs/plan-2026-09-open-issues.md` — the **#533** row, which is the stage brief
these tranches actually read. It now carries the cause and the control in place
of the reading it offered, and it carries the finding this branch does **not**
fix: `_inside` reaches `_emit` only on the happy path and `_merge_completed`
returns the first container's result unchanged when it carries other than one
marker, so a future abort again reports every declared container-side check as
never-run whatever it printed. The precondition, not the opportunity: read the
`--- inside the container ---` block of the job log, never the host's roster, to
tell a check that failed from one that never ran.

The same file's **#584**, **#585**, **#587** and **#588** rows each inherited the
abort precondition and each now says it is discharged and that the rest of theirs
is not — so a seat reading one of those rows alone cannot read a green lane into
it.

## Friction

`ratchet-budgets.md`: cost: `coordinator_loc` and `max_class_loc` are both at
zero headroom, so a two-line `finally` had to be paid for by deleting a comment
and a blank line elsewhere in the same class. The payment
is honest and the rule worked as designed; the friction is that the cheapest
thing to delete is prose, which is the opposite of what this repository wants
deleted.

Fix review: blocked 65dbba8c0cd47fde6f9cd8d90e4fc16b3a7a5346 conflict: coordinator.py conflicts with origin/main 07bdc557 — the branch deletes the line #733 replaced with `boost.apply(self)`

First adversarial review. Reviewed from a locked detached worktree at `65dbba8c`, restored clean after every mutation. **Every measurement below passed.** The block is contract step 13 alone, and the substance of the fix is not in question.

---

## The block: a real, measured conflict on a production path

```
$ git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main 65dbba8c0cd47fde6f9cd8d90e4fc16b3a7a5346
EXIT=1
CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/coordinator.py
Auto-merging docs/plan-2026-09-open-issues.md
Auto-merging tests/features.py
```

The `claimnotes` driver was already installed (`MERGE-CLAIM: already-installed`); stderr carried **no** `MERGE-CLAIM:` line, because neither claim file is in the conflict — both are byte-identical to the merge base on this branch. So the path is not one of the two step 13 disposes of, and this is not GitHub's status field: `mergeable` reads `null / unknown` on three consecutive polls, which is why it was measured rather than read.

The conflicting hunk, `--diff3`:

```
<<<<<<< 65dbba8c
||||||| merge-base 36c649d
            # Apply current action to heat pump
=======
            boost.apply(self)
>>>>>>> origin/main
            await self._apply_action()
```

This is the shape that costs the most to resolve wrong. The branch **deleted** that comment as one of the two lines it paid the `coordinator_loc` / `max_class_loc` ratchet with; `main` **replaced the same line** with a production call, `boost.apply(self)`, landed by #733 (`07bdc55`). Resolving "ours" silently drops the two-hour boost switches from every cycle — no conflict marker left behind, no obviously failing test. Resolving "theirs" keeps `boost.apply(self)` and gives back the deleted line, which is one of the two the ratchet payment was made from.

I cannot verify a merged tree that does not exist yet, so per step 13 this is mine to block on. Two things to re-take after the resolution, because both were measured on a tree that will not be what merges:

- **`tests/structure.py`.** It passes here with every metric `ok` (`STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`), but `main` has itself cut 6 net lines from `coordinator.py` since the merge base, so the headroom the payment was sized against has moved. Re-run at the resolved head.
- **`tests/features.py`.** The merged `_async_update_data` will contain `boost.apply(self)` inside the `try:` the new `finally:` now closes. Nothing I ran exercised that combination.

Nothing else in this review is a reason to withhold `merge`.

---

## 1. Mutation proof — reproduced exactly, not vacuous

Head, before touching anything: `ALL 2123 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED`, exit 0.

**M1 — delete `finally: self._refresh_task = None` from `_async_update_data`:**

```
1 of 2123 FEATURE CHECKS FAILED
FAIL and a refresh that already FINISHED leaves no handle behind, so the task that drove it
     survives the unload (#533)
     [caller survived=False, cancelled=True, handle kept past the refresh=True]
```

Exactly one check, exactly the one the body names, exactly the detail string the body quotes. Restored: `git diff --stat` empty.

**M2 — move `self._refresh_task = asyncio.current_task()` back above the `_skip_solve_once` early return:**

```
1 of 2123 FEATURE CHECKS FAILED
FAIL and the setup-time light refresh -- which runs in the SETUP task and never solves --
     records no handle at all (#533)
     [caller survived=False, cancelled=True, handle kept past the refresh=True]
```

Everything above was measured with the fixer's own in-process checks in `tests/features.py`. Per contract step 9 that is theirs, not the finder's, and the body says so. I also built **my own probe** (below) to attack the other configurations; it is mine, not the finder's either.

## 4. Other configurations — differential, pre-fix vs head

My probe, appended to `tests/features.py` in the worktree and removed afterwards (tree verified clean). Pre-fix column is the merge-base production shape, reconstructed by applying M1 and M2 together and diff-checked against `36c649d`'s file.

| configuration | pre-fix | head `65dbba8c` |
|---|---|---|
| refresh completed, then unload | handle = the **caller's** task | `None` |
| setup-time light refresh (zero-evidence install) | handle = the **caller's** task | `None` |
| refresh raised before the solve | handle = the **caller's** task | `None` |
| `async_shutdown` with no refresh ever | `None`, latch set | `None`, latch set |
| `async_shutdown` twice | ok | ok |
| two overlapping refreshes, B finishes while A still solves | handle = **B** (a finished task); A not cancelled | handle = `None`; A not cancelled |

The first three rows are the defect and it is closed on all of them, including the two the body claims but does not have a check for (the raising path is covered by the `finally` and nothing pins it).

The last row is a **residual, not a regression**: an in-flight refresh loses its cancellation handle the moment a second refresh overlaps it, and it did before this branch too — pre-fix the handle was a *finished* task, so `refresh.cancel()` was a no-op either way and A survived in both trees. `_entry_released` was `True` in both, which is what actually stops the actuation. Worth one sentence in the #237 row; not a blocker and not this PR's to fix.

The body claims a cancellation-**ordering** defect, not a race, and does not claim any interleaving impossible — correctly, in my reading. The test parks the caller on an `asyncio.Event` the shutdown does not touch, so the ordering is deterministic rather than lucky. One limit worth stating: `tests/hastub`'s `DataUpdateCoordinator.async_refresh` does not call `_async_update_data` at all, so the test drives `_async_update_data` directly and the inline path is *modelled* by hand. That is a fair model of real HA's `_async_refresh`, but nothing in this suite pins it, and the container lane is the only thing that would.

## 6. The #525 disclosure — it did not reproduce, and I could not confirm the attribution either

Asked to test it, so both halves are reported.

**Your account is not refuted and I am not endorsing it.** I have no red to explain, so I cannot distinguish the two. nodes.title: feat: two-hour DHW and space-heat boost switches
nodes.body:
`switch.heat_pump_optimizer_boost_dhw` and `switch.heat_pump_optimizer_boost_space` each apply maximum heat on that channel for two hours. Space matches the global boost action (nameplate electrical power, comfort ceiling, full ECL displace). DHW matches the planner's own hot-water ceiling (80 % of nameplate) and turns the pump on. The channels are independent and do not call `async_set_mode`, so they do not stomp comfort or economy.

State lives in `boost.py`: a Store next to the away override, and a weak map keyed by coordinator so the class does not grow an attribute or a method. Away and boost restore share one spawn. The overlay runs immediately before `_apply_action`. The lookup is `held_for`, not `state`: `tests/features.py` already has eleven top-level `state =` assignments, and `no-copies` treats that name as a reimplementation.

Merged `a94bbaf` (#734). `coordinator_loc` and `max_class_loc` 10005 → 9999, recorded with this change: the overlay left the class and the score change came with the merge. Inherited #734 score claims dropped; this branch moves no goldens. leaves #201 open.
