nodes.title: record: #734 merged without a row and main went red
nodes.body:
`main` went red on `record` at 15:53:48Z, six seconds after #734 merged without a
disposition row. `checkRecord` enumerates **every** merge on `main` regardless of
who opened it, so a merge nobody recorded reddens the required check for both lanes
and every subsequent merge inherits it.

Neither open pull request in that lane writes the row, so this one does. Outside
#201; the row says so.

## Head

`a0b9470524294a9192ed4ad4050bbd30660d654c`

## Mutation proof

The row is the deliverable, so the mutation is its absence.

**Corrected after review, because the arm this section first carried was vacuous.**
It ran the check at the *branch head*, where the merge has not happened and the
window therefore does not contain this pull request at all. That arm prints the
same figure whether or not the self-row exists, so it evidenced the #734 row and
evidenced nothing about the second row this branch exists to add. The review
(`5621955377`) reproduced that and it is the second instance of the class on a
record branch today. The real arm simulates the merge — `git commit-tree` over
this head's tree with `origin/main` as parent, `refs/remotes/origin/main`
repointed **and the tree checked out**, because the check reads the working tree:

```
live main (the red):        RECORD: 18 merged pull request(s) in v6.3.20..origin/main;
                            1 without a disposition ... for merged pull request #734
                            TOTAL: 1 error(s)                                exit 1
simulated merge:            RECORD: 19 merged pull request(s); 0 without a disposition
                            TOTAL: 0 error(s)                                exit 0
null control A, parent tree: RECORD: 19 merged; 2 without  -> names #737 and #734
null control B, self-row cut: RECORD: 19 merged; 1 without  -> names #737
```

Nineteen, not eighteen: the simulated window contains this pull request, which is
what makes the self-row testable. Both null controls fire, so the zero is a
measurement. Control B is the one that pins the self-row specifically — cut that
one line and the check names this pull request.

## Null control

`main` itself at `a94bbaf` is the control arm, and it is failing in CI now
(check-run 102943398074). It is not a constructed negative: the same command over
the same window differs only by this one line.

## Figures

```
node .claude/workflows/policy_lint.mjs --record --since v6.3.20
node .claude/workflows/policy_lint.mjs
```

Three-dot against the merge base: one file, two insertions, zero deletions -- #734's row and this pull request's own. Both
claim files byte-identical to `origin/main`. `VERSION`, the manifest version and
the `RELEASE_NOTES.md` heading untouched.

## Red checks

`main` is red on `record` and **that is the defect this fixes**, not a red on this
branch. On this branch: a red `pr-contract` at an outgoing commit is the S10
ordering arm working; a red at the head this body names is the arm broken. Re-derive
rather than reading a count here — a run list written in this section is falsified by
the edit that writes it.

`nightly-status` will be red: it is #713's check reporting a genuinely failed
nightly, is not one of the eighteen required contexts, and is named rather than fixed.

## Forward-carry

none. The row is itself the record instrument for the merge it describes.

## Friction

- `delivery-status-tracking`: unenforced: the rule says every merge needs a disposition, and `checkRecord` enforces it **after** the merge, on `main`, where the cost lands on whoever merges next rather than on the branch that skipped it. Measured here: #734 merged at 15:53:42Z and `main` was red six seconds later, from a lane that had two open pull requests neither of which carried the row.

leaves #201 open.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Fix review: merge a0b9470524294a9192ed4ad4050bbd30660d654c

Reviewed from a detached, `git worktree lock`ed worktree at `a0b9470`, in a private `mktemp -d`. Head unchanged at posting time; `origin/main` still `a94bbaf` (re-fetched after the last measurement). API refusals: **0** over every `gh api` call in this review (paginated `check-runs?filter=all`, `pulls/*/files` for all 11 other open PRs, rulesets).

## 1. The merge simulation, and it is a real one

`origin/main` repointed **in an isolated clone** and the tree **checked out**, merge commit built with `commit-tree`:

```
SIM = commit-tree <a0b9470 tree> -p a94bbaf -m 'record: #734 merged without a row and main went red (#737)'
    = d6081aebdf5040f3a5857a04bd06ef0ef5fc8e2e
git update-ref refs/remotes/origin/main d6081ae && git checkout --detach d6081ae
HEAD^{tree} == a0b9470^{tree}   (verified)

$ node .claude/workflows/policy_lint.mjs --record --since v6.3.20
RECORD_ENUM: subject (GITHUB_TOKEN is not set)
RECORD: 19 merged pull request(s) in v6.3.20..origin/main; 0 without a disposition in docs/plan-2026-09-open-issues.md or docs/HANDOVER.md
TABLES: 0 split table(s) ... CAPS: 0 ... RENDER: 9 table(s), 137 row(s)
TOTAL: 0 error(s) over 19 merged pull request(s)          EXIT=0
```

Nineteen, not eighteen: the window now contains this pull request, so the run **does** exercise the self-row.

## 2. Null controls — three arms, all fire

**Live arm, `main` as it stands** (same isolated clone, `origin/main` = `a94bbaf`):

```
RECORD: 18 merged pull request(s) in v6.3.20..origin/main; 1 without a disposition
ERROR [record] ... for merged pull request #734 (fix: overall score is driving, not the house grade (#734))
TOTAL: 1 error(s) over 18 merged pull request(s)          EXIT=1
```

**Null control A — same simulation, parent tree (no rows):**

```
RECORD: 19 merged pull request(s); 2 without a disposition
ERROR ... for merged pull request #737
ERROR ... for merged pull request #734
TOTAL: 2 error(s) over 19 merged pull request(s)
```

**Null control B — same simulation over commit 1 only (`bb91228`, the #734 row, self-row deleted):**

```
RECORD: 19 merged pull request(s); 1 without a disposition
ERROR ... for merged pull request #737
TOTAL: 1 error(s) over 19 merged pull request(s)
```

So the self-row (§2 of the dispatch) is present **and load-bearing**: deleting it reddens `record` on this pull request's own merge. Both rows are inside `## Delivery status` (the `### The UX programme` heading below them is `###`, which `recordRegion`'s `^##\s` does not close on — there is a self-test for exactly that).

## 3. The one thing wrong here, named rather than waved past

The body's `## Mutation proof` positive arm is the **branch-head arm**, and I reproduced it exactly:

```
origin/main = a94bbaf (NOT repointed), HEAD = a0b9470
RECORD: 18 merged pull request(s); 0 without a disposition
TOTAL: 0 error(s) over 18 merged pull request(s)
```

Eighteen. That run measures a history this branch is not in, and it **cannot see #737** — it prints the identical figure under null control B, where the self-row has been deleted. So as written, the body's positive arm evidences the #734 row and evidences nothing at all about the self-row that the second commit exists to add. The negative arm (`main`, 18/1) is a real measurement and reproduces.

Not blocking, because the deliverable itself verifies green under a proper simulation with two null controls that both fire — but the evidence in the body is the vacuous arm, on a record branch, on the day that vacuity was already caught once. The figures should read 19/0, and this is the second instance of the class.

## 4. Both rows against source, not against the summary

**#734's row** — checked against #734's body and its diff at `a94bbaf`, not against this body:

| claim in the row | source |
|---|---|
| merged `a94bbaf` | `mergeCommit.oid = a94bbaf1a2e…`, `mergedAt 2026-09-10T15:53:42Z` |
| overall was the mean of whichever of envelope/machine/operation existed | diff: `available = [s for s in (envelope, machine, operation) if s is not None]` → `(machine, operation)` |
| fresh install has neither machine nor operation evidence, so overall *was* envelope | code: envelope needs only `_thermal_params`; machine needs `COP_BASELINE_MIN_SAMPLES` samples; operation needs a day book. The five `coord_*` goldens go `"overall": 58.3` → `null` in the same commit |
| ~5 for a ~24 h house | `clip((τ_h−20)/80,0,1)×100`, τ_h=24 → 5.0. Re-derived |
| operation skipped any day under 1 kWh | diff: `if kwh < 1.0` → `if kwh < 0.2` |
| overall now mean of machine and operation; envelope stays in the breakdown | diff + docstring rewrite |
| **"Row written after the merge, not before"** | **present, in bold, in the row.** `delivery-status-tracking.md` sanctions exactly this shape ("the same session **or an immediate record PR**"), so the row is honest about the one departure and the departure is inside the rule |
| outside #201 | no `wave-*-groups.json` names 734; the plan names no `#65`; #734's body says "leaves #201 open" |

The row omits #734's new 0.2 kWh floor, "no driving evidence leaves overall unset", the claimed goldens and the `10006 → 10005` budget re-record. Summary, not omission of anything that changes the reading.

**Figure I could not take at face value:** the row's "`record` went red on `main` at 15:53:48Z" is the check-run's `started_at`. It **concluded** `failure` at `15:54:32Z`. Same for the body's "red six seconds later" — six seconds is merge→start; merge→red is fifty. Check-run `102943398074` — the id the body cites — confirmed by direct read: `name=record conclusion=failure head_sha=a94bbaf1… started=2026-09-10T15:53:48Z completed=2026-09-10T15:54:32Z`.

**#737's row** is accurate and matches what I measured in §2.

## 5. Whole-file comparison, not the diff

`git show origin/main:docs/plan-2026-09-open-issues.md` vs `git show HEAD:…`, compared as whole files:

```
1525 lines (main) → 1527 lines (head)
diff -u0: @@ -621,0 +622,2 @@   two '+' lines, zero '-' lines
```

Nothing of another lane's dropped. Independently: `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main a0b9470` exits **0**, no `MERGE-CLAIM` marker (driver installed first), and the merged tree is `9771e074…` — **byte-identical to `a0b9470`'s own tree**. Seven of the eleven other open pull requests touch this document; I checked every one of the eleven for an added line naming #734 or #737 and **none writes either row**, so there is no duplicate to close mine against. `main` carries no `#734`/`#737` in either disposition file. `docs/HANDOVER.md` byte-identical to `main`.

## 6. The rest

- Both claim files byte-identical to `origin/main`. `VERSION`, the manifest version, the `RELEASE_NOTES.md` heading: untouched (empty diff).
- `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`, every metric equal-line.
- Gate under lease `fixrev737`, keyed on the mode line: `MODE: SCOPED -- 0 script(s) run, 21 scoped out.` — exit 0. A docs-only change reaches no measured closure.
- Reds on **every** commit, paginated `filter=all`: `bb91228` has `pr-contract` red — read the job log, it is `` `## Head` does not name bb91228 ``, i.e. the S10 ordering arm, and it is **green at `a0b9470`**; body names it. `nightly-status` red on both commits — #713's reporter, not one of the 18 required contexts, named not fixed. No required context is red at the head; `mergeable_state unstable`, not blocked.
- Forward-carry `none` accepted: nothing here constrains a later stage.

## 7. The friction entry — you asked, so: accurate in mechanism, one word too strong

Every limb re-derived:
- `record` really is post-merge only: `governance.yml` job `record` carries `if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'`, and the check-runs confirm it — `skipped` on both branch commits, `failure` on `main`. `pr-contract` is the mirror-image `if: … == 'pull_request'`. There is **no** PR-time disposition arm.
- "every subsequent merge inherits it" holds: `checkRecord` enumerates the whole `v6.3.20..origin/main` window, so the next pusher's own push-event run fails on someone else's omission. That is the cost, and it does land on them.
- "two open pull requests in that lane, neither carrying the row": **I had to supply the rule to check this.** Eleven pull requests were open at 15:53:42Z, all authored by `tvofi`, so "lane" is not author. Under my own rule — open `feat/*` branches at that instant — the count is exactly two, #733 and #735, and I verified from their file lists that neither touches a disposition document at all. So the figure holds under a rule the body does not state; per step 8 I am reporting it as re-derived under my definition, not as confirmed under yours.

Where I would push back is **"unenforced"**. It is enforced — post-merge, and post-merge is the window `delivery-status-tracking.md` itself sanctions ("the same session **or an immediate record PR**"). The absence of a pre-merge arm is not obviously an oversight either: most rows are written by a *following* record PR by design, so a PR-time check demanding a self-row would refuse the ordinary shape. The defect you actually measured is narrower and worth stating in those terms: **the detector fires on a commit that is not the offending branch's, so it can neither attribute the omission nor be paid by the party that made it** — and #734 declared `## Friction: none` while skipping the row, which is the same fact from the other side. As "unenforced" it overstates; as "enforced where it cannot be attributed" it is exactly right and survives the root-cause seat.

## Could not establish

- Whether CI's **API-mode** enumeration (`GITHUB_TOKEN` set → `RECORD_ENUM: api`) agrees with the subject-mode enumeration I ran. It cannot be simulated: a `commit-tree` SHA has no `/commits/<sha>/pulls` mapping, so API mode would *skip* the synthetic commit and never test the self-row. Subject mode is the strictly stronger arm here — it enumerates #737 from the `(#737)` subject the squash will carry — so passing it implies the API arm passes on that commit. I did not verify the other 18 enumerate identically in both modes.
- Whether `#201` has received the comment `delivery-status-tracking` item 3 owes for this state change. Post-merge, and yours.

nodes.title: fix: overall score is driving, not the house grade
nodes.body:
The headline 5/100 on a DHW-only cheap-hour plan was the house time-constant grade, not a judgment of when the tank ran. Overall was `mean(envelope, machine, operation)` of whichever existed; envelope is `clip((τ_h − 20) / 80, 0, 1) × 100`, and a ~24 h house is 5. A fresh install has no machine or operation evidence, so overall *was* the house. Operation also skipped any day under 1 kWh, which is most summer DHW-only days.

Overall is now the mean of machine and operation only. Envelope stays in the breakdown (click the headline; sensor attributes `envelope` / `machine` / `operation`). A day under 0.2 kWh still grades, so a cheap DHW-only day can score 100. No driving evidence leaves overall unset (sensor unavailable) instead of publishing 5/100.

The five `coord_*` fixtures record `insight.scores.overall` as null and are claimed: a fresh capture has no machine or operation evidence. `coordinator_loc` and `max_class_loc` 10006 → 10005, recorded with this change. leaves #201 open.

## Head

`b63470bda78ba637042e6276d45bced2793b9a4d`

## Mutation proof

Averaging envelope back into overall turns `a fresh install does not publish the house grade as overall` and `a ~24 h house is not 5/100 overall while nothing has been driven` red in `tests/features.py`. Restoring the 1.0 kWh skip floor turns `a DHW-only cheap day under 1 kWh still grades operation` red.

## Null control

Merge-base `36c649d` still averages the house into overall, so a leaky-house install with no COP or operation book publishes ~5/100. A 0.8 kWh cheap DHW day is skipped and never writes `_operation_score`.

## Figures

`ALL 1244 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED`: `PYTHONPATH=tests:tests/hastub:custom_components python3 tests/entities.py`
`ALL 2123 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED`: `PYTHONPATH=tests:tests/hastub:custom_components python3 tests/features.py`
`STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`: `PYTHONPATH=tests:tests/hastub:custom_components python3 tests/structure.py`

## Red checks

`nightly-status` — #713's reporter. The last concluded scheduled Tests run was red; the report is that job's own log. This pull request did not change a test workflow or the nightly lane. The cheaper detector is the scheduled `nightly-ha` job, which already ran; this reporter is the standing cost #713 paid so that conclusion is visible. The check is not a required context and does not block a merge.

## Forward-carry

none

## Friction

none

nodes.title: fix(#505): the #195 partition is a predicate, not a list of module names
nodes.body:
The #195 tranche partition was a list of module names, and #505 is what a list does when
the tree moves under it. The fix is not a fresher list — that has the same defect one merge
later — but a predicate whose complement is a real group, plus the enumerator that prints
the partition at a merge base so the next seat derives its scope instead of trusting a
roster string.

    coordinator.py  -> W5-G7
    everything else -> W5-G8, the residual, created here

`tools/audit/w5-partition/coverage_tree.sh` measures the whole package over the default-gate
script list **derived** from `tests/run.sh` (`grep -oE 'run "\$PYTHON" tests/[a-z_]+\.py'`,
less `env_drift`, which is `golden.py`'s drift-mode alternative, and `rolling`, which is
`SLOW=1`-only). It writes nothing inside the worktree. `tools/audit/w5-partition/partition.py`
prints the partition and refuses two conditions, each demonstrated firing beside its null
control by `--self-test`: a roster carrying no residual group, and a module a *done* tranche
drove to the bar that is below it again.

**One deliverable, not two, and the measurement is why.** The issue asks whether testing a
module at 0.0 % deserves its own tranche. There is no such module. `process_worker.py` was
untested when #505 measured it at `d979110`; #540 merged the next day and pinned it, and #654
lifted it again — so the pull-forward the issue asks about is already spent, and the module
is now one ordinary member of the residual, among the smallest deficits in it. Nothing in
the below-bar set is at zero. What would make me wrong: a module at or near zero that no
tranche covers would deserve exactly the pull-forward #505 describes, and the enumerator is
what answers that at any head — at this one it prints none. The second thing that would make
me wrong is a residual too large to execute, and the answer there is that a group is not a
pull request: W5-G3 above it is one group and one issue over eight merges, and W5-G8's brief
says to order by missed statements, stop at the size ceiling, and re-run the enumerator
between pull requests.

The coverage work itself is explicitly a later tranche's, and the carry is in the tree rather
than in this thread — see `## Forward-carry`.

Closes #505.

## Head

`4e9ffe6c398b78ace00a5662676aacfe689f9014`.

Two commits sit between this head and `8355196`, the head every figure below was measured at,
and neither changes an input the instrument reads:

- `6feed31`, the merge of `origin/main` at `36c649d`. #729 rewrote the `#724` bullet of the
  pull-request list and the `#509` row of the issues table; #730 rewrote the `feat` row. Each
  is adjacent to a line this branch edits, so the conflict was adjacency, not content — main
  never touched the wave-5 row or the `#505` row. Resolution and its whole-file proof are in
  `## Null control`.
- `4e9ffe6`, fourteen comment lines in `tools/audit/w5-partition/coverage_tree.sh`, naming the
  one script the derived list drops (below).

The control for "no measured input moved", rather than the assertion:
`git diff --stat 8355196..HEAD` names exactly `docs/plan-2026-09-open-issues.md` and
`tools/audit/w5-partition/coverage_tree.sh`;
`git diff --stat 8355196..HEAD -- custom_components tests tools/audit/w5-partition/partition.py`
is empty; and of the sixteen `^[+-]` lines in the `coverage_tree.sh` diff, the count that are
not `^[+-]#` is **0** —

    git diff 8355196..HEAD -- tools/audit/w5-partition/coverage_tree.sh \
      | grep -E '^[+-]' | grep -vE '^(\+\+\+|---)' | grep -vE '^[+-]#' | wc -l

so the harness is byte-identical in every executable line, `partition.py` byte-identical
entire, and the package and suite byte-identical entire. That is what discharges `fixer.md`
step 6 here: the evidence describes one tree, and the control is that the merge did not make
a new one. `partition.py --self-test`, `tests/structure.py`, `tests/entities.py`,
`tests/closure.py selftest` and `.claude/workflows/brief_lint.mjs` were re-executed at
`4e9ffe6` regardless and are green — 11, ratchet PASSED, 1244, 8 and `TOTAL: 0 error(s)`. So
was the **whole `fast` coverage stage and the mutation proof on top of it**; see
`## Mutation proof`, which reproduces the recorded fast-only figures to the statement.

**This body was also rewritten out of a duplicated state**, which is worth saying because the
diff of it is large for a repair round that changed two things. Every H2 from `## Head` down
appeared twice; the earlier copy's `## Red checks` did answer `typing` and the later one did
not, and both a script and a reviewer read the later one. See `## Friction`.

**Derived-list drop, now in the harness header rather than left to be re-measured.** The
derivation greps for `run "$PYTHON" tests/<name>.py`, and that substring does not occur in
`run_always "$PYTHON" tests/closure.py selftest`, so `closure.py` is in the default gate and
silently absent from `DERIVED`. `grep -nE 'run_always "\$PYTHON" tests/' tests/run.sh` returns
the whole dropped set: `env_drift`, already excluded above and symmetrically, and `closure`.
It is harmless and measured rather than argued — running `tests/closure.py selftest` alone
under this file's own `coveragerc` leaves every statement of
`custom_components/heatpump_optimizer` missed, so no module gains a covered line and the
partition is unchanged. Widening the pattern would add a gate-scoping selftest and no
coverage. The header says all of that.

## Mutation proof

The fix's line is the roster's residual group. Revert it — run the enumerator against
`origin/main`'s own `wave-5-groups.json`, the same coverage data — and the enumerator refuses:

    git show origin/main:.claude/workflows/wave-5-groups.json > $W/roster_main.json
    python3 tools/audit/w5-partition/partition.py --coverage $W/out/coverage.json \
      --roster $W/roster_main.json

goes to exit 1 with `RESULT modules_unassigned=22` and `REFUSED: the roster carries no
W5-G8 …`, and 22 of the 23 below-bar rows print `-> NONE`. With this branch's roster the same
data prints `RESULT modules_unassigned=0` at exit 0. That is #505 reproduced and closed on one
instrument. `origin/main`'s roster is unchanged by #729 and #730 —
`git diff --stat 6799ef4..origin/main -- .claude/workflows/wave-5-groups.json` is empty — so
the mutation's input is the same file it was at the reviewed head.

**Re-executed at `4e9ffe6`** rather than carried across the merge, over the `fast` stage —
which the `## Null control` bullet below establishes selects the same below-bar set as the
whole default gate. The pair, with each exit status read from `partition.py` and not from a
pipeline: branch roster `RESULT modules_unassigned=0`, **exit 0**; `origin/main`'s roster,
same coverage data, `RESULT modules_unassigned=22` and the `REFUSED: the roster carries no
W5-G8 …` line, **exit 1**. Rows printing `-> NONE`: **22** under the mutation, **0** under the
branch roster. And the run reproduces the recorded fast-only figures exactly —
`coverage_statements=14885`, `coverage_missing=1202`, `modules_measured=53`,
`modules_below_bar=23`, `coverage_total_pct=91.9` — which is the strongest available control
that the merge did not move the tree the figures describe.

`partition.py --self-test` mutates the two refusals rather than the tail of the script: a
roster with the residual group deleted (refused), a done tranche's module pushed back below
the bar (refused), and for each the null control that must *not* fire — the same module above
the bar, and a below-bar module no list ever named, which is assigned anyway. It also carries
the control for the bar itself: the same module at 99 % is not printed at all.

## Null control

- **The conflict resolution, proven whole-file rather than at the hunk.** A narrow read of a
  conflict region cannot see a line silently dropped elsewhere, so the resolution was built by
  taking `origin/main`'s file verbatim and re-applying only the three lines this branch owns.
  Two independent checks, each with the control that makes it discriminating:
  `git diff origin/main...HEAD -U0 -- docs/plan-2026-09-open-issues.md` is exactly three
  one-line hunks (`@@ -82 +82 @@`, `@@ -355 +355 @@`, `@@ -620,0 +621 @@`); and comparing the
  **multiset** of lines, the resolution loses 2 of `origin/main`'s lines — precisely the two
  rows this branch replaces — gains 3, and introduces 0 duplicates. The null control for that
  second check is the same comparison against the *unresolved* branch side, which loses 37 of
  main's lines and gains 37: the check does discriminate, so 2 and 0 are readings and not a
  method that always reports clean.
- **The end-to-end scripts.** The roster asserts that end-to-end scripts cannot buy
  coverage. Measured rather than repeated, for the four it names plus the one it does not: the same
  head measured with the fast scripts only, and again with `validate`, `edge`, `backtest`,
  `optimality` **and `stress.py`** added, moves the missed count of exactly one module
  (`optimizer.py`, 81 → 77) and leaves the below-bar set identical, 23 modules both times.
  `optimizer.py` is above the bar in both. So the partition is invariant to whether the
  expensive half of the gate runs — which is also the bound `tests/closures.json` predicts:
  `stress.py`'s measured closure contains eleven production modules and is a superset of the
  other four.
- **`process_worker.py`.** The same measurement over `tests/features.py` at `09722e9^`
  (`24920ef`, the commit before #654) reads 86.3 % — far above the figure #505 recorded, not
  at it. The 0.0 % reading did not survive to #654; #540 had already ended it.
- **`tests/features.py`.** It fails two checks under the coverage harness at this head and
  passes 2121 of 2121 without it. The two are the #525 heartbeat pair, and its own null
  control fails with it — both arms read zero ticks — so the tracer removed the stall the
  check exists to see. That is the instrument, not the tree, and it is written into the
  harness header rather than left for the next seat to rediscover.

## Figures

Coverage over the tree at a named commit is an in-tree corpus with a closed window, so these
are literals here and nowhere else — no brief and no plan cell restates one.

- The partition at `8355196`, and every figure in the table below:
  `W=$(mktemp -d); W5P_WORK=$W tools/audit/w5-partition/coverage_tree.sh all && python3 tools/audit/w5-partition/partition.py --coverage $W/out/coverage.json`
  → `coverage_total_pct=92.0`, `coverage_statements=14885`, `coverage_missing=1198`,
  `modules_measured=53`, `modules_below_bar=23`, `modules_unassigned=0`, exit 0.

| | #505, recorded at `d979110` | re-measured at `8355196` |
|---|---|---|
| total statement coverage | 90.4 % | **92.0 %** |
| statements | 14209 | **14885** |
| modules below the 95 % bar | 30 of 53 | **23 of 53** |
| below-bar modules in no tranche | 9 | **22** — the defect grew while the issue sat |
| `coordinator.py` missed / tree deficit | 714 of 1369 | **680 of 1198**, 56.8 % |
| `process_worker.py` | 0.0 %, 36 of 36 missed | **94.1 %, 3 of 51 missed** |

- `process_worker.py` at `24920ef` (`09722e9^`), same instrument narrowed to
  `tests/features.py`: **86.3 %, 7 of 51 missed**. Command in `## Null control`.
- End-to-end marginal contribution, fast-only against the full default-gate set at the same
  head: total missed **1202 → 1198**; one module moves (`optimizer.py` 81 → 77); the below-bar

**Mutation pair, exit status read from `$?` immediately after `partition.py`, never through a pipeline:**

```
ARM 1  branch roster           EXIT=0
  RESULT coverage_total_pct=91.9 / statements=14885 / missing=1202
  RESULT modules_measured=53 / modules_below_bar=23 / modules_unassigned=0
  rows -> NONE: 0     REFUSED lines: 0

ARM 2  origin/main roster (fix reverted), same coverage data   EXIT=1
  RESULT ... identical first five lines ...
  RESULT modules_unassigned=22
  rows -> NONE: 22
  REFUSED: the roster carries no W5-G8; the residual predicate has no group to
           assign to ... -- this is #505
```

`origin/main`'s roster carries `W5-G1..W5-G7` and no `W5-G8`. **The mutation is not vacuous**, and all six figures reproduce to the digit across a different platform. The single assigned row under the mutation is `coordinator.py 83.3 pct 4063 stmts 680 missed 56.6 pct of deficit -> W5-G7`.

`partition.py --self-test`: **11** checks, both refusals firing and each null control not firing. `tranche_for` returns `W5-G8` for every module but `coordinator.py`, so the partition is total by construction — which is why round one's synthetic never-imported module landed in the residual.

**And the deliverable's own premise re-measured**: the lowest below-bar module is `away.py` at **75.5 %**, then `wood_fuel.py` 75.6, `coordinator.py` 83.3. **Nothing at or near zero**, so #505's asked-for pull-forward has no subject, as the body says.

## The derived-list drop — independently measured

Not taken from the previous reviewer. My own enumeration: `grep -oE 'tests/[a-z_]+\.py' tests/run.sh` (every script named anywhere) minus `DERIVED` gives **two** names, `closure` **and `gate_lock`**. The header's own re-derivation command, `grep -nE 'run_always "\$PYTHON" tests/'`, returns `env_drift` and `closure` — accurate for what it greps, but the header calls that "the whole dropped set" and `gate_lock.py` is executed by `run.sh` too (line 93 `exec ... flock-wrap`, lines 195/212 `renew`).

**Harmless, measured not argued, and identically so for both**: neither `tests/closure.py` nor `tests/gate_lock.py` imports `custom_components.heatpump_optimizer` at all, so neither can cover a package statement and the partition is unchanged by either. The header's conclusion holds; only its scope word is narrower than the truth. A precision note, not a block — `tools/audit/` is `INERT` and no figure moves.

## Standing gates at `4e9ffe6`

- `VERSION` 6.3.20, manifest 6.3.20, `RELEASE_NOTES.md` heading `## v6.3.20` — `git diff origin/main...HEAD` over all three is **empty**. Untouched.
- Claim files **byte-identical** to `origin/main`, both of them. The branch claims nothing.
- `tests/structure.py` → `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`. `tests/structure_budgets.json` and `.claude/workflows/policy_budgets.json` byte-identical to `origin/main` — **no budget moved, none re-recorded**.
- `tests/entities.py` → `ALL 1244 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED`. `tests/closure.py selftest` → `ALL 8 closure shrink pins PASSED`.
- Classification: both new files are under `tools/audit/`, and `closure.is_inert()` returns **True** for each. Deliberately classified.
- Gate, **keyed on the mode line**: `MODE: SCOPED -- 0 script(s) run, 21 scoped out.` A scoped run correctly selecting nothing — the diff is a roster string, a plan row and two `INERT` files. Not a `FULL` zero.
- `brief_lint.mjs` → `TOTAL: 0 error(s) across 4 file(s)`. `check-wave-script.mjs` → `48 passed, 0 failed`. `policy_lint.mjs --budgets` → every cap under, `--pr-body` on the live body → `0 error(s)`.
- **No literal metric in a live brief**: the only metric-shaped literals in W5-G7's and W5-G8's briefs and notes are "tranche 3 of 4" and "4 of 4" — ordinals. Every coverage figure is gone from the roster and replaced by the instrument.
- Carry present in both roster destinations, `brief` **and** `resume.note`, for W5-G7 and for the newly created W5-G8; read back from the file, not taken from the body. Preconditions, not opportunities, with their controls and a re-measurement instruction.
- Disposition in all three places in the plan: Delivery-status Wave 5 cell (line 82), the `#505` issues row (line 355, `DONE`), and the PR bullet (line 621).

## Head and freshness

`origin/main` re-fetched at posting time: still `36c649d`, unmoved through the whole review. Live PR head re-read at posting time: `4e9ffe6c398b78ace00a5662676aacfe689f9014` — the SHA in `## Head`, the SHA I measured, and the SHA I am posting against. No re-measurement was needed.

**`nightly-status` is red at this head and stays red.** 29 check-run objects, 0 refusals, exactly one non-green name: `nightly-status`. It is #713's reporter of a genuinely failed nightly, not one of the eighteen `main-protect` contexts, and nothing in this diff reaches it. Naming it, not fixing it. All eighteen required contexts are green.

## API refusals, and what I could not establish

**2 refusals**, both counted, both the same `gh` **client-side** guard on `actions/jobs/<id>/logs` ("the response contains terminal escape sequences") — recovered with `--allow-escape-sequences`. **0** server-side refusals, **0** rate-limit refusals, `gh` exit 0 on every `check-runs` page.

Could not establish, stated rather than reported as confirmed:

- **The body's "24 check-run objects" at `4e9ffe6` does not reproduce — I count 29.** CI kept running after the body was written; it is a figure about a live head, which never converges. The load-bearing part does reproduce: exactly one non-green name, `nightly-status`, and all eighteen required contexts green. The `42` at `8355196` reproduces exactly.
- `tests/features.py` passing 2121 of 2121 **bare** is round one's measurement, not re-taken here; I confirmed only the harnessed arm (`2 of 2121 FAILED`, both arms of the pair at 0 ticks).

nodes.title: policy: a figure over a corpus the tree cannot see had no rule, and the split is inside one section
nodes.body:
`## Figures` in `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` asks for *"the command that
printed it"*, and nothing executes that command. The contract therefore has grip
only where an instrument in the tree prints the figure; where the corpus is the
GitHub API or this repository's own review history, a command that did **not**
print the number satisfies the section exactly as written. This lands the
countermeasure the root-cause seat proposed for that gap — a writing rule, not a
detector — as an equal-line rewrite of one clause in
`.claude/rules/writing-for-agents.md`, which is at its cap.

The finding is #201 comment
[5618564043](https://github.com/tvofi/heatpump_optimizer/issues/201#issuecomment-5618564043)
and it governs where this body differs from it.

## Approval

**This is policy and the owner's approval is required before it merges**
(`CLAUDE.md`, *Where the policy is*; decision 0007). Nothing here is merged on a
seat's judgement.

What is being approved, verbatim — the clause added to the criteria paragraph of
`.claude/rules/writing-for-agents.md`:

> A **measurement** names its instrument — a metric, a cap, `--budgets` — never
> the figure it prints. Where the corpus is not in the tree and its window still
> open, the instrument is the **enumerator**: the command that, run alone, prints
> exactly that number, its literal only in `## Figures`. No enumerator, no figure.

The first sentence is the rule the file already carried, moved; the rest is new.
It addresses **process state (c)** — the process was followed and did not produce
the intended result — which is the state the seat named and evidenced.

**Two departures from the seat's proposed wording, both deliberate.**

1. **A closed window is exempt, and the seat's draft did not say so.** *"Six
   `Fix review: revise` verdicts on #686, #687, #689, #690 and #708"* is a fact
   about a finished window that no later event moves. *"456 first lines in the
   corpus"* is not: #719's round-2 verdict (comment `5618397017`) re-ran that
   sweep, got a different total, got a third from the literal `grep` form of the
   same rule, and reports the comment corpus itself as having grown between the
   two runs. Those numbers stay in that comment and are not restated here —
   under the clause this pull request adds, an open-window figure whose
   enumerator I have not written is not mine to state. A clause that refused the
   closed case too would refuse the legitimate history already in the plan, the
   handover and the release notes, which is the false-fire surface the seat
   priced when it refused to build a check. The discriminator is written into
   the condition — *its window still open* — not bolted on as an exception,
   because an exception at the end is what gets routed around.
2. **It says `A **measurement**`, not "a durable artifact".** The paragraph it
   joins already lists **measurement** as the first thing a sentence may carry,
   and the file's `paths:` and scope sentence already reach pull-request bodies,
   issues, comments, briefs, rosters and `docs/HANDOVER.md`. Naming the artifact
   would have re-scoped a rule that is already scoped, in a file with no line to
   spare for it.

**One file, not two, and the reason is mechanical as well as editorial.**
`brief-citations.md` rule 4 refuses a literal in a wave brief and requires that
*"a stated count the tree answers must equal what it answers"* — a corpus
`brief_lint.mjs` can open, which is precisely the case this clause does not
cover. Its own text forbids stating a rule the linter does not implement
(*"Extending the plan format means extending the linter in the same PR"*), and
an out-of-tree corpus is one no linter can reach. `fixer.md` step 3 and
`orchestrator.md` section 1 carry the warning half already — *"state the rule or
name the instrument, never the number"*, *"a paged listing is a sliding window"*
— and both are at their caps, and `policy_lint`'s `duplicates` check refuses a
repeat of a clause across the corpus. So the extension goes in the one file that
states the rule, and the other three keep pointing at it.

## Head

`7e36ae6791cc06b8bd352f5f770a0fedb7e25c9a`

Branch `claude/figure-enumerator-rule`, merge base `a1369a2`. Three commits: the
clause, the disposition row, and a merge. The history is worth one sentence
because a reviewer will ask. The branch was pushed at `03d36df` off `6250ea9`,
then `git fetch origin` showed `docs/plan-2026-09-open-issues.md` had moved on
`main`, so it was rebased onto `a1369a2` and the row written against the current
file rather than a copy of it — which diverged HEAD from the pull request's head
ref. `prepr.sh` refuses the force-push past that (*"the push is refused as a
non-fast-forward and the force-push past it is forbidden — merge, then rewrite
`## Head` at the merge commit"*) because a rewrite of a pushed head can drop a
commit somebody else put there and the check cannot tell that case from this
one. Merged as prescribed; `03d36df`'s two files are byte-identical to the
rebased commit's, and `git diff origin/main...HEAD` is the three files below and
nothing else.

Worktree claimed with `git worktree lock`, not a root-level marker — a tracked
marker file changes the diff and flips `GATE_SCOPE=auto` to `MODE: FULL`.

## Mutation proof

This change is prose in a policy file. It adds no check, so there is no arm to
break; `defect-root-cause.md`'s *A detector must be shown to detect* binds a
check, test, lane or hook and does not bind here, which the seat states in its
§5 and which this body does not dress up otherwise.

What is mutation-proven is that the caps this change had to fit under are live
and would have refused it. Driven at this head:

- **The line cap refuses one more line.** Appending a single line to
  `.claude/rules/writing-for-agents.md` and running
  `node .claude/workflows/policy_lint.mjs`:
  `ERROR [budgets] .claude/rules/writing-for-agents.md: 66 lines exceeds its cap
  of 65. Cut, or state the case for a higher cap in the pull request body.`,
  exit 1. Restored, exit 0.
- **The generated Cursor rule refuses drift.** With `.cursor/rules/writing-for-agents.mdc`
  reverted to its pre-change bytes, `node .claude/workflows/rules_sync.mjs --check`
  exits 1 with `RULES-SYNC: 1 file(s) out of date. Run without --check.`
  Regenerated, exit 0.

The corpus's own controlled comparison is what stands in for a fixture, and each
half was re-read from its source rather than taken from the seat's summary:

- **Failing on the defect.** #719 `## Figures` bullet 1 gives
  `gh api --paginate '/repos/tvofi/heatpump_optimizer/issues/comments?per_page=100'`
  and then two literals that command cannot print. Blocked in round 2
  (comment `5618397017`): *"the two enumeration totals in the Delivery-status row
  do not re-derive under the rule that row states"*.
- **Passing once fixed.** #719 bullet 2, same section, same author: *"the row
  states the enumerator, not the number:"* followed by a `git log … | grep -cE`
  line. It replaced a literal that round 1 (comment `5617886425`) had blocked,
  and round 2 left it untouched. Its corpus is `git log` — in the tree.
- **Caught before commit, at zero rounds.** #713's body, under its `## Figures`
  discussion: *"the rule for that, not a count — a count moves whenever a job or
  a matrix arm is added, and the first draft of this pull request carried one
  that was already stale by one."* No reviewer was involved.

## Null control

**The rule does not go green by stating fewer numbers.** The same bodies that
carried the refuted figures state figures a reviewer re-executed and matched —
`MODE:` lines, `--budgets`, entity totals, mypy censuses — and every one of them
is an in-tree instrument named rather than restated. The clause leaves those
exactly as they are; it changes only the case where no instrument exists.

**The unmodified tree accepts the defect**, re-driven here rather than quoted.
With #719's live body and its own live head — `gh pr view 719 --json body`,
`gh pr view 719 --json headRefOid` — `node .claude/workflows/policy_lint.mjs
--pr-body <that body> --head <that head>` exits 0 with `PR-BODY: 0 error(s)`.
`checkPrBody` validates that `## Figures` is non-empty and not a bare `n/a`,
validates `## Forward-carry` destinations against the tree and `## Friction`'s
grammar, and validates nothing about a figure. Emptying that section in the same
body is what turns it red — `pr-body: ## Figures is empty`, exit 1. The
asymmetry is the cause stated as code, and this change does not alter it: no
check moves here.

**The three deletions that paid for the added lines, each with the test it
failed.** The file's own criterion is that a sentence stays only if it carries a
measurement, the rule behind one, a decision and why, a constraint, or a refusal
— **and is the only place in the artifact that carries it** — and that
*"restating the ask, narrating the route"* is cut, not shortened.

1. *"If you are unsure whether something is filler, keep it — a redundant
   sentence costs a reader a second, a dropped control ships a defect."*
   **Fails uniqueness.** Its tie-break restates the sentence two before it
   (*"precision wins and the artifact gets longer"*) and its cost asymmetry
   restates the sentence immediately before it (*"A short artifact missing a
   control is a defect"*). Neither fact leaves the file.
2. *"Split the state rather than asking one file to be both."* **Narrating the
   route.** The split is performed by the three paragraphs that follow it, and
   the constraint it previews is stated as **"Nothing goes in both."**
3. *"That is what non-redundant means here."* **Restating.** It defines the
   sentence it follows and adds no fact.

The instrument sentence itself was **moved, not deleted**: out of the
`docs/HANDOVER.md` paragraph, where it reached one file, into the criteria
paragraph that reaches the whole development record. That relocation is the
substance of the fix — the rule was scoped to the one artifact whose figures
were least often the problem.

## Figures

Every figure below is the output of an in-tree instrument, named rather than
restated — which is the discipline this pull request is about, applied to itself.

* the file against its cap, the floor, the corpus and all three role caps —
  `node .claude/workflows/policy_lint.mjs --budgets`
* the whole policy corpus, its fixtures and the known-bad ledger —
  `node .claude/workflows/policy_lint.mjs`
* the generated Cursor rule against its source —
  `node .claude/workflows/rules_sync.mjs --check`
* the roster citations —
  `node .claude/workflows/brief_lint.mjs`
* the gate mode and the scripts it selected —
  `GATE_SCOPE=auto GOLDEN_MODE=drift GOLDEN_REF=$(git merge-base origin/main HEAD) ./tests/run.sh`
  — key on the `MODE:` line, never the count
* the diff's line symmetry —
  `git diff --numstat $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)...HEAD -- .claude/rules/writing-for-agents.md`

Two literals are stated in this body, both over a **closed** corpus, which is
what the clause exempts and why it is phrased as it is: the five pull requests
carrying the six `Fix review: revise` verdicts, and the two named #719 review
rounds. Their enumerator, for a reader who wants it rather than because the
clause demands it:
`gh api repos/tvofi/heatpump_optimizer/issues/719/comments --paginate --jq '.[] | select(.body|test("^Fix review:")) | .id'`.

The one figure this body does **not** state is how far the class reaches across
the durable artifacts. The seat measured it with a predicate it wrote and did not
commit, so no enumerator can be written for it here, and by the clause's own last
sentence it is not stated. It is in the seat's §3 with its own derivation.

## Red checks

`none` at this head. The rule, rather than a run list: a check is red here only
if `check-runs?filter=all`, paginated, reports a `conclusion` of `failure`,
`timed_out`, `cancelled` or `action_required` for a run on this commit — read
from the API, because `gh pr checks` hides a red-then-green run. Any that appears
is answered under `defect-root-cause.md`'s second trigger, in this section, with
the cheaper detector and its standing cost or the recorded finding that none
exists.

## Forward-carry

`none` for a later stage. The seat's two unaddressed causes are recorded rather
than propagated, because neither has more than one instance and
`finding-propagation.md` carries constraints, not hypotheses: **C2**, a
retraction that did not reach every copy, needs a withdrawal rule that names
every location; **C3**, an authorization that left no artifact, is the
governance-record problem. Both are in #201 comment `5618564043` §5, which is
the artifact a later seat reads.

## Friction

`brief-citations.md: unenforced: rule 4 refuses a literal metric in a wave brief and brief_lint.mjs enforces it; the same discipline over an out-of-tree corpus is enforceable by nothing, and this pull request states it as a writing rule for exactly that reason`

Fix review: merge 7e36ae6791cc06b8bd352f5f770a0fedb7e25c9a

**This is policy. It does not merge on my verdict — the owner's approval is required first (`CLAUDE.md`, *Where the policy is*; decision 0007).** Two findings below are the owner's to rule on, not mine to block on, and I have put them first for that reason.

Reviewed from a detached worktree at `7e36ae6`, claimed with `git worktree lock` and removed after; every temporary file in a private `mktemp -d`. Head at posting time re-read: `7e36ae6`, unmoved. **`origin/main` moved under this review, `a1369a2` → `4e28724`** (four merges). The merge base is unchanged, so every measurement below still describes this head; I re-took the conflict measurement and added a merged-state simulation against the new `main`.

**API calls.** 11 data-bearing `gh` calls, every exit status checked. **0 refusals**, 0 secondary-rate-limit 403s. One call returned HTTP 404 — my own wrong endpoint (`issues/201/comments/<id>` instead of `issues/comments/<id>`); retried and returned. No figure here rests on a call that did not return.

## The two judgements for the owner

**1. Deletion 1 is a partial loss, and its stated test is only partly met.** The body cuts *"If you are unsure whether something is filler, keep it — a redundant sentence costs a reader a second, a dropped control ships a defect"* for uniqueness against two adjacent sentences. Opening the surrounding text: the survivors carry the priority ordering (*"precision wins and the artifact gets longer"*) and the **expensive** half of the asymmetry (*"A short artifact missing a control is a defect"*). They do not carry the **cheap** half — that redundancy costs almost nothing — and they do not carry the explicit default under uncertainty. That matters here because the very next paragraph is an *only if* (*"a sentence stays **only if** it carries … and is the only place"*), which pushes the other way when a seat cannot classify a sentence; the deleted sentence was the resolver between the two paragraphs.

Instrument, so this is checkable rather than an opinion about prose: `grep -rniE "if you are unsure|when unsure|in doubt|keep it\b" CLAUDE.md .claude/rules/ tools/audit/briefs/ .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` at this head returns nothing. After this pull request the under-uncertainty default appears **nowhere in the corpus**, not merely nowhere in this file — so the file's own uniqueness test (uniqueness *within the artifact*) is the weaker test here and it passed while a corpus-wide copy was lost.

I do not block on it. The default is derivable from *"Precision outranks concision, **always**"* plus *"cutting evidence is never compliance with this rule"*, both of which survive and are bolder for the neighbour being gone, and the file is at 65/65 so the trade was paid for. But it is a real loss in the one file whose whole subject is when to cut, and the owner should rule on it rather than inherit it.

**2. The clause's first act was to suppress a figure it does not actually reach.** The body declines to state how far the class reaches across the durable artifacts, *"by the clause's own last sentence"*. Read the condition as written: *"Where the corpus is **not in the tree** and its window still open"*. That figure's corpus is `docs/plan-2026-09-open-issues.md`, `docs/HANDOVER.md` and `RELEASE_NOTES.md` at a pinned SHA — **in the tree, and a closed window**. Neither leg of the antecedent holds, so the enumerator branch and its *"No enumerator, no figure"* do not reach it. Sentence one does bite (name the instrument, and the predicate was never committed), but the honest repair is to write the regex out, which turns an ad-hoc grep into an enumerator; it is not silence.

So my explicit view: **this is not the rule working, it is the rule being over-applied by the person who wrote it, in the safe direction.** No information is lost to a reader — the analysis is one link away and the body points at it — so the cost is zero. The diagnostic value is not zero: it is evidence against the body's own claim that the condition self-applies cleanly, since the first application of it got the antecedent wrong. That is a reason to watch the clause, not to refuse it.

## The strongest claim: the relocation is real

Verified against the base text, not the summary. Before, the sentence was grammatically bound to one artifact — *"It links to the Delivery-status table rather than restating it, **and it names an instrument** … never the figure that instrument prints"*, where *It* is `docs/HANDOVER.md`. It could not reach a body, an issue or a brief; it was a property of one file. After, it sits in the criteria paragraph, which is unscoped inside the file and therefore governed by the file's own scope sentence — *"pull-request bodies, issues, comments, commit messages, briefs, roster entries, reports, and `docs/HANDOVER.md`"*. **The relocation genuinely widens the reach**, and it is the substance of the change rather than a rewording.

One correction to the body. It says *"the file's `paths:` **and** scope sentence already reach pull-request bodies, issues, comments, briefs, rosters"*. The `paths:` cannot reach a body, an issue or a comment — none is a file, and the globs name `docs/HANDOVER.md`, `docs/plan*.md`, `tools/audit/briefs/**`, `.claude/workflows/*-groups.json`, `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`. The reach to those three is carried by the **scope sentence alone**; `paths:` only decides when the harness loads the rule. The conclusion is unaffected — the new clause reaches exactly as far as the four criteria beside it — but the mechanism is one thing, not two.

## The two departures

**The closed-window condition does separate the two named cases.** *"Six verdicts across five pull requests"* names a corpus that admits no new members; *"456 first lines in the corpus"* names one that grew between two runs of the same sweep — #719's round-two verdict reports exactly that. The discriminator a reviewer applies is *can this corpus gain a member*, which is checkable. Writing it into the condition rather than as a trailing exception is the right call: an antecedent must be satisfied to reach the obligation, where a trailing exception is read after it and can be skipped.

Two residual weaknesses, neither blocking. *Window* is undefined in the clause and exemplified only in this body, which is not policy — a seat can narrow a corpus definition to call a window closed. That route-around is partly self-limiting, since pinning a window to a timestamp is also what makes an enumerator writable. And sentence one's *"never the figure **it** prints"* takes *it* as the instrument, so for an out-of-tree corpus with no instrument the sentence is vacuous and the closed-window case falls through both sentences — which is what the body relies on to state its own two closed-window literals. That reading is the natural one, but it needs the antecedent tracked, and finding 2 above is what happens when it is not.

**The narrower noun covers the refuted set.** Checked against the root-cause seat's own C1 list rather than the summary: #705's in-module site count, its six types stated as three and its four `by_code` rows stated as three; #709's red count and its green-jobs count; #711's *"six times in one day"*; #719's verdict set, its merge count and its two sweep totals. Every one is a stated count offered as evidence, which is a measurement. C3 (#722) is outside it, and the seat itself says so in the same words — *"That is not a measurement at all"* — so the narrowing loses nothing the seat claimed. The boundary the narrower noun creates and does not draw is between a count offered as evidence and a count carried inside a *decision and why* or a *constraint*; none of the refuted figures sits on the far side of it, so the gap is theoretical today.

## The one-file argument, tested rather than accepted

I drove the duplicates claim instead of reading it. Appending the clause verbatim to `tools/audit/briefs/fixer.md` and running `node .claude/workflows/policy_lint.mjs` produces **both** halves of the argument at once:

```
ERROR [duplicates] tools/audit/briefs/fixer.md:259: repeats 12 words from .claude/rules/writing-for-agents.md:30
ERROR [budgets]    tools/audit/briefs/fixer.md: 261 lines exceeds its cap of 257
```

Restored; worktree clean. The other legs hold on inspection: `brief-citations.md` governs `brief_lint.mjs`'s corpus and forbids stating a rule the linter does not implement (*"Extending the plan format means extending the linter in the same PR"*), and its rule 4 covers the in-tree case this clause deliberately does not; `fixer.md` step 3 carries the warning half at `fixer.md:30` and `orchestrator.md` carries *"A paged listing is a sliding window"* at `orchestrator.md:48`, both files at their caps per `--budgets`. **I agree the rule belongs in one file.**

## The role caps, re-derived at both ends

`node .claude/workflows/policy_lint.mjs --budgets`, run by me at the merge base and at this head:

- **role `record` and role `policy` each sat at exactly zero headroom at `a1369a2`** and each fell by four at this head. Role `fixer` did not move. `corpus` fell by the same four; `always-loaded` did not move, so nothing was reclassified out of the floor and `ratchet-budgets.md`'s re-record clause is not engaged.
- The per-file cap was at zero headroom too — the file is 65 lines at both ends, `git diff --numstat` over it is symmetric. So **both** constraints bound, not the byte-derived ones *rather than* the line count as the body has it. The body's substantive point survives and is the sharper one: the line cap alone would have allowed a reflow that added words, and the two zero-headroom role caps are what refused that.

No cap was re-recorded; `.claude/workflows/policy_budgets.json` is not in the diff.

## Mutation arms and the null control, re-driven

Both arms the body claims reproduce at this head, tree clean after each: appending one line gives `ERROR [budgets] … 66 lines exceeds its cap of 65`, exit 1; reverting the generated rule to its pre-change bytes gives `DRIFT .cursor/rules/writing-for-agents.mdc`, exit 1. I added a third the body did not claim — running the generator writes **0 files across 9 sources**, so the committed `.mdc` is byte-identical to the generated form, and the counts match with no orphan.

The null control I re-drove independently, and then strengthened it, because the PR's own arms only show the section must be non-empty:

- **Arm A** — #719's live body at its live head: `PR-BODY: 0 error(s)`, exit 0.
- **Arm B** — the same body with `## Figures` emptied: `ERROR [pr-body] '## Figures' is empty`, exit 1.
- **Arm C, mine** — the same body with `## Figures` replaced by two bullets of invented cardinals and **no command on either line**: `PR-BODY: 0 error(s)`, exit 0.

Arm C is the cause stated as an executed control rather than as a reading of `checkPrBody`: the contract's *"with the command that printed it"* has no enforcement at all, not merely weak enforcement. The asymmetry is real and this change does not alter it, which is what a writing rule is for.

## The #719 pair, verified against source

This is the whole evidential basis for state (c), so I read both rounds rather than the seat's summary of them.

- **Round 1** (`5617886425`) blocked a `## Figures` citation for stating a merge count its own command did not print: *"`## Figures` cites `git log --first-parent --oneline a6e95ff..origin/main`, which prints thirteen lines, not nine."*
- **The repair replaced that with the enumerator form**, and **round 2** (`5618397017`) executed it and left it standing — its merge-enumeration table re-derives all three forms and finds none disagreeing, and its own words are *"the narrow repair is to correct or drop the two totals; **nothing else in the correction needs to move**."*
- **Round 2 blocked the `gh api` totals**: *"the two enumeration totals in the Delivery-status row do not re-derive under the rule that row states"*, after nine executed counting rules, none reaching the stated figures.
- **The split is corroborated by the author's own live body**, which opens `## Figures` with *"Every corpus total the previous body stated is **gone**, not restated"* — the `gh api` figures were in that section and the `git log` enumerator survived beside them.

**What I could not establish, per step 8.** GitHub serves no pull-request body edit history, so I cannot read the byte-level `## Figures` section at `2d9039b`. The claim that bullet 1 and bullet 2 stood *side by side in the same section at the same moment* rests on round 1's citation of `## Figures`, round 2's *"it now sits in the tree rather than only in the body"*, and the live body's own sentence above — strong and mutually independent, but circumstantial rather than the bytes. Relatedly, the body attributes to bullet 2 the quotation *"the row states the enumerator, not the number:"*; the live body reads *"the row states the enumerator and no number:"* and the string as quoted appears in neither verdict comment nor the tree. **I could not re-derive that quotation.** Neither gap touches the conclusion: the substance of the split — a `gh api` figure refuted and a `git log` figure executed and left standing, same body, same author, same round — is verified from the verdicts themselves.

#713's evidence I verified verbatim in its live body: *"the rule for that, not a count — a count moves whenever a job or a matrix arm is added, and the first draft of this pull request carried one that was already stale by one."* Zero rounds, as claimed.

## Everything else

- **The disposition row**, by whole-file diff against the branch's own base: **one line inserted, nothing removed**, at the insertion point the row claims.
- **The merge commit.** Three-dot against the merge base is exactly the three intended files and nothing else. `03d36df`'s two files are byte-identical to the rebased commit's.
- **Conflict, measured not read.** `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` exits **0** against `a1369a2` and again against the moved `4e28724`, driver installed (`MERGE-CLAIM: already-installed`), no `MERGE-CLAIM: refused` line on any path. GitHub reports `mergeable_state: unknown` while it recomputes; the measurement is the answer.
- **Claim files** byte-identical to `main` on both paths — the branch claims nothing and touches no fixture. `VERSION`, the manifest and the notes heading are untouched.
- **Ratchet**: `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`.
- **Gate**, keyed on the mode line: `MODE: SCOPED`, and on a branch that is the legitimate reading.
- **Reds**: `check-runs?filter=all`, paginated, on **every** commit in the branch. No run on any commit has a conclusion of `failure`, `timed_out`, `cancelled` or `action_required`. `## Red checks: none` is correct and `defect-root-cause.md`'s second trigger is not engaged.
- **Forward-carry**: `none` is right. C2 and C3 are recorded in #201 comment `5618564043` §5 in the terms the body states, and neither is a constraint on a later stage on one instance. The clause's own downstream obligation lands in a file every seat loads, which is stronger propagation than a brief.
- **Because `main` moved and took a 200-line `policy_lint.mjs` change with it**, I simulated the merged state — this head's two rule files and its plan row applied on `4e28724` — and ran the newer linter: `TOTAL: 0 error(s) across 36 policy file(s)`, `FIXTURE ok` across 12 check classes, `rules_sync --check` clean, `--record` **0 without a disposition**, and both role caps unchanged from this head. Merging will not redden `main`.

`merge` on the work. **The clause itself is the owner's call, and findings 1 and 2 are what I would want in front of that call.**

nodes.title: record: leftover #677 and #682 no longer say in review
nodes.body:
Leftover #677 and #682 still said in review after #720 and #721 landed. This record names the merge SHAs and this pull request, so `checkRecord` does not redden `main`. The squash that landed #720 omitted the closing keyword, so #677 was marked completed from the issue. leaves #201 open.

## Head

`0f9c67fa67b68a3178c93cfa8f0aa4320f91f65e`

## Mutation proof

A leftover row that still says in review after the merge is the defect this records. Reverting the #677 or #682 row to that wording is the break; `checkRecord` still passes because `#720` and `#721` remain in the file. The check this row exists for is the next merge of *this* pull request: omit its own number and `record` reddens `main` for that number.

## Null control

The unmodified `origin/main` leftover still says in review. This branch replaces those cells with **CLOSED by #720, merged `e49b2fb`** and **CLOSED by #721, merged `8db8abe`**, and the matching Delivery-status bullets with the same SHAs.

## Figures

`git log -1 --oneline e49b2fb` — `e49b2fb fix(#677): enumerate merges from the commit-to-PR API (#720)`. The leftover row carries that SHA rather than restating it.
`git log -1 --oneline 8db8abe` — `8db8abe fix(#682): compare rendered disposition structure to source (#721)`.
`git log -1 --oneline 52b9eb6` — `52b9eb6 record: rows for #720 and #721, written before their merges (#725)`.

## Red checks

`nightly-status` — #713's reporter. The last concluded scheduled Tests run was red; the report is that job's own log. This leftover record did not change a test, a workflow, or the nightly lane. The cheaper detector is the scheduled `nightly-ha` job, which already ran; this reporter is the standing cost #713 paid so that conclusion is visible. The check is not a required context and does not block a merge.

none

nodes.title: ci(#533): the nightly's conclusion reached nobody for two nights, so a red check now says so
nodes.body:
The nightly's conclusion reached nobody for two nights. `nightly-ha` and `slow`
run on `schedule` alone, are `skipped` on every push- and pull-request-triggered
commit, and are not among the 18 required contexts on `main-protect`. A
scheduled run's conclusion therefore attaches to whatever commit was `main`'s
head when the cron fired — beside that same commit's own `skipped` entry from
the push — and the next merge moves the head and strands it. Both `nightly-ha`
arms failed on the 2026-09-09 and 2026-09-10 schedules and a seat sent looking
found it, not the lane.

The root-cause seat costed a countermeasure that files an issue and **rejected**
it: `issues: write` against a `permissions: contents: read` floor this workflow
states as deliberate, plus dedupe-and-close logic, and a standing false-positive
cost of an issue filed for a registry outage. This is the cheaper shape.

**`tests/nightly_status.py`, run by a new `nightly-status` job on every pull
request.** It reads the last **concluded** scheduled run of `tests.yml` and
reports it as its own check.

**Why a red check and not a warning inside a green job.** `ci-autofix.mdc` says
read the summary line and not the tick; `brief-citations.mdc` names
`FIXTURE ok: N error(s)` as a shape "designed to print beside a clean exit,
which is exactly the shape that lets a real error be waved through". A warning
inside a passing job is that shape, and the defect being fixed is precisely that
nobody looked.

**Which run "the last nightly" means**, stated in the module docstring and in
the job comment: the most recent `schedule`-triggered run **that reached a
conclusion**, never the most recent one outright. The two differ for the ~45
minutes the lane takes; a verdict that flips to "no answer" for those minutes
every night teaches people to re-run the check rather than read it. A newer
in-flight run is an extra line, never the verdict.

**Four states, one exit code each.**

| state | when | exit |
|---|---|---|
| `FAILED` | **the run's own conclusion** is outside `{success, skipped, neutral}`, **or** a job of that run is | 1 |
| `PASSED` | that run is recent enough, its own conclusion is a passing one, it ran the watched lanes, and nothing failed | 0 |
| `RUNNING` | nothing has concluded inside the window and a run is in flight | 1 |
| `ABSENT` | no scheduled run; **or** the newest concluded one is older than `--max-age-nights` (2, so three nights of silence is `ABSENT`); **or** it concluded without running a watched lane | 1 |
| `UNREADABLE` | the API call failed, was rate-limited, did not parse, returned a jobs page smaller than its own `total_count`, or carried a run with no `created_at` | 2 |

`FAILED`'s two halves are both needed and the run's half is authoritative: a run
can conclude non-`success` while every job the listing carries reads `success`
or `skipped`, and reading only the jobs is what produced
`NIGHTLY PASSED … run conclusion 'failure'` beside exit 0. When no job failed,
the report says the run's own conclusion is the evidence and how many jobs it
judged — because "the nightly failed" beside a clean job list reads as a broken
check.
`FAILED` names every failing job, its age in nights, the run id and a URL per
job: "the nightly failed" trains blindness, `nightly-ha (stable)` with a run id
does not. `ABSENT` is deliberately three situations under one word because all
three are the same error — missing evidence read as good evidence — and the
report says which one it is. Staleness wins over `FAILED`: a failure nine nights
old is not "the last nightly failed", it is "the nightly has not run for nine
nights", and the two have different fixes.

**Its own failure mode.** `UNREADABLE` exits 2, never 0. A check that goes green
when it could not look converts an open defect into a closed one, which is the
shape `defect-root-cause.mdc` says this repository keeps producing. The cost of
failing closed is a red check during a GitHub API outage; the cost of failing
open is the two nights above, silently.

**Permissions.** The job declares `actions: read` at **job** level. Actions
metadata is not repository content and `contents: read` cannot see it, so this
is a widening of a floor the workflow states as deliberate, and it is written
down as one — far narrower than the rejected `issues: write`, but a widening.
A job-level `permissions:` block **replaces** the workflow default for that job
and is inherited by no other, so every other job still runs on `contents: read`.
Verified below, and pinned as a property rather than as its instance: the check
asserts the whole set of jobs that override the floor.

**It must not become a required context, and is not one.** The property that
makes `nightly-ha` unrequired is real — a registry outage or a Home Assistant
release can redden it, neither of which is a reason to refuse an unrelated merge
— and requiring this would transfer that property to every pull request in the
repository. It runs on `pull_request` only and not on pushes to `main`, for the
same reason: a lane that can go red for reasons outside this repository must not
be able to turn `main` red. Every report, green or red, says in its own text
that it blocks nothing.

**Classification of the new file.** `tests/nightly_status.py` is on
`closure.py`'s `NOT_A_TEST` list and excluded in `run.sh` (it needs the Actions
API, which this suite has neither the network nor a token for), and it is **not**
`INERT`: `tests/entities.py` imports it and drives its states, so it lives in
that script's measured closure. `tests/closures.json` grows by that one path.

**Concurrency.** #709 is editing `nightly-ha`'s comment and adding its install
step, and a third seat may touch `coordinator.py`. This branch touches neither
`coordinator.py` nor `nightly-ha`'s own lines: its workflow hunks are a bullet
in the header block and a new job inserted after `nightly-ha` ends. Its
`tests/entities.py` hunk is appended at the end of that file, well clear of
#709's insertion point in the workflow-wiring block.
`docs/plan-2026-09-open-issues.md` is untouched. The evidence is not the
distance but the trial merge against #709's head, which is clean (figure
below).

Leaves #533 open — this addresses the notification gap its newest comments
record and none of its coverage tranches. Part of #201.

## The defect the review found in this branch, and the fix

**The check written to stop a nightly failure reaching nobody could itself
report `NIGHTLY PASSED … run conclusion 'failure'` beside exit 0.** The
adversarial review of `97a6d3e` constructed it and executed it. `verdict`
classified a concluded run from `failing_jobs(jobs)` alone and never read
`concluded["conclusion"]`, so **all nine non-`success` run conclusions returned
`PASSED` exit 0** whenever every job the jobs endpoint listed read `success` or
`skipped`. That is a warning printed next to a clean exit — the exact shape the
"WHY A RED CHECK AND NOT A WARNING INSIDE A GREEN JOB" section above argues
against by name, printed about itself. It is the defect this whole file exists
to prevent, in the file.

Five fixes, in the order the review ranked them. Every one carries a check that
is shown failing on the defect and passing on the fix, both runs pasted below.

1. **`verdict` reads the run's own conclusion, and it is authoritative.** The
   job list refines it. The **whole** non-passing vocabulary is refused, not
   only what CI has produced: the backtests below found `failure` and nothing
   else, and `cancelled`, `timed_out`, `action_required` and `stale` are absent
   from the observed population entirely. Untested is not cleared, and a hole no
   current input reaches is still a hole in a check whose entire job is to not
   lie. A design choice, and said out loud in the code so a later reader meets
   it as a tightening rather than a defect.
2. **`pick_runs`'s ordering is pinned.** Replacing its `sorted(...)` with
   `list(runs)` left **all 1236 checks passing** at `97a6d3e`; nothing in the
   suite called `pick_runs`, `collect` or `_jobs`, and only `verdict` was
   driven. The sort its docstring justifies most loudly — "an order that is
   documented but not asserted is one an API change silently reverses" — was
   pinned by nothing.
3. **A run with no `created_at` is `UNREADABLE` (exit 2).** It raised `KeyError`
   from `r["created_at"]`, which is not what `main`'s `except Unreadable`
   catches, so `sys.exit(main())` printed a traceback and exited **1**. Red
   rather than falsely green, so not urgent — but exit 1 is this reporter's word
   for "the nightly FAILED", and the truth was "could not look", which is what
   exit 2 is for.
4. **`_jobs` compares the received `total_count` to `len(jobs)`** and fails
   closed when they differ. It requested one page of 100, followed no `Link`
   header, and received `total_count` without ever using it, so a run's overflow
   jobs — including any failing one — would have been dropped in silence, and a
   dropped failing job is a PASS. Comparing two integers is cheaper than
   pagination and removes the silent case rather than the limit. The refusal is
   unreachable today because no run of this workflow comes near a hundred jobs —
   **the rule for that, not a count**, is under `## Figures`; a count moves
   whenever a job or a matrix arm is added, and the first draft of this pull
   request carried one that was already stale by one.
5. **The staleness boundary matches its own comment.** `MAX_AGE_NIGHTS`'s
   comment said "three is the first age that cannot be either of those" while
   the code was `nights > 3`, needing **four** nights of silence and reading a
   three-night gap as `PASSED`. The constant moved to 2 rather than the
   comparison, because `> max_age_nights` is the reading the flag name
   `--max-age-nights` already promises.

**And the fixture encoded the defect.** `_ns_run`'s default was
`conclusion="failure"`, so every state case in `tests/entities.py` was silently
a run that had *failed* — and every one of them still read `PASSED`. That is why
no check here caught it. The default is now `"success"`, the ordinary nightly,
and each case varies one property and leaves the rest ordinary.

## Head

`ed5e6fde97921f599f62583a76f3fc19855aeade`

The review's measuring surface was `97a6d3e`, and this head is that plus two
commits. **No rebase and no merge**, so `fixer.md` step 6's re-execution trigger
fires on the new commits' own evidence rather than on a moved base.

- `8d6ab48` — the five fixes above and their checks, in
  `tests/nightly_status.py` and `tests/entities.py` and nowhere else. Steps 2–4
  were executed there: five mutations, the before/after runs of the classifier
  end to end, the live arm at both ends, the backtest at both ends, the
  gate-scope derivation and the structure ratchet. **Every check at `8d6ab48`
  concluded `success` or `skipped` except `nightly-status`**, which is the
  countermeasure reporting the genuinely failed 2026-09-10 nightly and is
  answered under `## Red checks`. Read them with `--paginate` and `filter=all`.
- `ed5e6fd` — **comments only**, correcting a jobs-per-run figure that was stale
  when it was written; the correction and its measurement are under
  `## Figures`. It changes no behaviour: `ALL 1243 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED`,
  `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`, `ALL 2 typing-ruler source checks PASSED`, all
  re-run at this head. The mutation arms and the before/after runs above are
  quoted from `8d6ab48` and are not re-executed here, because a comment cannot
  move them — and that is stated rather than implied, because "re-run at the
  head" is a claim and this is the honest scope of it.

Everything below that names `97a6d3e` or `9893ee3` is explicitly anchored there
and says why.

Three-dot against `e50aa51`, this branch changes six files:
`.github/workflows/tests.yml`, `tests/closure.py`, `tests/closures.json`,
`tests/entities.py`, `tests/nightly_status.py`, `tests/run.sh`. Nothing else,
and `docs/plan-2026-09-open-issues.md` is untouched — this pull request's
disposition is #718's row.

## Mutation proof

### The five checks this repair round added: failing on the defect, passing on the fix

**`fixer.md` step 2's order, executed in that order.** The checks were written
and run FIRST, against `tests/nightly_status.py` exactly as `97a6d3e` left it —

## Cost test

`defect-root-cause.mdc`'s form, both sides in wall-clock per occurrence over a
release cycle.

**`cost(countermeasure, recurring)`** — one `nightly-status` job per
pull-request run, forever, measured on this PR's own first push at **7 seconds
end to end** (figure above). Two GitHub API GETs. The job runs concurrently with
`fast` (23 minutes on that same push), `browser`, `typing` and `closures`, and it
is not a required context, so **no pull request waits on it**: the wall-clock it
adds to a merge is zero and the cost is one runner allocation of seven seconds.
At the measured volume — 807 pull-request runs in seven days — that is ~1614 API
calls a week against `GITHUB_TOKEN`'s 1000/hour per-repository budget, about
0.7 % of one hour's allowance spread over a week, and ~94 runner-minutes a week
in a matrix that already spends far more than that on a single run.

**`cost(defect) × P(recurrence)`** — the observed occurrence: the lane first
failed on the run created 2026-09-09T07:25Z and the diagnosis was posted
2026-09-10T08:03Z, a detection latency of about **24.6 h from the second
failing night and 48.6 h from the first**, and it took a seat sent looking
rather than any signal. Four tranches merged on 2026-09-09 without the lane's
answer. With this check the latency is bounded by the next pull-request run:
115/day at the measured volume, so minutes. `P(recurrence)` uses the measured
class frequency rather than an estimate — 6 of the last 12 completed scheduled
runs concluded other than `success` (rule and command above), and **none of them
is a required context**, so every one of those was a conclusion nobody was told
about.

Seven seconds of a parallel runner, adding zero to any merge, against ~24–48 h
of undetected darkness at roughly a 50 % per-night rate. The countermeasure
pays.

**The bound.** It degrades nothing: no production file is touched, no structural
budget moves (`tests/structure.py` measures
`custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/**/*.py` only, and passed unchanged), and
no existing check is loosened. The complexity added is one stdlib module and one
job.

**What it deliberately does not do.** It does not file, close or comment on an
issue, does not write anywhere, and holds no write scope. The rejected
auto-filing design's standing false-positive cost — an issue filed for a
registry outage — becomes here a red check that blocks nothing and says in its
own text that it blocks nothing.

Only because it changes what the fixer must do next.
