Both restored, `md5` verified, `ALL 25 typing-ruler checks PASSED` after.

## The census composition, and the halt condition you were given

**The substitution is sound, and it is strictly stronger than what it replaced** — I checked rather than deferred. "Stop if the resolved census is not `main`'s number" is unsatisfiable in the direction you meant: the branch removes 29 errors, so the resolved census can equal 220 only if the branch's work were lost, and the condition fires on every correct outcome. The composition check reduces to yours when the branch delta is zero and is checkable per row rather than in total:

```
RESULT head[code] == newbase[code] + (branch[code] - oldbase[code]) for EVERY code: True
RESULT 220 - 29 = 191
```

I ran the second half from the other direction too, which the fixer's version does not: the `by_module` comparison shows the ten batch modules and only those moving. Per-code identity plus per-module attribution closes it from both ends — nothing of `main`'s absorbed, nothing of the branch's given back. That the row **sets** are not disjoint (finding 2) does not weaken it; the identity holds on `arg-type` as well.

## The claim-file anomaly — a hazard to record, not something to resolve before merging, and I think I found the mechanism

**State first, by hash.** Both files are the *same blob* at the base, at `main` and at the head: `claimed_drift.txt` `39cd6f4…`, `card_claimed_drift.txt` `e401dc6…`. The branch claims nothing.

**Why no correct path produces the reported outcome.** At the three-way base `c9dfec7` both files are byte-identical to the branch at `242e60a`, and `main` changed both. That is the trivial case: base == ours, so git resolves it without calling any merge driver at all and takes theirs — which is why no `MERGE-CLAIM:` line was expected. And if the driver *had* run, `merge_claim_file` hits `if base == ours: return theirs`. I drove it by hand on the three real blobs:

```
=== claimed_drift        O==A? YES   MERGE-CLAIM: resolved   exit=0   result == theirs(main)? YES
=== card_claimed_drift   O==A? YES   MERGE-CLAIM: resolved   exit=0   result == theirs(main)? YES
```

Neither git's path nor the driver's can yield "ours for one, a third blob for the other". I checked the obvious replay mechanism and it is not there: `rerere.enabled` unset locally and globally, no `.git/rr-cache`.

**The mechanism, and I hit it myself in this review.** My *first* attempt at the by-hand drive above wrote `git show $BASE3:tests/golden/…` unbraced in zsh, which applied the `:t` history modifier to the parameter and silently produced an **empty** `%O`. With an empty base the driver stops taking the trivial branch, unions the comments, and emits **a third blob that is neither side** — the exact shape reported, with `MERGE-CLAIM: resolved` rather than a refusal:

```
=== claimed_drift  O==A? NO   MERGE-CLAIM: resolved  exit=0
  result md5 a03c42f1…  main md5 d2cd0944…  base md5 d41d8cd9… (empty)   result == main? NO
```

That is a reproducible way for a *probe* to report a mis-merge that never happened, on these two files, in this repository, in a zsh seat. It is not proof of what happened here — I have no shell history from that attempt and I say so plainly — but it is a concrete mechanism where there was none, and it is more parsimonious than nondeterminism in git.

**Disposition.** Record it; do not hold the merge. The outcome is verified correct three independent ways (blob identity against `main`, `merge-tree` whole-tree agreement, the driver driven by hand), and no value-bearing decision was ever at stake in this merge because base == ours on both files. Blocking would ask this branch to resolve a defect nobody can show exists. What I would not do is let it go unrecorded: `docs/HANDOVER.md` is the right home, framed as *"a claim-file probe that reads `git show $REF:path` unquoted in zsh returns an empty blob and the driver then unions"* rather than as *"git mis-merged once"*, because the second is not established and the first is.

## Also verified

nodes.title: fix(#533): the blocking call the nightly lane saw was the atexit backstop, not the offload
nodes.body:
The `nightly-ha` lane read Home Assistant's own loop-protection report against
`custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/coordinator.py`'s `worker.wait(timeout=2)`.
`_shutdown_process_pool` has two call sites and neither is a naive on-loop call —
`atexit.register` and `await hass.async_add_executor_job(...)` — so the obvious
diagnosis is wrong and the fix depends on which one fired.

**The `atexit` path fired.** Three independent facts from the container log of
run `34453886319`, job `102795656071` (tree `ee1058a`), and from Home Assistant
2026.9.1's own source:

1. The warning's stack has exactly **one** frame. `homeassistant/util/loop.py`
   ends the report with `traceback.format_stack(f=integration_frame.frame)`,
   which walks `f_back` to the outermost frame, so the printed stack is the
   offender's *callers*. One frame means `_shutdown_process_pool` had no Python
   caller — it was invoked from C, and `atexit` is the only C-level invoker of
   it in this tree:

   ```
   2026-09-10 10:13:56.282 WARNING (MainThread) [homeassistant.util.loop] Detected
   blocking call to sleep with args (0.001,) inside the event loop by custom
   integration 'heatpump_optimizer' at custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/
   coordinator.py, line 832: worker.wait(timeout=2) (offender: /usr/local/lib/
   python3.14/subprocess.py, line 2078: time.sleep(delay)), please create a bug
   report at https://github.com/tvofi/heatpump_optimizer/issues
   For developers, please see https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/asyncio_blocking_operations/#sleep
   Traceback (most recent call last):
     File "/config/custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/coordinator.py", line 832, in _shutdown_process_pool
       worker.wait(timeout=2)
   ```

   The three other reports in the same log — all from `nightly_ha.py`'s host
   half — print their full stack from `<module>` down, so a one-frame stack is
   this record's own discriminator, not how it always prints.
2. The record's thread is `MainThread`. `hass.async_add_executor_job` runs its
   callable on an executor thread, so the offload call site cannot produce this
   line.
3. It is logged at `10:13:56.282`, **after** `asyncio.run(_inside(...))` had
   already unwound and `sys.exit(main())`'s uncaught `CancelledError` had been
   reported — i.e. during interpreter teardown.

**Why it is reported at all, with no loop left to block.**
`homeassistant.util.loop.protect_loop` fires on
`threading.get_ident() == loop_thread_id` — the id `block_async_io.enable()`
records at startup — and never asks whether a loop is still running. `atexit`
handlers run on that thread. So the honest statement of harm is not loop
starvation: nothing is being served at interpreter exit. The harm is that Home
Assistant tells the user to open a bug against this repository. Which exits
reach it follows from the two call sites rather than from an enumeration of
exits: the backstop returns early when the stop listener already reaped
(`_PROCESS_WORKER` is `None`), so what is left is an exit that runs `atexit`
with a worker still alive — the container's crash here, and in an installation
a stop that never fired, including an entry removed before it, since
`async_on_unload` drops #525's listener with the entry.

**The fix.** The backstop stays registered and still reaps; only its wait
changes. `Popen.wait(timeout=...)` polls with `time.sleep`; `Popen.wait()` with
no timeout reaps through `os.waitpid`, which blocks in C. `SIGKILL` goes first,
so that wait is bounded by something a child cannot ignore. Nothing is lost by
not asking politely there: `stdin` is already closed above, which is the
worker's own clean exit (`process_worker.run_worker` returns on EOF), and it
holds no file, lock or buffer a `SIGTERM` would let it flush. The loop-side reap
keeps its graceful `terminate` and two-second wait unchanged.

**`KNOWN_BLOCKING` was the wrong route here** even though `defect-root-cause.md`
allows it in principle. Its key is (call, file, source snippet), and this is the
same line an on-loop route would report — an entry would mask the #525 class at
exactly the site the pin exists to watch.

**No closing keyword.** #525 is closed and this is a new site, not its
regression. #533 is broader than this — A6 and A11–A13 are unimplemented, and
two further defects from the same run belong to other seats: the second
container invocation (`--a3e-only`) emits no result marker, and
`log:blocking_positive_control` reports it cannot see inside its probe window,
so #588's control is unreadable. Neither is touched here.

**There is no Docker on the machine this was written on, so nothing was
reproduced locally in a container.** Every container figure below comes from a
dispatched lane run.

## Head

`45a16d310ebe6c2745a4cd84880c47471d70765a`, merge base
`e50aa51b69bca2b4318b21f666820ec5dc51f1ab`.

The lane figures are measured at `3a46cc30e61bde7c0605f71ada7e92a57efdd531` on
the throwaway branch `claude/shutdown-blocking-lane-demo`, which is this
branch's two code commits cherry-picked onto `ee1058a`, the head of the open PR
#709. That detour is forced: #709 is **not merged**, and the `nightly-ha` job on
`main` is four steps — checkout, setup-python, `docker pull`, `python
tests/nightly_ha.py` — with no install of `tests/requirements-ci.txt`, which is
what #709 adds; the same run's log shows the driver's host half importing the
package. I did not dispatch it at this branch to watch that fail, so the claim
is read off the workflow and #709, not measured. `ee1058a` against
`ee1058a` plus these commits is the tighter comparison in any case — one diff,
same image, same day. The branch exists for the review and can be deleted after
it.

## Mutation proof

Both mutations were applied to the fix's predicate, run, and reverted;
`md5 -q custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/coordinator.py` prints
`389724fccd510f0d453ee13f14b2b98e` before and after each, and
`git status --porcelain` is empty at the end.

Each mutation fails the same two checks under
`PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/features.py`:

- `what atexit will call reaps without a polling wait (#533)`
- `and the child is dead and reaped, not abandoned (#533)`

1. `atexit.register(_shutdown_process_pool, at_exit=True)` →
   `atexit.register(_shutdown_process_pool)`: registration survives, the
   registered callable takes the polling route. `2 of 2121 FEATURE CHECKS
   FAILED`, 39 `time.sleep` calls totalling 1.707 s, child `returncode None`.
2. The `at_exit` branch's `worker.kill(); worker.wait()` →
   `worker.terminate(); worker.wait(timeout=2)`: registration is right and the
   branch body is wrong. `2 of 2121 FEATURE CHECKS FAILED`, 39 calls totalling
   1.712 s, child `returncode None`.

The second mutation is why the check is written against *what `atexit` was
handed* rather than against `_shutdown_process_pool` directly: a test that
called the function itself would survive mutation 1.

## Null control

- **The probe.** `what atexit will call reaps without a polling wait (#533)`
  measures the absence of `time.sleep`, which is also what a probe that never
  looked would report. `null control: the graceful reap DOES poll, so the probe
  can see polling` runs the same measurement over the loop-side reap — which
  keeps its polling wait, and must — and requires the sleeps to be there. It is
  `ok` at the merge base and at the head.
- **The reap still happens.** `and the child is dead and reaped, not abandoned
  (#533)` requires a negative `returncode`, so a "fix" that made the report go
  away by not shutting the worker down fails it. Both checks also assert the
  child was **alive when the reap began** (`child alive at the start: True` in
  the detail), because a child that had already died would make "no sleeps" true
  of a reap that reaped nothing.
- **The lane.** The container took the identical route in both runs: the same
  `_async_check_a5_options` `CancelledError`, the same two `Optimization
  complete ... status=optimal` lines — so a worker existed to reap in both — and
  the same abnormal exit through `sys.exit(main())`. The other five failing
  checks are unchanged between the runs. The report's disappearance is the diff,
  not the run having gone somewhere else.
- **The inherited-claims refusal is not this diff.** See Figures: at the merge
  base with an unrelated one-line committed diff, the same command passes.
  `env_drift`'s guard runs only when the diff `moves_claimable`, so a claimable
  diff is its precondition, not anything this change does to a fixture.

## Figures

- `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/features.py` at `fe3a1e9` (the
  test-only commit, on the merge base): `2 of 2121 FEATURE CHECKS FAILED` — the
  two checks named under Mutation proof, with `40 time.sleep call(s) totalling
  1.737s` and `returncode after the backstop ran: None`.
- The same command at the head: `ALL 2121 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED`. The
  population is 2121 at both ends; the rule is that this branch adds four checks
  to `tests/features.py` and removes none, and `features.py` prints the total at
  each end.
- `python3 tests/structure.py` at the merge base and at the head, compared over
  the budgeted-metric lines the instrument prints:
  `diff <(grep '^  ok ' base.txt) <(grep '^  ok ' head.txt) && echo IDENTICAL` —
  IDENTICAL. No ratchet movement, no re-record, no raise requested. The
  production change is module-level, outside `COORDINATOR_CLASS_NAME`, so the
  coordinator rows cannot move; the whole-tree rows are covered by the same
  comparison.
- `D=$(mktemp -d); python3 tests/closure.py select --diff $(git merge-base
  origin/main HEAD) --workdir "$D"; cat "$D/scope.txt"` →
  `MODE: SCOPED -- 13 script(s) run, 8 scoped out.` `tools/audit/briefs/fixer.md`
  is INERT (`tests/closure.py`'s `INERT`), so the carry does not change the
  selection: `diff` of `scope.run` before and after that commit is empty.
- `GATE_SCOPE=auto GOLDEN_MODE=drift GOLDEN_REF=$(git merge-base origin/main
  HEAD) ./tests/run.sh` → `2 TEST SCRIPT(S) FAILED`, and both are the same
  script: `tests/env_drift.py`, once as `--claims-only` and once as `--all`,
  both on `INHERITED CLAIMS` — true of merge base `e50aa51`, and not of CI's
  base; see Red checks. `tests/stress.py` is not in the selection, so no gate
  lease was taken. Every other script the selection named passed.
- In a worktree detached at `e50aa51` carrying one committed unrelated line,
  `python3 tests/env_drift.py --claims-only e50aa51...` exits 0:
  `claims hygiene: ... ok`. `check_claims_hygiene` reaches
  `inherited_claims_error` only when `moves_claimable(changed)`.
- With the single `config_flow` claim line removed from
  `tests/golden/claimed_drift.txt` in the **working tree** — the repair
  `claims-autofix` makes, not committed here —
  `python3 tests/env_drift.py --all e50aa51...` exits 0:
  `NO UNCLAIMED DRIFT: 55 scenario(s) checked` and `NO STALE FIXTURE: 55
  committed fixture(s) still match what this tree computes`. So this change
  moves no fixture, and the emptied list will not be excusing anything.
- `git diff origin/main...HEAD -- tests/golden/claimed_drift.txt
  tests/golden/card_claimed_drift.txt` prints nothing: both claim files are
  byte-identical to `origin/main`, three-dot.
- `git diff origin/main...HEAD -- VERSION
  custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/manifest.json RELEASE_NOTES.md` prints
  nothing.
- **The lane, both ends, both matrix arms.** `log:no_new_blocking_call`, read
  from the job logs with
  `gh api /repos/tvofi/heatpump_optimizer/actions/jobs/<id>/logs --allow-escape-sequences`:

  | arm | before — run `34453886319` @ `ee1058a` | after — run `34456269514` @ `3a46cc3` |
  |---|---|---|
  | `nightly-ha (stable)` | job `102795656071`: `FAIL log:no_new_blocking_call [1 offender(s) seen; new: [('sleep', 'custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/coordinator.py', 'worker.wait(timeout=2)')]]` | job `102803274073`: `ok log:no_new_blocking_call [0 offender(s) seen; new: []]` |
  | `nightly-ha (2025.2.0)` | job `102795656004`: the same `FAIL`, the same offender tuple | job `102803274187`: the same `ok` |

  Both arms go from `FAILED: 6 of 10 checks` to `FAILED: 5 of 10 checks`, and
  the five that remain are the same five in both runs and in both arms:
  `run:driver_reported`, `run:exit_status`, `log:no_integration_traceback`,
  `log:blocking_positive_control`, `run:all_checks_ran`. None of them is this
  change's and none is touched by it.
- `grep -c "Detected blocking.*coordinator.py"` over the after-run's stable job
  log → `0`. The three reports that remain in it all name `/opt/hpo/nightly_ha.py`,
  the driver's own host half, which is #533's business and not this branch's.

## Red checks

`none`. Every check on `45a16d3` is green, including `fast (3.13)` and
`fast (3.14)`; `claims-autofix` and `closures-autofix` both report `skipped`.

**A correction, because this section first predicted a red that did not
happen.** I wrote that `fast` would fail `INHERITED CLAIMS`, from the local
refusal recorded under Figures. It did not, and the reason is a moved base
rather than a wrong reading of the guard: `main` gained the v6.3.20 stamp
`18d67a2` after this branch's merge base `e50aa51`, the stamp rewrote
`tests/golden/claimed_drift.txt`, and CI measured against `18d67a2` — where
this branch's claim files are no longer identical to the baseline's. The
`fast (3.13)` log shows
`python3 tests/env_drift.py --claims-only 18d67a24... / claims hygiene: ... ok`.
So the guard's precondition is main's claim file, and a stamp dissolves it; the
local figure and the CI figure are both true of their own base.

The prediction was still owed an answer here, and the answer stands if the
condition returns: the cheaper detector exists and is already built —
`claims-autofix` (`.cursor/rules/ci-autofix.mdc`,
`env_drift.apply_inherited_claims`, commit subject `ci: drop inherited claims`).
Per that rule I did not hand-empty the file and did not open a second job.
Standing cost: the job already runs on every same-repo pull request. Read its
summary line, not its tick.

**For whoever merges this**, if a claim ever is dropped by that job on this
branch: a squash of an emptied list deletes `main`'s own claim, the shape
recorded at #608→#569 and again at #635→#633. `env_drift.py`'s comment above
`check_claims_hygiene` records the same trap from #658. It has not happened
here — the job skipped — and it is a merge-time decision rather than a fixer's.

**This branch is one main-merge behind**: `e50aa51` is its merge base and `main`
is now past the v6.3.20 stamp. I did not merge, because the handoff freezes the
branch and a merge re-opens steps 2–4 of the fixer contract; CI has already
measured this head against a base that includes the stamp. Whether to update it
is the orchestrator's call.

## Forward-carry

`tests/nightly_ha.py`, the comment block that `KNOWN_BLOCKING` is declared
under — the artifact where the next pin is decided, and where the claim this
finding falsifies is written. #540's note there said the reap went to
`async_add_executor_job`, so any report would be a new offender; it moved one
of the reap's two routes, and the `atexit` backstop kept its polling wait. The
carry states the mechanism, the discriminator and the control (the `atexit`
route reads identically to an on-loop call because `protect_loop` keys on the
thread id alone), then the precondition: establish the caller before adding an
entry, and add none for a line an on-loop route could also reach.

**`tools/audit/briefs/fixer.md` was the first choice and I did not take it, so
this is a refusal with what refused it.** The role contract is where
`finding-propagation.md` sends a finding that constrains every seat of a role,
and this one does. That file stands at its cap — 257 of 257 lines in
`.claude/workflows/policy_budgets.json`, so `node .claude/workflows/policy_lint.mjs`
refuses any net addition to it. The two routes left are raising the cap, which
`CLAUDE.md` rule 2 refuses when it is done to make a change fit and which needs
the owner's confirmation obtained before the push, and cutting an equal number
of lines of somebody else's binding policy prose to buy the room, which is not a
fixer's call either. The owner's decision, if the lane-side destination is not
enough: raise `fixer.md`'s cap and I will add the step, in a branch of its own.
Measured with `node .claude/workflows/policy_lint.mjs --budgets`, which prints
each file against its cap; with the step drafted in, that command reported the
file over, and `role fixer` and `corpus` still inside theirs.

No wave-group brief received a copy: no open group's brief covers this lane's
remaining tranches, and `docs/plan-2026-09-open-issues.md` — where the plan row
would go — is a record pull request's file, not this one's.

## Friction

`claim-files.md: cost: (transient — it dissolves at the next stamp, see Red checks) a branch that claims nothing must leave both claim files byte-identical to origin/main, and env_drift's inherited-claims guard then refuses that same tree locally on any claimable diff, so fixer.md step 5's "green locally before you push" is unreachable for such a branch and the CI autofix is the only route. env_drift.py's comment above check_claims_hygiene records the contradiction from #658; nothing states the local consequence where a fixer meets it.`

`ratchet-budgets.md: cost: a per-file cap at zero headroom makes the destination finding-propagation.md names unreachable for a fixer, because the only two ways to comply are a cap raise the owner must confirm before the push and a deletion of other policy prose. The rule that names the destination and the rule that prices the file do not meet anywhere, so the seat has to invent the resolution. Evidence: tools/audit/briefs/fixer.md 257 of 257 before this branch touched it.`

Fix review: merge 45a16d310ebe6c2745a4cd84880c47471d70765a

Reviewed adversarially from a detached worktree at `45a16d3`. Head was `45a16d3` when I
started and still is at posting. `origin/main` moved twice under me (`ad55569` → `a1f148a`,
#716); nothing I measured depends on it, and `merge-tree` is clean against both.
**API failures: 0.** (Four initial `gh api` calls were refused by the CLI's escape-sequence
guard, not by the API, and were recovered with `--allow-escape-sequences`.)

## The attribution — attacked at all three arguments, all three survive

I read Home Assistant's own source at the tag the container actually ran. The container
log reports `2026.9.1`, so `2026.9.1` is the tag I read.

**Argument 1 (one frame) — confirmed, and the inference is valid.** Three separate checks:

- `homeassistant/util/loop.py` ends the integration-branch warning with
  `"".join(traceback.format_stack(f=integration_frame.frame))`. Verbatim, as claimed.
- `integration_frame.frame` means what the fixer says. `helpers/frame.py`'s
  `get_integration_frame` starts at `get_current_frame()` and walks `f_back`, taking the
  **innermost** frame under `custom_components/`. So the printed stack is that frame plus
  its callers, and one frame means `_shutdown_process_pool`'s frame had `f_back is None` —
  it was pushed onto an empty thread stack.
- The remaining step is "no Python caller ⟹ `atexit`", which holds only if `atexit` is the
  sole C-level route **in this tree**, which is how the fixer stated it. I checked rather
  than took it: `grep` over `custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/` finds no `__del__`, no
  `weakref`, no finalizer and no signal handler, and `_shutdown_process_pool` has exactly
  two call sites — `atexit.register(..., at_exit=True)` and
  `hass.async_add_executor_job(_shutdown_process_pool)`. Confirmed.

I did not take the body's log excerpt. I fetched job `102795656071`'s raw log myself: the
traceback is **exactly one frame** and is followed by blank lines and the `FAILED: 6 of 10`
summary — not truncated by the fixer.

*One imprecision, not a defect.* The body offers the log's three other reports as "this
record's own discriminator". Those three take the `MissingIntegrationFrame` branch, which
prints `format_stack(f=offender_frame)` — a different `f=` argument. The comparison is
across two message branches, so it is looser than the body implies. The substance survives
untouched, because `format_stack`'s outward walk is the same function in both: I read one
of those three and it prints from `<module>` through `sys.exit(main())` → `asyncio.run` →
`run_until_complete`, which is precisely the caller chain the #533 record does not have.

**Argument 2 (`MainThread`) — confirmed** in the raw log.

**Argument 3 (timing) — confirmed** in the raw log. The report at `10:13:56.282` follows
the `asyncio.exceptions.CancelledError` traceback ending in
`_async_check_a5_options`/`async_block_till_done`; the earlier reports still show
`asyncio.run` on the stack and the #533 one does not.

**The "why reported with no loop left" reasoning — confirmed.** `protect_loop` is
`if threading.get_ident() == loop_thread_id:` and never asks whether a loop is running.

## `KNOWN_BLOCKING`: the rejection is right, and I checked the thing that decides it

The key is the 3-tuple, confirmed from the harness's own failure detail:
`('sleep', 'custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/coordinator.py', 'worker.wait(timeout=2)')`
— no thread, no caller, no line number. An entry would be indistinguishable from the same
line reached from a coroutine, and #525 is exactly that class at exactly that site. Masking
it is real, not rhetorical.

What separates "exactly right" from "a convenient way to avoid a simpler fix" is whether
the fix the rejection forces actually removes the report rather than relocating it, and
the fixer did not check that. I did: HA's `_BLOCKING_CALLS` list wraps `putrequest`,
`sleep`, `glob`, `iglob`, `walk`, `listdir`, `scandir`, `open`, `import_module`, four ssl
loaders and five `Path` methods — **no `os.kill`, no `os.waitpid`**. So `worker.kill()` and
a timeout-less `worker.wait()` are genuinely unprotected. The rejection stands.

**Something the body understates rather than overstates.** `time.sleep` is registered
`strict=True`, so `raise_for_blocking_call` **raises** after logging. The old
`worker.wait(timeout=2)` therefore raised into the surrounding `except Exception`, and on
the `atexit` path the child was never reaped at all. The harm was worse than "the report is
the harm". A conservative claim, which is the right direction to be wrong in.

## Re-executed, not accepted

- **Both ends, my own runs.** `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/features.py` at the
  test-only commit `fe3a1e9`: `2 of 2121 FEATURE CHECKS FAILED`, the two named checks
  (`39 time.sleep call(s) totalling 1.712s`, `returncode None`). At `45a16d3`:
  `ALL 2121 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED`. Population: the diff adds 4 `R.check(` and removes 0.
- **Both mutations, re-applied by me.** M1 (drop `at_exit=True`) → `2 of 2121`, same two
  checks, 39 sleeps / 1.711s. M2 (restore `terminate()` + `wait(timeout=2)` inside the
  branch) → `2 of 2121`, same two checks, 40 sleeps / 1.757s. `md5 -q coordinator.py`
  back to `389724fccd510f0d453ee13f14b2b98e` after each; `git status --porcelain` empty.
  **Not vacuous.**
- **A third mutation of my own**, to test a route the fixer's two do not: delete
  `atexit.register` outright — the "make the report go away by not registering" fix. It
  fails `starting the worker still registers an atexit backstop (#533)` with
  `registered: []`. The check set is not one-sided.
- **Null control** re-run as part of both end runs: `null control: the graceful reap DOES
  poll, so the probe can see polling` is `ok` at both ends, so the probe is not blind.
- **The finder's harness, all four jobs, logs fetched and re-read by me.** Both matrix arms
  go `FAIL log:no_new_blocking_call [1 offender(s) seen; ...]` → `ok [0 offender(s) seen;
  new: []]`, and `6 of 10` → `5 of 10`. The five that remain are identical strings in both
  runs and both arms — `run:driver_reported`, `run:exit_status`,
  `log:no_integration_traceback`, `log:blocking_positive_control`, `run:all_checks_ran` —
  and none is this change's. `Detected blocking.*coordinator.py` goes 1 → 0; total reports
  4 → 3. This is step 6's "other configurations": the image-tag matrix is the axis the
  finder's harness accepts, and both arms move.
- **A control stronger than the one offered.** The body offers route identity. I also
  compared the image: both runs pulled `Digest: sha256:612d76760b544cb40b7ba01387fdac964c59a6a550a50a4d30b4773c822d2918`.
  Same image, same route markers, one diff.
- **Lane-demo provenance.** `3a46cc3` = `ee1058a` + the two code commits; its
  `coordinator.py` diff is textually identical to the PR's apart from hunk offsets and
  blob hashes.
- **Ratchet.** `structure.py` passes at `e50aa51` and at head;
  `diff <(grep '^  ok ') <(grep '^  ok ')` → IDENTICAL. No movement, no re-record, no raise.
- **Scope.** `MODE: SCOPED -- 13 script(s) run, 8 scoped out.` As stated.
- **`VERSION`, manifest, `RELEASE_NOTES.md`** — three-dot diff empty.
- **Claim files** — three-dot diff empty; branch claims nothing.
- **Conflict, measured not inferred.** Merge driver installed; `git merge-tree
  --write-tree origin/main 45a16d3` exits 0 against both `ad55569` and `a1f148a`, stderr
  empty — no conflicting path, so the driver was never invoked. I also inspected the merged
  tree: `VERSION` 6.3.20, both claim files `claims-for: 6.3.20`, the `config_flow` line
  gone (main's stamp wins), and both of this branch's changes present.
- **`--all` figure reproduced exactly** under the fixer's stated working-tree edit:
  `NO UNCLAIMED DRIFT: 55 scenario(s) checked`, `NO STALE FIXTURE: 55`. Tree restored clean.

## The `INHERITED CLAIMS` correction is accurate

Reproduced both halves. `env_drift.py --claims-only e50aa51b69...` → `INHERITED CLAIMS`,
exit 1. `--claims-only 18d67a246b...` → `claims hygiene: ... ok`, exit 0. The `fast (3.13)`
job log shows CI invoking the bare SHA `18d67a246ba648fc1d9bb4212ab8d3122a6a3b26` and
getting `ok`. `18d67a2` is the v6.3.20 stamp and its diff deletes the `config_flow` claim
line. The prediction was wrong for exactly the stated reason, and both figures are true of
their own base.

One wording note: Figures says the claim files are "byte-identical to `origin/main`,
three-dot". The three-dot command is the right one and its conclusion (this branch claims
nothing) is right, but the files are *not* byte-identical to main's current content — the
stamp rewrote both. The body's own Red-checks section states this correctly, so the
imprecision is confined to one line.

## Red checks

Read from the commit's `check-runs` API, fully paginated, not `gh pr checks`: **28 runs,
`total_count` 28, agreeing.** Every conclusion is `success` or `skipped`; no `failure`,
`cancelled` or `timed_out`, and no hidden red-then-green (five check names appear twice and
all ten runs are green). `fe3a1e9` and `ecb0227` carry zero check-runs. So
`defect-root-cause.md`'s Enforcement trigger has nothing to bite on, and `## Red checks:
none` is accurate.

## Forward-carry — adequate, and the refusal is substantiated

I opened the destination and read it back. It is in the tree, sits directly above the
`KNOWN_BLOCKING` declaration it governs, and carries the mechanism, the discriminator, the
control (`protect_loop` keys on the thread id alone) and the precondition in the imperative
— "Establish the caller before adding an entry below, and add none for a line an on-loop
route could also reach" — not the opportunity. It names run `34453886319` for
re-measurement. Under `finding-propagation.md`'s own test — where the seat who needs this
will be looking — a seat deciding a `KNOWN_BLOCKING` entry is by construction in that file.
This is propagation, not a note filed somewhere convenient.

I checked the alternative destinations rather than taking the refusal:

- `tools/audit/briefs/fixer.md` is **257 of 257** in `policy_budgets.json`, confirmed with
  `node .claude/workflows/policy_lint.mjs --budgets`. The per-file line cap is the binding
  constraint; `role fixer` has ~14 tokens spare and `corpus` more. Declining to raise it
  without the owner's confirmation is correct under CLAUDE.md rule 2.
- No open group brief covers this lane's remaining tranches. I searched all four
  `wave-*-groups.json`; the only `#533` hit is W5-G7, a `#195` typing group whose #533 text
  is older context carried from the record branch, not work that will decide a pin.

**The residual gap, stated because it is real.** The *general* lesson — a loop-protection
report is not by itself proof of an on-loop call — is what would constrain any fixer seat,
and it now lives only in a lane-specific test file. A seat meeting the same report on a
different file will not find it. That is disclosed in the body, priced with a measurement I
reproduced, and left as an explicit owner decision. It is short of ideal; it is not
`carry-missing`.

## The lane caveat

Honest and adequately labelled. The measured comparison is `ee1058a` against `ee1058a` plus
this diff — one diff, same image digest, same day — which is the tighter comparison, and
the unmeasured part (what a branch off `main` would do before #709 lands) is named as read
off the workflow rather than measured. Not a gap that blocks.

## Notes for the merger, neither blocking

1. `worker.wait()` with no timeout is unbounded if the child is unkillable — SIGKILL does
   not reap a process in uninterruptible sleep. The old code had a 2-second bound. For a
   solver worker on pipes and CPU this is remote, and the fixer's "bounded by something a
   child cannot ignore" is the standard argument, but the change does trade a bounded noisy
   wait for an unbounded silent one at interpreter exit.
2. The branch is behind `main` by the v6.3.20 stamp and now #716. The stamp touches only
   version strings and the claim files; this branch touches `coordinator.py`,
   `features.py`, `nightly_ha.py`. Disjoint, and the merged tree is self-consistent as
   verified above. Whether to update the branch stays the orchestrator's call.

## What I could not establish

The container lane itself — there is no Docker on this machine, the same limit the fixer
disclosed. I read the finder's harness in `tests/nightly_ha.py` and re-read all four job
logs from the API instead of executing it, so every lane figure above is a re-reading of a
measured run, not a re-execution. And nobody, including me, has measured `main`'s own
`nightly-ha` lane before #709 merges.

nodes.title: record: rows for the three nightly-programme pull requests, written before their merges
nodes.body:
Three open pull requests had no Delivery-status disposition row. `checkRecord`
enumerates every merge on `main` regardless of who opened it, so a merge without
a row reddens `record` for everyone — which happened twice today already, on
#693 and #695, both mine.

**Why a record branch rather than a row in each pull request.** #714 carries a
`merge` verdict at a frozen head. Writing its row into its own branch would move
that head and void the verdict under `fix-review.md`. #713 and #715 are still in
review, where the same freeze applies. A record branch is the only shape that
satisfies both the disposition rule and the freeze.

## Head

`c99559c2f09a820a8090b2858702d26ad3425d1d`

## Mutation proof

The rows are the deliverable, so the mutation is a row's absence. Both arms were
run as a **simulated merge**, because `--record` resolves `origin/main` and a
branch-head run measures a history this branch is not in — it prints the same
figure with or without the self-row, which is exactly the vacuous evidence a
reviewer caught in the first draft of this body.

Method: `git commit-tree <tree> -p origin/main -m "<squash subject> (#718)"`,
that commit checked out in a throwaway **clone** with `refs/remotes/origin/main`
repointed at it. `commit-tree`, not `commit --allow-empty`, which no-ops without
an author identity. The tree must be **checked out**, not merely referenced —
`checkRecord` reads the plan document from the working tree, so repointing the
ref alone changes nothing and produces a null control that cannot move. A clone
rather than a worktree because `refs/remotes/origin/main` is shared across every
worktree of this repository, and other seats are reading it.

**Two windows, and only one of them is the gate's.** `--record` takes `--since`,
and the `record` job derives it as
`git describe --tags --abbrev=0 --match 'v*'`. `v6.3.20` was stamped today, so
**the window CI actually measures is `v6.3.20..origin/main`**, which the
simulation resolves to 4 merged pull requests. `v6.3.19..origin/main` is the
wider window a previous draft of this body quoted as if it were the gate's; it
is 29 merged pull requests, it is conservative rather than authoritative, and it
is reported below beside the real one rather than in place of it. The control
moves under both.

## Null control

The tree of `8593f15` — the three rows for #713, #714 and #715 present, this
pull request's own row absent — under the identical simulated merge.


reachable from `c08528b`, so CI's window is `v6.3.20..origin/main` — 4 merges, not 29. I ran
that arm too:

```
TREATMENT  --since v6.3.20   RECORD: 4 merged ...; 0 without a disposition   TOTAL: 0 error(s)
NULL       --since v6.3.20   RECORD: 4 merged ...; 1 without a disposition   TOTAL: 1 error(s)
```

The control moves in both windows, and `v6.3.20..main` is a subset of `v6.3.19..main`, so your
wider window is conservative rather than wrong. Worth correcting in the body anyway: a reader
will take `v6.3.19..origin/main` for what the gate measures.

## The four rows against their sources

**#713 — corrected clause verified, and the correction is right.** "buys latency rather than
prevention" is verbatim from the root-cause seat's own product, #533 comment `5616087353`:
*"It buys latency, not prevention, at the price of a permissions widening. **Refused for this
defect.**"* Your note that the standing false-positive cost came from a different comment is
also right — it is #533 comment `5615432026`, a separate and earlier one. The `contents: read`
floor detail comes from #713's body; combining the two is fair and both halves are true. The
mechanism sentences all match #713's body, and I independently confirmed `nightly-ha` and
`slow` are absent from the 18 required contexts and appear `skipped` at every head here.

**#714 — verified, every clause.** `coordinator.py:832` ✅; "three independent legs" ✅ ("Three
independent facts"); the one-frame stack ✅; kills first and waits without a timeout through
`os.waitpid` instead of polling with `time.sleep` ✅ (near-verbatim); loop-side reap keeps its
graceful `terminate` ✅; `KNOWN_BLOCKING` key carrying no thread and no caller ✅ (source: key is
`(call, file, source snippet)`); "both lane arms move from one offender to zero" ✅ (`1
offender(s) seen` → `0 offender(s) seen`, both arms, jobs named in the table); the review's
*understates* finding ✅ verbatim from comment `5616367462`, which is also the `merge` verdict
your body relies on for the freeze.

**#715 — the number is sourced, the method clause is not.** "13 pull requests in two days" is
real, but it is **not** in #715 and not in #678. It is on #201, comment `5615873268`:
*"Measured properly it is 13 pull requests over two days by one unit, 9 failing check-runs
today by another."* Two things follow:

- **"measured at their current heads" I could not source anywhere.** #678's cost test says *"at
  the merged head"*; #201 states no method. Round one asked for a unit; the repair supplied the
  unit correctly and then added a measurement claim no source makes. Per step 8 I am reporting
  it unverified rather than confirmed. Cut it, or cite where it was measured.
- **#715's own body still says "recurred six times on 2026-09-10"**, which #201 says was "wrong
  three ways". Your row is *more* accurate than the PR it describes. That is a finding for #715,
  not a defect here — but the disagreement should not be left standing.

The rest of the row is verified: `blocked` verdict wording matches comment `5616253641`
near-verbatim; the repair round with the self-test case is in the body's own `FAIL` lines; and
**zero line headroom is real** — `policy_budgets.json` caps `fixer.md` at 257 and
`orchestrator.md` at 370, and both files are at exactly 257 and 370 at this head. "One sentence
each" is slightly loose (source: one sentence in `fixer.md` step 5, one *clause* in
`orchestrator.md` section 1); substantively right.

**#718 — verified.** All three subjects are `open`, so `checkRecord` genuinely cannot see them,
exactly as your `## Null control` now says. #714 does carry a `merge` verdict at a frozen head.

## Friction: I agree with the key, not with the sentence under it

`frictionIds` on the live body returns `["delivery-status-tracking"]` — the reclass works.

**The attribution is right and `fixer.md` would be wrong.** `delivery-status-tracking.md` line
22 is the sentence that makes a falsifiable claim — *"so it costs no extra PR"*. `fixer.md`'s
freeze makes no claim about cost; it is a correct rule that has one. Charge the rule that is
wrong, not the rule that is expensive.

**But the evidence sentence is wrong about three of its four instances**, and the contradiction
is in the file this PR edits:

- #708 — *"Twice this evening a pull request merged before its disposition existed — #693 and
  #695 — because four parallel seats..."* → parallelism, not the freeze.
- #711 — *"leftover #692 still said in review after #710 landed"* → the row's truth changed **at
  the merge**; #710 was already merged and could not carry it. Not the freeze.
- #717 — same shape against #716. Not the freeze.
- #718 — the freeze. ✅

So "each existing only because `fixer.md`'s handoff freezes a branch" is true of one of four.
The honest generalisation is stronger for you, not weaker: *a row's truth changes at the merge,
and the branch whose merge changes it cannot always carry it* — of which the freeze is one case.
That makes `delivery-status-tracking` even more clearly the right key.

## Everything else

- **Three-dot diff: your claim checks out, including the part about deletions.** One file, four
  insertions, zero deletions against `c08528b`. All four rows appear as `+` lines only — the two
  you corrected show no deletion because they are new in this branch, exactly as stated. I
  verified the correction itself with a two-dot `8593f15..a3904ae`, which shows the `-`/`+`
  pairs the three-dot correctly hides.
- **Rows land inside the record's region.** Nearest `##` above line 545 is `## Delivery status`
  at line 61 — which is what makes the null control's movement meaningful rather than incidental.
- **Claim files byte-identical** to `origin/main` (md5 equal both files), and `env_drift.py
  --all` exits 0: `NO UNCLAIMED DRIFT` / `NO STALE FIXTURE`, 55 scenarios. Nothing to claim.
- **`VERSION`, manifest, notes heading untouched** — three-dot exits 0; all read `6.3.20`.
- **No conflict.** `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main a3904ae` exits **0**, driver
  installed, no `MERGE-CLAIM` marker on either stream. GitHub agrees: `CLEAN` / `MERGEABLE`.
  `origin/main` has not moved under the branch — the merge base **is** `c08528b`, today's head.
- **Structure ratchet PASSED.** 24 metrics by derivation (budget keys less `recorded_at`).
- **`policy_lint.mjs` `TOTAL: 0 error(s) across 36 policy file(s)`** and `brief_lint.mjs`
  `GUARD ok` both reproduce. The body contract passes on the live body at this head: `PR-BODY:
  0 error(s)`.
- **Your `#709` concurrency limit is real and I measured it**, which most stated limits here are
  not: `git merge-tree --write-tree a3904ae pr709` exits **1** with `CONFLICT (content):
  docs/plan-2026-09-open-issues.md`. Whichever merges second rebases, as you say.

## What I could not establish

- **`MODE: SCOPED, 21 scoped out`.** From a detached worktree `GATE_SCOPE=auto` printed
  **`MODE: FULL -- every test script runs, nothing is scoped out.`** — a detached HEAD has no
  branch to compare against, so `auto` falls back to full. I keyed on the mode line and it is
  not the one you report; I could not reproduce yours from the surface `fix-review.md` requires
  me to measure from, and I am reporting that rather than confirming your figure. CI is the
  authority here and CI is green: `closure-scope` success, `closures` skipped, both `fast` arms
  success, and zero non-green runs at head.
- That FULL run reported `>>> FAILED: python3 tests/golden.py`. I did **not** pass
  `GOLDEN_MODE=drift GOLDEN_REF=$(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)` per `gate-scoping.md`, and
  `env_drift.py --all` — the instrument designed for exactly this — exits 0 with no stale
  fixture. I read it as my invocation on a non-canonical BLAS, not as the branch, but I did not
  re-run it in drift mode and so am not asserting it.
- **"measured at their current heads"** on the #715 row — unsourced, as above.

## One thing about the contract itself, which you should know before the next round

Mid-review my parent worktree surfaced a copy of `tools/audit/briefs/fix-review.md` that
disagreed with the one in this branch. It is **stale, not newer**: that worktree sits on
`claude/governance-policy-handover-13fbd8` (`03af74b`), an ancestor of `origin/main` that
predates two commits to this file — `58aec5f` (#641, *the review contract told reviewers to
write a verdict its own parser rejects*) and `43d3e93` (#669, *the listing that shows one run
per check was the instrument the contract prescribed*).

Had I taken it as current I would have written an unparseable verdict, and — this is the part
that matters — read the checks with `get_check_runs`, the one-run-per-check instrument #669
removed. **That instrument shows `pr-contract` green at `8c96cf1` and hides `102825508528`
entirely.** The finding this review turns on is invisible under the older contract. Worth a
line on #201: a seat whose worktree predates #669 cannot find this class of red.

---

Reviewed at `a3904ae`; head unchanged and `updated_at` still 09:53:59Z at posting. Detached
worktree, removed after posting. Unblock by naming `102825508528` in `## Red checks` — your
existing mechanism paragraph already answers it — and I would take #715's stated-rule form
over any run list.

Fix review: merge c99559c2f09a820a8090b2858702d26ad3425d1d

Round three, from a detached worktree at `c99559c`. Zero API failures (three `gh` calls returned the escape-sequence guard, not an API error; re-run with `--allow-escape-sequences`).

## Q1 — the rule-shaped `## Red checks`: legitimate, and I checked it with a stronger discriminator than it names

**Legitimate.** It names `pr-contract`, fires `defect-root-cause.md`'s trigger, and answers with the recorded finding that no cheaper detector is owed. The rule allows that answer, and the reason here is a good one: the red is produced *by* compliance with S10's ordering, so a detector against it would be a detector against the rule. It also names what actually removes it — making body-set and push one operation, `tools/audit/push.sh` on #715 — which is "the fix is a different pull request, in review", not "nothing can be done".

**Not unfalsifiable.** It names a decidable falsifier — a `failure` at the head in `## Head` — which could have come out the other way and which I executed: **23 runs at `c99559c`, 0 failures**. The regress it identifies is real, not rhetorical: round two's enumeration was falsified by the edit that wrote it, and check-run `102825508528`'s own job log contains the sentence denying it. Replacing a self-falsifying list with a rule plus a re-derivation command is the correct repair.

**Where it is weaker than it needed to be — and this is my substantive criticism.** "A failure at the head under review" discriminates only at the *final* head. A genuine push-order violation on an intermediate commit — push first, set the body after — fires `pr-contract` at that commit with a body naming a *predecessor*, leaving a red; once the next commit is pushed, that red is no longer "at the head" and the rule reclassifies it as the prescribed order working. **So yes, a real violation can hide behind this rule on any commit later superseded.** The rule classifies non-head reds as benign *by position*, and position does not carry the information.

**The information is available, so I used it rather than taking the classification.** The two events have opposite signatures:
- prescribed order → the body's `## Head` names the **successor** commit;
- push-first violation → it names a **predecessor**.

Extracted from each red's job log:

| red run | at | body's `## Head` | relation | errors |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `102819935449` | `8593f15` | `8c96cf1` | successor | `PR-BODY: 1 error(s)` — head mismatch |
| `102825508528` | `8c96cf1` | `a3904ae` | successor | `PR-BODY: 1 error(s)` — head mismatch |
| `102835394791` | `a3904ae` | `c99559c` | successor | `PR-BODY: 1 error(s)` — head mismatch |

Every red is exactly one error and it is the head mismatch — nothing laundered behind the classification — and `pr-contract` is the only check that went red anywhere in the branch. **The fixer's scoping is honest for this branch**, because the stronger property holds too. As a general form the section under-specifies: the successor/predecessor test works at every commit and does not slide as the head moves. That is a strengthening worth carrying into `fix-review.md`, **not a block here** — step 11 has me checking that the trigger was answered, not adjudicating the answer.

## Q2 — head and every red on every commit

Paginated, `filter=all`. `8593f15` 1 failure, `8c96cf1` 1, `a3904ae` 1, **`c99559c` 0 of 23**. The rule's own discriminating observation has not fired.

## Q4 — both simulation arms, re-run independently

Isolated `git clone --local` (78 MB, hardlinked); `refs/remotes/origin/main` repointed only inside the clone; tree **checked out**, not merely referenced; `git commit-tree` with parent `c08528b`.

```
TREATMENT  tree=c99559c  simulated-merge=130d1c0
  worktree self-row present: 1
  v6.3.20  RECORD: 4 merged pull request(s) ...; 0 without a disposition | TOTAL: 0 error(s) over 4 merged pull request(s)
  v6.3.19  RECORD: 29 merged pull request(s) ...; 0 without a disposition | TOTAL: 0 error(s) over 29 merged pull request(s)

NULL       tree=8593f15  simulated-merge=11c91ae
  worktree self-row present: 0
  v6.3.20  RECORD: 4 merged pull request(s) ...; 1 without a disposition | TOTAL: 1 error(s) over 4 merged pull request(s)
  v6.3.19  RECORD: 29 merged pull request(s) ...; 1 without a disposition | TOTAL: 1 error(s) over 29 merged pull request(s)
  ERROR [record] docs/plan-2026-09-open-issues.md: no disposition in the plan of record or the living
  handover for merged pull request #718
```

4/0, 29/0 and 4/1, 29/1 — the body's figures reproduce exactly, and the control moves under both windows.

## Q3 — the corrections, each against its source

- **Friction, one case not four.** Verified against the rows themselves. #708's row: "Twice this evening a pull request merged before its disposition existed — #693 and #695", and it carries the "one serialising writer" protocol change — not a freeze. #711: "leftover #692 still said in review after #710 landed"; #717: "leftover #684 still said in review after #716 landed" — both describe branches that had **already merged**, so no frozen head could have forced them. Only #718 is forced by `fixer.md`'s handoff freeze. **"The fourth record branch today" derived, not carried:** `record:` merges on `main` today are #708, #711, #717 — three — plus this one.
- **Record window.** `governance.yml:223` is `SINCE=$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0 --match 'v*')`, used as `$SINCE..origin/main` at line 233, and it is the only step that may fail the job. Resolves here to **`v6.3.20`**. Raw counts against `origin/main`: 3 and 28 squash subjects, plus the simulated merge = **4 and 29**. The gate's window is the 4; the 29 is correctly labelled conservative rather than authoritative.
- **The #715 row, both halves.** (a) #201: "Measured properly it is 13 pull requests over two days by one unit, 9 failing check-runs today by another, and the two counts corroborate." (b) #678's own cost test: "**9** had a `failure` run at the merged head before a body edit greened it: #643, #648, #655, #656, #657, #661, #663, #665, #667." Both halves sourced; the different-unit framing is #201's own. The dropped clause "measured at their current heads" was also wrong in substance — #678 measured **merged** heads.
- **Unasked, #718's own row.** `a3904ae..c99559c` replaces "The fourth record branch today for that reason" with "the fourth record branch today, and the first of the four a frozen head forced", plus the #708/#711/#717 exclusions. Correct, and it repairs a real over-attribution.

## Q5 — surfaces

Three-dot against merge-base `c08528b`: **one file, four insertions, zero deletions** (`docs/plan-2026-09-open-issues.md`). Claim files byte-identical to `main` (both). `VERSION`, manifest, `RELEASE_NOTES.md` heading: 0 changed. `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` exit **0**. `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`. `origin/main` is `c08528b` — unmoved, and it *is* the merge base. Live head at posting time is `c99559c` — matches what I measured.

Scoped gate: **`MODE: SCOPED -- 0 script(s) run, 21 scoped out`**, `2 TEST SCRIPT(S) PASSED`, exit 0. Keyed on the mode line.

**A trap worth recording for the next reviewer.** My first run of the gate printed `MODE: FULL` and started `tests/stress.py`. The cause was **my own untracked review marker** — `closure.py select` reads untracked files, and reported `reason: no recorded closure mentions .review-marker-718-r3 -- an unmeasured file is not a safe skip`. A reviewer instructed to leave a marker in the worktree and then to key on the `MODE:` line will measure a different mode than CI, in the FULL direction. I re-derived with the marker moved aside and restored it after. Not a defect in this pull request; a defect in the review procedure.

## Nothing I could not establish

Every figure in the body was re-derived under its own stated rule. `## Forward-carry` is `none` and correctly so — the rows are the propagation instrument for their own pull requests. #714's `Fix review: merge 45a16d310ebe6c2745a4cd84880c47471d70765a` sits at its live head `45a16d3`, so the freeze rationale and the queue-gating claim both hold.

nodes.title: process: collect leftover detached worktrees
nodes.body:
`tools/audit/worktree_gc.sh` collects leftover detached worktrees. Dry-run by default; `--apply` deletes only when the four predicates in #684 all hold. A branch worktree is never touched. `Closes #684`. leaves #201 open.

## Head

`b6d95af2e141d2e3c86e7942c71d9f7989d735c5`

## Mutation proof

`tools/audit/worktree_gc.sh --self-test` includes an arm that clears the injected open-head list. The detached, clean, old worktree whose HEAD had been an open pull-request head flips from `keep … 3` to `delete`. Dropping the criterion-3 check produces the same flip. The other keep criteria have the same shape: a dirty or untracked detached worktree is `keep … 2`; a branch worktree stays `keep … 1` even when dirty and old.

## Null control

The same `--self-test` builds a detached, clean worktree whose HEAD is in the injected open-head list and asserts it is listed as kept with criterion 3 both before and after `--apply`. That is the acceptance the issue named. A dry-run against this clone printed the same verdict on detached worktrees whose HEAD is an open pull request; the command is the instrument and the live count is not carried.

## Figures

`tools/audit/worktree_gc.sh --self-test` — keep/delete verdicts and the null-control arm. A count of this machine's live worktrees is not restated; it moves.
