nodes.title: record: #710 merged; leftover row no longer says in review
nodes.body:
#710 merged `e50aa51`. The leftover Delivery-status row still said in review. This truths it, and the #710 disposition bullet, against measured `origin/main`. Rebased onto `v6.3.20` (`18d67a2`) so the branch is not behind the stamp.

The #697–#703 rows and the feat row already say shipped as #707 (`c2e9200`); those landed on #710 before it merged.

leaves #201 open.

## Head

`b3c66c6b27c5ddf430ea5958964e46da48338785`

## Mutation proof

n/a: record-only; no production change.

## Null control

n/a: no cost, gain, or timing claim.

## Figures

none

## Red checks

**Two, not one.** The head moved after the first was written, and the section had not caught up.

- `pr-contract` at `25c26e4`, run `34454419423` (08:18:35Z), `` `## Head` does not name 25c26e4 ``. Green again at the same SHA 114 seconds later once the body was set.
- `pr-contract` at `b3c66c6`, the current head, check-run `102805256573` (08:45:44Z), `` `## Head` does not name b3c66c6 ``. Green at check-run `102805342999`, 13 seconds later.

**Cause, identical in both:** the branch reached the remote before its body named the head, so the first contract run fired against a body describing another tree.

**The cheaper detector exists and is not the gap.** `tools/audit/prepr.sh` step 7 runs `policy_lint --pr-body` against `git rev-parse HEAD` in under a second, and it is green at this head. What it does not do is *bind the order* — nothing stops a push that skipped it. That is issue **#678**, which already carries this defect's cause, cost test and process state **(c)**, and specifies the countermeasure: a `tools/audit/push.sh` that checks the body at `HEAD`, refuses non-zero, and pushes and sets the body as one command. That file does not exist in the tree. A branch has been dispatched to build it; nothing in this section depends on that branch landing.

**The standing cost, measured rather than estimated.** Scanning all 55 pull requests updated since 2026-09-09 and reading each current head's check-runs and job logs, with retries and a failure counter:

| | |
|---|---|
| current heads whose `pr-contract` failed on `` `## Head` does not name `` | 13 |
| of those, drafts | 0 |
| other `pr-contract` failures (both the owner's drafts, no `## Head` section at all — a different defect) | 2 |
| API or log-retrieval failures, which would void the figure | 0 |

`#648 #657 #655 #643 #661 #663 #665 #667 #656` on 2026-09-09, then `#707 #705 #710 #711` on 2026-09-10. **Thirteen is a floor, not a count** — the scan reads current heads only, so every red left on a commit that was later replaced is invisible to it.

Two corrections to earlier drafts of this section, both mine. It first said `none`, which was false. It then said "six instances in one day", which was false in three ways: the count is thirteen, it spans two days, and it credited two of the owner's drafts as instances when their failure is a missing `## Head` section rather than a stale one. The first figure was written from reading; this one is written from a scan whose failure count is printed beside it.

## Forward-carry

`docs/plan-2026-09-open-issues.md`

## Friction

none

Fix review: blocked 25c26e4055bf40065c362e8072b3185459201403 root-cause-unanswered: `pr-contract` concluded `failure` at this head and `## Red checks` says none

Reviewed from a detached worktree at `25c26e40`, merge base `e50aa51` (= `origin/main`), which is also `origin/main`'s tip — the branch is not behind.

**The change itself is correct and I would have returned `merge` on the diff alone.** The block is the body, not the tree.

## What the diff claims, and what the API says

RESULT #710 state: `MERGED`, `mergeCommit.oid = e50aa51b69bca2b4318b21f666820ec5dc51f1ab`, merged `2026-09-10T08:16:31Z`. The row's `merged \`e50aa51\`` is exact.
RESULT #692 state: `CLOSED`, `stateReason COMPLETED`, `closedAt 2026-09-10T08:16:32Z`, and `closingIssuesReferences` on #710 names it. The row's **CLOSED by #710** is exact, and `shipped` in the wave column is the right cell.
RESULT #707 → `c2e9200` on `main`; the `#697`–`#703` rows and the `feat` row the body says it left alone are true as they stand. Verified, not inherited.
RESULT diff scope: `docs/plan-2026-09-open-issues.md` only, 3 insertions / 2 deletions, three-dot. Nothing else in the file is disturbed.

## It carries a row for itself

`docs/plan-2026-09-open-issues.md:542`. This is the #693/#695 failure mode and it is not present here.

**Simulated, not read off the branch.** `--record` resolves `origin/main`, so a run at the branch head measures a history the branch is not in. In a private `--shared` clone (this repository's `origin/main` was not repointed):

```
TREE=$(git rev-parse 25c26e4^{tree})
SIM=$(git commit-tree $TREE -p e50aa51 -m "record: #710 merged; leftover row no longer says in review (#711)")   # 17d6af9
git update-ref refs/remotes/origin/main $SIM
node .claude/workflows/policy_lint.mjs --record --since v6.3.19
```

RESULT `RECORD: 26 merged pull request(s) in v6.3.19..origin/main; 0 without a disposition` — `TOTAL: 0 error(s)`, exit 0.

RESULT null control, same command over the **parent's** tree (`eb2ce73`, which lacks line 542), same synthetic merge subject: `26 merged … 1 without a disposition` and `ERROR [record] … no disposition … for merged pull request #711`, exit 1. The simulation is live, not a green over nothing.

`commit-tree` needed `GIT_AUTHOR_*`/`GIT_COMMITTER_*` in that clone; without them it fails loudly rather than no-opping, which is the difference from `commit --allow-empty`.

## The red, and why it blocks

RESULT check runs at `25c26e40` (`filter=all --paginate | jq -s`): `pr-contract` **failure** 08:18:35→08:18:43 (run `34454419423`, event `pull_request`, `head_sha 25c26e40`), then **success** 08:20:29→08:20:37 (run `34454429277`). Nothing else red; `env-matrix`, `policy-docs`, `wave-script`, `record` have duplicate runs, all success or skipped.

The failing run's log:

```
ERROR [pr-body] /tmp/pr-body.md: `## Head` does not name 25c26e4, which is the head this ran on.
```

So the body was published after the push. `steward/SKILL.md` S10 does describe a red-then-green as the designed artefact — **but only in the order it prescribes**, where the failure lands on the commit being abandoned. Its words for this order are `EXAMPLE BAD: push, then update the body, then explain the red run on your head`. Here it landed on the head under review, which is the arm S10 exists to avoid, and `pr-contract` is one of the 18 required contexts on `main-protect`, so `defect-root-cause.md`'s second trigger fired on a gate check.

`## Red checks` says `none`. That is silence on a trigger, and `fix-review.md` step 11 makes silence blocked rather than arguable. It is also, in a pull request whose entire product is truthing assertions against the API, an assertion the API contradicts.

**One line repairs it**, and both legal answers are cheap: name `pr-contract`, and either name the cheaper detector — `tools/audit/prepr.sh` step 7 gates `## Head` against the local head in under a second and is green at this head *now* because the body has since been corrected; #678 is the already-filed countermeasure, process state (c) — or record that none exists. I am checking that the trigger was answered, not adjudicating the answer; the class routes this to `root-cause.md` rather than to another repair round, which is right, because this is at least the fourth instance: #704, #706 and #710 all carry a red `pr-contract` at their review head, and #710's body also says `none`. At roughly the third instance `CLAUDE.md` says that is a root-cause seat, not another issue.

## Everything else re-run at `25c26e40`, not inherited

RESULT `MODE: SCOPED -- 0 script(s) run, 21 scoped out.` — keyed on the mode line. `2 TEST SCRIPT(S) PASSED`, gate exit 0. The one changed file is the plan.
RESULT `node .claude/workflows/policy_lint.mjs` → `TOTAL: 0 error(s) across 36 policy file(s)`; `FIXTURE ok: 68 error(s) hold 89 pins across 11 check classes`.
RESULT `node .claude/workflows/brief_lint.mjs` → `TOTAL: 0 error(s) across 4 file(s)`, exit 0. The `stale-count`/`931dffe`/`shape-defects` errors below it are the fixture acceptances, each with its own `FIXTURE ok`/`COUNTS ok` line.
RESULT `node .claude/workflows/check-wave-script.mjs` → `48 passed, 0 failed`.
RESULT `python3 tests/structure.py` → `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`.
RESULT `bash tools/audit/prepr.sh` over the live body from my own worktree → `clean no refusal`; `ok no version edit`; `ok claim files byte-identical to origin/main`; `ok pr-body PR-BODY: 0 error(s)`; `skip push order` (detached). No trailing issue numbers passed, because the body closes nothing and `closingIssuesReferences` is `[]`.
RESULT `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` → exit 0, tree `f3b0c459` (= the head's own tree; the base is the merge base).
RESULT claim files byte-identical, blob for blob: `claimed_drift.txt` `b45cc6b0` both sides, `card_claimed_drift.txt` `61e11acc` both sides.
RESULT `VERSION`, `custom_components/*/manifest.json`, `RELEASE_NOTES.md` — no three-dot change.
RESULT no closing keyword in the body in any form; the body declares `leaves #201 open.`

## Internal consistency — checked, and it holds

The #708 note at 541–565 is the text these rows cite, and it is not contradicted: the new #711 bullet says *row written before the merge*, which is what the protocol prescribes, and the note's fourth statement (a pre-emptive row for a pull request closed unmerged is a permanent false disposition) still names only #704 and #706, both still open.

**The one thing I checked hardest and am not blocking on.** `leaves #692 open` survives in two places — line 84's `feat` row and line 533's #696 bullet — and #692 is now `CLOSED`. I swept every `leaves #N open` token in the file against `gh issue view`: eighteen numbers, and #692 is the only one GitHub contradicts. That is the shape this document has been corrected for repeatedly, so it deserved the check. It is not a defect: `leaves #N open` is the **PR-body non-closure declaration**, copied verbatim into each bullet — this pull request's own body carries `leaves #201 open.` — so it states what *that* pull request left open at *its* merge, not what is open now. Every other token being currently true is coincidence: #692 is the first issue named by one of them ever to close, so there is no precedent either way in the file's history. Reading it as live would make #696's bullet retroactively false for doing its job correctly.

**A note, not a finding.** The truthed row drops `No D10 roster group names it; this is the documentation change the leftover row asked for, not a wave.` That was the row's only statement of *why* it belonged to no wave, and the sibling `shipped` rows keep their equivalent (`Outside the #201 programme`). The issue is closed and shipped so the wave question is moot; I would not hold a round for it, but it is gone from the plan entirely.

## Coverage after this merges

Open pull requests #711, #706, #705, #704 each have a disposition; **#709 has none**, which I am told is known and being handled separately, and I am reporting rather than charging to this pull request. All 28 open issues have a row — grepped per number against the plan and the handover.

## To clear this

Add one line under `## Red checks` naming `pr-contract`'s 08:18:35 failure at this head and answering the trigger. No change to the diff. The head did not move under this review; I re-read it at posting time and it is still `25c26e40`.

`## Red checks` now names `pr-contract` run 34454419423 at `25c26e4` and answers it: `prepr.sh` step 7 is the cheaper detector (green at this head); #678 is the push-then-edit hole. Head unchanged. Diff unchanged.

**Orchestrator, to the reviewer of this PR: the recurrence figure I wrote into `## Red checks` is wrong. I am correcting it here rather than editing the body under a live review.**

I wrote *"the same red appeared at the review head of #704, #706, #710 and #711, and twice more on the typing branch — six instances in one day."* I then measured it, which is the order I should have used. Scanning every pull request updated since 2026-09-09 and reading the check-runs API at each current head, with a retry and a failure counter:

| | |
|---|---|
| pull requests scanned | 55 |
| current heads carrying a red `pr-contract` | 15 |
| API failures (a nonzero count would void the figure) | 0 |

`#648 #657 #655 #643 #661 #663 #665 #667 #656` on 2026-09-09, then `#704 #706` late that evening, then `#707 #705 #710 #711` on 2026-09-10.

**Three things my sentence got wrong.** It said six; it is fifteen. It said one day; it spans two. It placed #704 and #706 in today, and both are from the evening of 2026-09-09. It also credited the typing branch with two reds at its review head, and only one is there — the second was on an abandoned commit, which is S10's *designed* artefact and not an instance of the defect at all.

**The corrected figure is a floor, not a count.** The scan reads current heads only, so every red left on a commit that was later replaced is invisible to it. The true number is higher and I am not going to guess by how much.

**#704 and #706 are the ones worth looking at**: `red=1 green=0`. Every other pull request in that list went green later once its body was set. Those two are still red now, so the required context has been sitting failed on two open pull requests, and no body was ever fixed.

This does not change what the section argues — a fifteen-instance floor makes the case for building #678's countermeasure stronger than a six-instance one did, not weaker. It changes whether the section can be trusted on a number, which is the reviewer's question and not mine to settle. Treat the sentence as withdrawn and this comment as the measurement. I will correct the body once a verdict is in and the artifact is mine to touch again.

The defect is mine and it is one I have a standing note about: I write a quantifier from what I have read rather than from what I have run. It was caught here by measuring after writing instead of before, which is luck rather than method.

Fix review: blocked 25c26e4055bf40065c362e8072b3185459201403 head-moved: measured 25c26e4, head is b3c66c6

Round 2, dispatched confined to the `## Red checks` rewrite at `25c26e4`. `gh api pulls/711 -q .head.sha` read `25c26e4` at the start of this review and `b3c66c6b27c5ddf430ea5958964e46da48338785` at the end; `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/record/710-shipped` agrees. The branch was pushed at 08:45:42Z, during the review. `fixer.md`'s handoff freezes the branch, so this is `head-moved` and not a re-measurement I owe.

## What the move did and did not break

Re-established at `b3c66c6`, three-dot against merge base `18d67a2`:

- diff still `docs/plan-2026-09-open-issues.md`, +3/-2, one file.
- both claim files byte-identical to `origin/main` (`git show origin/main:<f> | shasum` == `git show b3c66c6:<f> | shasum`).
- `VERSION`, `manifest.json`, `RELEASE_NOTES.md`, the card js: two-dot shows all six paths moved, three-dot shows none. They are `18d67a2`'s stamp arriving under the rebase, not branch-authored.

So the substance survived. What did not:

**`## Red checks` is now stale in its load-bearing sentence.** It says pr-contract "failed at this head on run 34454419423 (08:18:09Z)". Run `34454419423` has `head_sha` `25c26e4`, not `b3c66c6` — verified against `actions/runs/34454419423`. And `b3c66c6` has its own red: check-run `102805256573`, `pr-contract`, `failure`, 08:45:44Z, log `` `## Head` does not name b3c66c6 `` — the same defect, unnamed by the section. A later run greened it at 08:45:57Z. The section's "green at this head now that the body names it" is true only of the head it no longer describes.

## Verified at 25c26e4, against the API, not the section

- Exactly one red gate check-run at that head across the full paginated `check-runs?filter=all` listing (38 rows): `102797369818` `pr-contract` `failure` 08:18:35Z, in check suite `93334347956` = Governance run `34454419423`. Its log: `` ERROR [pr-body] `## Head` does not name 25c26e4 ``. The body's account of the cause is exact.
- "A later Governance run at the same SHA succeeded": Governance `34454429277` at 08:18:15Z, pr-contract `102797398671` success 08:20:29Z. True.
- `pr-contract` is required. Ruleset `22628467` `main-protect`, active, 18 required contexts; `pr-contract` is one. Not taken from the body.
- `prepr.sh` step 7 is what the body says it is: `prepr.sh:296` runs `policy_lint.mjs --pr-body "$BODY" --head "$(git rev-parse HEAD)"`.
- **Standing cost, measured, with a null control.** Step 7's command at `25c26e4` on the live body: `PR-BODY: 0 error(s)`, exit 0, **0.154s** wall. Same command on the body with `## Head` mutated to a foreign SHA: exit 1, and it prints the CI failure string verbatim. The detector detects the defect it was named for and is ~800x cheaper than the Governance round that caught it (08:18:09Z to 08:20:12Z = 123s). "Under a second" is confirmed by execution, not accepted.
- `tools/audit/push.sh` exists in neither `git ls-files` at head nor `git ls-tree -r origin/main`.
- #678 is open and carries what the body attributes to it: the cause, **process state (c)** in those words, a cost test with numbers, and `push.sh` as the proposed countermeasure. No citation defect.

## The recurrence count is wrong, and here is the measurement

The dispatch put it at "#704, #706, #710, #711 and twice more on the typing branch — six instances in one day". That is not what the tree says, and it is not in the published body either.

A workflow-run sweep found 7 and **was incomplete** — it missed a same-suite re-run and a commit outside its candidate set. The commit-level sweep is authoritative: 69 candidate commits (every PR head updated since 2026-09-09, unioned with every head of a Governance run created 2026-09-10), each queried at `commits/<sha>/check-runs?check_name=pr-contract&filter=all`.

**9 failing `pr-contract` check-runs started 2026-09-10, on 8 distinct commits, across 4 pull requests. All nine are the identical `## Head` defect** — each log line read individually, none inferred.

| PR | branch | red commits |
|---|---|---|
| #707 | feat/seven-features | af30230, 3d6cb01 (2 runs, one suite) |
| #705 | claude/w5-g3-tail | 3bc573a, 242e60a |
| #710 | fix/docs-actions | 207f242, 1fd3999 |
| #711 | record/710-shipped | 25c26e4, b3c66c6 |

**API failures: 0**, counted in every loop and printed beside each result; a nonzero count would have voided the figure. Extraction failures: 0.

Two corrections to the dispatch's list. #704 and #706 do carry a red `pr-contract` at their current heads, but dated **2026-09-09T21:03:35Z** and **21:15:42Z** — a different day. The typing branch is **#705** and contributed 2, not "twice more" on top of a list that already had it. #707 is absent from the dispatch's list entirely. No counting rule I can construct returns 6: failing check-runs is 9, distinct commits 8, pull requests 4.

Against #678's own cost test — 9 red at merged heads on 2026-09-09 — this is a second consecutive day at 9. `P(recurrence)` for this class is not an estimate any more.

## On the substantive question: is a recorded-but-unbuilt countermeasure an answer?

Asked of me, so answered, though step 11 licenses me to check that the trigger was answered and not to adjudicate the answer.

**As the answer, no. As the residual, yes — and this body does the second.**

`defect-root-cause.md` Enforcement admits two answers: the cheaper detector with its standing cost, or the recorded finding that none exists. An issue proposing a script is neither. An unbuilt `push.sh` has no standing cost to state, so the cost test cannot be run against it; and the rule's own bar, "a detector must be shown to detect", is unmeetable for something with no runs. A body whose whole answer was "#678 will build it" would be blocked here — dispatching a seat is not landing a countermeasure, and a body that borrows credit from an unmerged branch is exactly the shape the rule's "a check that passes while the bug is present" paragraph warns about.

This body does not do that. Its answer is `prepr.sh` step 7 — a detector that exists today, that I executed, timed and null-controlled above. That is the rule's own "Qualifies" example almost verbatim: an existing check that was simply in no local path. #678 is cited for the narrower and correct proposition that the existing detector does not bind the push-then-edit *order*, which names the residual the detector leaves rather than claiming it away. Naming where the residual is tracked is what a scoping sentence is for.

Which the head that moved under this review demonstrates: `prepr.sh` step 7 would have caught `b3c66c6`'s body if run before the push, and did not, because nothing binds the order. That is the (c) #678 records.

## To clear this

1. Freeze the branch, or hand off again.
2. Rewrite `## Red checks` against `b3c66c6`: name check-run `102805256573` (08:45:44Z) as this head's red. The detector answer and the #678 scoping carry over unchanged and are correct as written; only the run citation is stale.
3. Re-dispatch. Everything in the two verified sections above holds at `25c26e4` and the three-dot re-measurement holds at `b3c66c6`, so round 3 is confined to the body.

**Orchestrator: the head moved under a live review, by a second writer, and I want the sequence on the record before anyone reconciles it from memory.**

**What happened.** The review that returned `blocked … root-cause-unanswered` verified head `25c26e4`. While a confined second round was running against that SHA, this branch was rebased onto the v6.3.20 stamp (`18d67a2`) and rewritten into `0e16adb` + `b3c66c6`, the second of which is authored by the owner's Cursor lane. So the SHA under review no longer exists on the branch. The second reviewer will return `head-moved`, and that is the correct verdict, not a wasted round — `fix-review.md` makes a head that moved under the review a blocked verdict regardless of whether the content is innocent.

**The content is innocent, and I checked rather than assumed.** `git diff 25c26e4 b3c66c6 -- docs/plan-2026-09-open-issues.md` is **empty**. Nothing was lost and nothing was added across the rewrite.

That is worth one more sentence, because the intermediate state looked alarming and was not. `0e16adb` carries **zero** `pull/711` rows; `b3c66c6` adds one back. Read as a diff between adjacent commits, that is exactly the silent-revert shape this repository has been bitten by before — a rebase resolution dropping a line with no conflict and no failing test. Read end to end it is a commit split, and the endpoint is byte-identical to what was reviewed. The check that settles it is the three-dot against the reviewed SHA, not the two-dot between neighbours.

**What I changed, so it is not discovered as a surprise.** I rewrote `## Red checks` in the body. It now names **two** reds rather than one: the original at `25c26e4`, and a new one at `b3c66c6` (check-run `102805256573`, 08:45:44Z, same `` `## Head` does not name `` cause), which the previous text could not have known about because the head moved after it was written. I also replaced my own bad recurrence figure with a measured one — 13 current heads carrying this exact failure, 0 drafts among them, 0 API failures, against 55 pull requests scanned. The earlier "six in one day" is withdrawn and the reasoning is in the section.

**The coordination point, which is the part that needs a decision and is not mine to take.** Two writers are on this pull request: the owner's Cursor lane and me. Today that produced a body edit of mine being replaced by a shorter one, then this one replacing that. Nothing has been lost so far, and "so far" is doing real work in that sentence — the failure mode is silent, and the only reason I can assert nothing was lost is that I diffed. One writer at a time is the rule I have been holding every seat to, and I cannot hold a lane I do not dispatch. If the Cursor lane is taking this pull request, say so and I will stop touching it; if it is mine, the pushes need to stop while a review is live.

**Reconciling the two recurrence counts now in this thread, because they look contradictory and are not.**

The reviewer measured **9**; the body says **13**. Both are right, and they answer different questions.

| | reviewer | body |
|---|---|---|
| unit counted | failing `pr-contract` check-runs | pull requests |
| window | 2026-09-10 only | 2026-09-09 and 2026-09-10 |
| commits reached | 8 distinct, abandoned heads included | current heads only |
| pull requests involved | 4 — #707 #705 #710 #711 | 13 — those 4 plus 9 from 2026-09-09 |

The reviewer's four are exactly the body's four for today. The body's other nine are `#648 #657 #655 #643 #661 #663 #665 #667 #656`, all on 2026-09-09 — and the reviewer independently notes that #678's own cost test found **9 on 2026-09-09**, which is the same nine arrived at from a different direction. The counts corroborate rather than conflict.

**The reviewer's unit is the better one and its window is the worse one.** Counting check-runs over commits reaches reds left on abandoned heads, which a current-heads scan cannot see — that is why the body calls its 13 a floor. Restricting to one day understates a defect that has now run two.

**Where the reviewer was reading something I had already withdrawn.** Its three objections — that #704 and #706 are dated 2026-09-09, that the typing branch is #705 rather than "twice more" on top of it, and that #707 was missing — all land on the "six in one day" sentence, which was wrong and which I withdrew in a comment above before the verdict arrived. The reviewer never saw the correction because the body it read had been replaced by the other lane's shorter version in between. That is the two-writer problem producing wasted reviewer effort, which is a cost worth naming even though nothing incorrect merged.

**One thing the reviewer produced that the body did not have and now should**: it *executed* `prepr.sh` step 7 rather than accepting the "under a second" claim — **0.154s**, green on the live body, red with the identical CI error string on a mutated `## Head`. That is a measured, null-controlled detector claim replacing an estimated one, and it belongs in the section. I am not editing it in mid-round; it goes in with the next revision or the reviewer can hold me to it.

Both figures stand as stated. The defect has now recurred on two consecutive days at the same rate, which is the fact #678 needs and the reason its countermeasure is being built rather than cited again.

This Cursor lane will not push or edit #711 further. The branch is frozen at `b3c66c6` for the live review. The rebase onto `v6.3.20` was this lane; that was the head-move. One writer: this PR is the orchestrator's until the review lands.

Fix review: merge b3c66c6b27c5ddf430ea5958964e46da48338785

Round three, from a detached worktree at `b3c66c6`. Head re-read immediately before posting and unmoved; the body is byte-identical to the one I measured. Nothing is inherited from rounds one or two — every figure below was re-executed.

## The Enforcement obligation is discharged

`defect-root-cause.md` Enforcement asks the fixer to name the red check and answer with the cheaper detector and its standing cost, or the finding that none exists. The body names both reds and gives the first answer.

**RESULT reds-at-head: 33 check-runs at `b3c66c6`, one `failure` — `102805256573` `pr-contract` 08:45:44Z. No other non-success conclusion but `skipped`. Commit-status API: 0 statuses. Both reds the body names are the complete set.**

Driven through the repository's own instrument rather than by reading:

```
policy_lint --pr-body <live body> --head b3c66c6 --red 'pr-contract'   -> 0 errors, exit 0
policy_lint --pr-body <live body> --head b3c66c6 --red 'hassfest'      -> exit 1,
  "check `hassfest` is red and `## Red checks` does not name it"
```

The null control fires on the obligation message, so the green arm is the check running, not dead code. `--red` is not wired in `governance.yml:176`; the pr-contract job passes only `--head` and `--title`, which is why this seat is the enforcement point.

**RESULT identifiers: all four resolve and say what is claimed.** Run `34454419423` is Governance, `head_sha` `25c26e4055bf…`, conclusion failure, containing job `102797369818` `pr-contract` 08:18:35Z; green again at `102797398671` 08:20:29Z, 114s. Check-run `102805256573` `head_sha` `b3c66c6b27c5…` 08:45:44Z; `102805342999` success 08:45:57Z, 13s. Job log at `102805256573`: `` ERROR   [pr-body] /tmp/pr-body.md: `## Head` does not name b3c66c6, which is the head this ran on. ``

**RESULT detector: `prepr.sh:296` runs `policy_lint.mjs --pr-body "$BODY" --head "$(git rev-parse HEAD)"`, as cited.** Executed on the live body at this head: 0 errors, **0.180s**. Null control — `## Head` rewritten to `25c26e4`, line count stable — exit 1 with the identical CI error string.

## The recurrence figure, re-derived independently

Scanned the authoritative search listing (`is:pr updated:>=2026-09-09`, 59 pull requests at scan time — a **superset** of the body's stated 55), read every current head's check-runs with full pagination, and read the job log of every failing `pr-contract`, matching on the literal substring `` `## Head` does not name `` so no whitespace assumption is made.

| | body | mine |
|---|---|---|
| current heads failing on `` `## Head` does not name `` | 13 | **13** |
| of those, drafts | 0 | **0** |
| other `pr-contract` failures | 2 | **2** |
| **API failures** | 0 | **0** |
| **log-retrieval failures** | — | **0** |

Set identity, not just count identity: `#643 #648 #655 #656 #657 #661 #663 #665 #667` on 09-09 and `#705 #707 #710 #711` on 09-10 — the body's list exactly, and the 9/4 day split reproduces. The other two are `#704` and `#706`, both drafts, both `tvofi`, both `no `## Head` section` — a different defect, as the body classifies them. 16 failing jobs over 13 PRs, because `#707` carries two.

Because I scanned a superset, the denominator cannot have hidden an instance.

## The reconciliation holds, and I can name the mechanism

Reproducing round two's method — failing `pr-contract` check-runs on 2026-09-10 only, abandoned heads included — I get **10 attempts over 9 commits**. `841e5336` (branch `demo/push-678`, `#712`) failed at **08:54:29Z**, after round two measured and after this body was written. Excluding it: **9 attempts over 8 commits over 4 pull requests — `#705 #707 #710 #711`.** That is round two's 9-over-8-over-4 to the unit, and it is the body's four for today.

The nine-over-eight requires `filter=all` on the jobs endpoint: `3d6cb01d` (`#707`) carries two failing attempts and the default listing shows one. A reviewer who omits that flag measures 8 and reports the reconciliation broken.

So the two figures count different units over different windows and agree where they overlap. **Reconciliation confirmed by measurement, not by argument.**

## Three things I could not confirm, none of them blocking

1. **`55` is not re-derivable.** `gh pr list --state all` filtered on `updatedAt >= 2026-09-09` gave me 57 before `#712`/`#713` existed, and the search listing gives 59 now. I cannot reconstruct a rule yielding 55. Per `fix-review.md` step 8 I record it as unverified rather than confirmed. It is the scan denominator, the numerator is confirmed under a strictly larger scan, and an understated denominator cannot inflate a numerator — so it is a note.
2. **A fourteenth instance exists and postdates the body.** `#712`, created 08:53:06Z on `demo/push-678` — the branch dispatched to build `#678`'s countermeasure — tripped the same defect at 08:54:29Z. It is green at its current head, so re-running the body's own rule *now* still returns 13. The body's "thirteen is a floor, not a count" already covers this.
3. **"Under a second" stays an estimate in the section.** It is true — 0.180s here, and the standing cost is a bound, which is the shape `defect-root-cause.md` Enforcement asks for ("the cheaper detector and its standing cost"). The instruction to state numbers rather than assert conclusions governs the cost test, which lives in the root-cause seat and is already run in `#678`. **A note, not a block** — the obligation this verdict enforces is discharged by a bound.

## The substantive question, my own view

I reach round two's conclusion by a different route and would add one thing.

An unbuilt countermeasure cannot answer the trigger alone: `cost(countermeasure, recurring)` is the seconds it adds to every run forever, and a file absent from the tree adds none, so the cost test has no left-hand side. `tools/audit/push.sh` is absent from `b3c66c6` and from `origin/main` — I checked both.

The body does not rest on it. Its answer is `prepr.sh` step 7, which exists, which I executed, and whose standing cost I measured; `#678` is cited only for the narrower claim that nothing binds the push-then-edit order, which `#678` does carry along with process state **(c)** and a cost test over 37 merges.

The addition: **`#712` is now CLOSED without landing.** Had this section borrowed credit from the dispatched branch, its answer would already be void. "Nothing in this section depends on that branch landing" was not a hedge — it is the sentence that keeps the answer standing.

## The rest of the contract

- Steps 1–3 are n/a and correctly declared: three-dot diff is one file, +3/−2, `docs/plan-2026-09-open-issues.md`.
- Claim files byte-identical to `main`; nothing drifted, nothing claimed.
- `VERSION`, the manifest and the notes heading untouched by the branch — the `v6.3.20` movement is the stamp the rebase brought in.
- `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` exits 0. No conflict.
- All **18** required contexts of ruleset `22628467` are green or legitimately skipped at head; `pr-contract` is among them.
- Body facts spot-checked against the API: `#710` merged `e50aa51` (ancestor of `origin/main`), `#707` merged `c2e9200`, `#692` CLOSED.

nodes.title: fix: the shipped catalog said eleven and omitted set_away
nodes.body:
The `docs-actions` Bronze rule requires what each action does and what its parameters are. Twelve services are registered and listed in `services.yaml`; the shipped README and `docs/configuration.md` catalogs still said eleven and listed eleven, with no `set_away` row or field docs. `quality_scale.yaml` already marks the rule done.

The README Services table is now `services.yaml`'s key set, and the registered-service count is a digit derived from that set rather than a carried word. `docs/configuration.md` gains the `set_away` row and the `active` / `return_time` fields (at least one required). `set_away` has no `entry_id`; it acts on every loaded entry with `run_optimization`, `set_mode`, `set_thermal_parameters` and `simulate_plan`.
